abstract: Hydrothermal ore systems commonly record repeated mineral growth, fluid infiltration, and isotopic re-equilibration, making it difficult to distinguish continuous ore formation from superimposed mineralising events. Petrochronology of fluid-sensitive accessory minerals can link mineral ages, textures, and trace-element signatures to resolve these overprinted histories. Here we integrate microtextural observations, in situ UPb geochronology, and trace-element geochemistry of allanite and apatite from the Mary Kathleen REE–U deposit, northwest Queensland, to test whether mineralisation reflects a single continuous event or multiple discrete fluid pulses. Allanite records four age populations between 1575 and 1487 Ma, indicating episodic REE–U mineralisation over ~90 Myr rather than continuous growth. Younger allanite domains are U-rich and generally more concordant, whereas older domains are U-poor and show stronger reverse discordance. Th/U and Eu/Eu* vary systematically with age, but we interpret these changes as recording evolving uranium mobility and fluid chemistry rather than a unique redox signal. Together with apatite UPb data, these results support repeated REE–U remobilisation during the Isan Orogeny and demonstrate the value of allanite–apatite petrochronology for reconstructing overprinted hydrothermal histories in complex metasomatic systems.

title: Distinct roles of sediment electron-accepting and electron-donating capacities in long-term oxidant consumption and contaminant degradation during in situ chemical oxidation
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Chenglong Yu, Lijun Fan, Hao Wang, Jianyuan Chen, Chuanzhiheng Luo, Shengyan Pu
abstract: The persistence and activation of oxidants in aquifers are critical for the performance of in situ chemical oxidation of contaminated groundwater but are largely constrained by aquifer chemical heterogeneity. However, the links between chemical heterogeneity of sediments and oxidant consumption and contaminant degradation remain unclear. Using a recently developed modified chemical probe method, we characterized the chemical heterogeneity of sediments from two contaminated aquifers by quantifying their electron-accepting capacity (EAC) and electron-donating capacity (EDC). We then investigated persulfate (S2O8 2−) consumption regulated by sediment EAC/EDC over 7–15 days. Results showed that S2O8 2− consumption correlates well with sediment EAC rather than EDC. Further analysis revealed that the initial fast kinetics were driven by oxidation of reactive EDC in expandable Fe-bearing phyllosilicates and the hidden cycling of EAC–EDC in Fe(III) oxides. In contrast, the subsequent slow kinetics were controlled by EAC–EDC cycling of structural Fe(III) associated with both Fe(III) oxides and expandable phyllosilicates. Although S2O8 2− consumption was governed by EAC, contaminant degradation was controlled by EDC. This is because reactions of S2O8 2− with EDC generate highly reactive oxidants (e.g., •OH and SO4•−), whereas reactions with EAC produce weak or negligible oxidants. Overall, these findings demonstrate the distinct roles of sediment EAC and EDC in oxidant consumption and activation, thereby providing quantitative insights for designing low-oxidant-consumption remediation strategies.

title: Aftermath of the Great Oxidation and Lomagundi–Jatuli Events: Geochemical and Isotopic Constraints on Earth's Early Habitability
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Abhisikta Goswami, Yirang Jang, Sanghoon Kwon, M. Santosh, Sarada Prasad Mohanty, Jiyoung Choi
abstract: In Earth's early history, the Lomagundi–Jatuli Event (LJE) represents a major carbon cycle perturbation associated with the later stages and aftermath of the Paleoproterozoic Great Oxidation Event (GOE), marked by enhanced marine carbon cycling and atmospheric oxygen accumulation. The Aravalli Supergroup (ca. 2.3–1.9 Ga) of Rajasthan, India, preserves an extensive sedimentary archive of these transitions. Previous studies documented carbon isotope perturbations, phosphogenesis, and redox evolution within these metasediments but lacked an integrated multi-proxy comparison of the geochemical and isotopic characteristics. The present study compares the geochemical and isotopic compositions of carbonaceous phyllites from two contrasting domains: the non-phosphoritic Umra sub-basin and the phosphorite-associated Udaipur domain. Integrated analyses of major and trace elements, chemical indices, redox-sensitive elements (Cr, Ni, U, Cu, V), REE + Y systematics, and stable isotopes (δ13Corg and δ15N) reveal variable depositional environments. The Umra sub-basin exhibits geochemical and isotopic variability, with fluctuating redox proxies, REE + Y anomalies, and carbon and nitrogen isotopic signatures indicating differences in depositional conditions and organic matter preservation. In contrast, the Udaipur domain records geochemical characteristics consistent with reducing conditions, including enrichment in redox-sensitive elements and depleted δ13Corg (V-PDB) values, following the LJE. These findings demonstrate environmental heterogeneity between the successions and support investigating relationships between phosphorite-associated sedimentation, nutrient cycling, and marine redox variability during the LJE and the GOE interval. The results contribute to understanding Paleoproterozoic carbon cycling and surface-environment evolution within the published geological framework, without independently establishing the relative depositional ages of the two successions.

title: Quartz as a recorder of the magmatic-hydrothermal transition in highly peraluminous rare-metal granites: evidence from the Beauvoir granite (French Massif Central)
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Océane Rocher, Christophe Ballouard, Antonin Richard, Lorenzo Tavazzani, Cyril Chelle-Michou, Patrick Carr, Alexandre Tarantola, Nicolas Esteves, Nordine Bouden, Julien Mercadier
abstract: Magma degassing is a ubiquitous process in granitic systems, particularly pronounced in highly peraluminous rare-metal granites (PRMGs), that influences crystallisation dynamics, metal transport, and ore deposition. In this study, we investigate the magmatic-hydrothermal transition in the Beauvoir leucogranite, a world-class PRMG and major lithium resource from the French Paleozoic Variscan belt, by integrating detailed petrographic observations of magmatic quartz and associated fluid inclusions with microthermometry and in situ analyses of quartz trace-element compositions and oxygen isotopes. The high H₂O contents of the Beauvoir melts (ca. 3.6–7.3 wt.%) favoured early H₂O saturation and magmatic volatile phase (MVP) exsolution during crystallisation, likely close to the liquidus. Early stages remained largely melt-dominated, with quartz cores recording increasing Li and Al contents across the granite units, consistent with progressive magmatic differentiation. In contrast, crystal rims exhibit a systematic depletion in Li and Al, reflecting increasing fluid influence on crystallisation dynamics, possibly combined with crystallisation of late-stage Li-bearing phases. In the apical and most evolved magmatic unit (B1), snowball-textured quartz overgrowths record catastrophic, high-intensity MVP exsolution events, likely triggered by rapid decompression and associated with strong undercooling and disequilibrium crystallisation. Cs fractionation modelling places these events at a late stage of evolution, corresponding to approximately 84–98% crystallisation. Snowball quartz is further characterised by a marked decrease in δ18O values from quartz cores to snowball rims of approximately 4.8–7.8‰, interpreted as the result of kinetic oxygen isotopic fractionation under disequilibrium conditions. Beyond its impact on quartz crystallisation, high-intensity MVP exsolution might have promoted the re-equilibration of pre-existing metal-bearing minerals, while strongly modifying the physicochemical conditions of the system, including its oxidation state, potentially enhancing the late-stage crystallisation of cassiterite (SnO₂) and columbite-group minerals.

title: Continental subduction transfers carbon and niobium‑tantalum to the deep mantle: Evidence from Nb Ta enriched orogenic peridotites
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Chun-Peng Xia, Ren-Xu Chen, Yong-Fei Zheng, Zhuang-Zhuang Yin, Guo-Chao Sun, Bing Gong, Xiang-Ping Zha
abstract: Continental subduction can deliver carbonate-bearing crustal material into the deep mantle to generate carbonate melts, but their migration, storage, and role in mass transfer within continental subduction zones remain poorly understood. We present an integrated petrological and geochemical investigation of orogenic peridotites from the Dabie–Sulu orogenic belt, combining whole-rock and mineral compositions, clinopyroxene Sr isotopes, rutile UPb ages, and comprehensive zircon analyses (cathodoluminescence imaging, UPb dating, trace elements, HfO isotopes and inclusion analyses). The garnet peridotites represent residues of the subcontinental lithospheric mantle (SCLM) that experienced variable degrees of metasomatism. Carbonate minerals, diagnostic clinopyroxene geochemical signatures (high Ca/Al, (La/Yb)N ratios and low Ti/Eu ratios) and P-T constraints provide multiple lines of evidence for carbonated silicate melt metasomatism. Elevated 87Sr/86Sr ratios in clinopyroxene and carbonate (0.7081–0.7106), together with high δ18O values (up to 14.1‰) and enriched Hf isotopic compositions in magnesite-bearing Triassic zircon domains, indicate that the metasomatic melt was derived from the deeply subducted South China Block. Most studied garnet peridotites have higher Nb and Ta contents than those of the Depleted Mantle. All have contents exceeding those of the modeled residue after 20% batch melting, and several samples show suprachondritic Nb/Ta ratios. This confirms that the metasomatized SCLM can act as a local high-Nb/Ta reservoir. Whole-rock and mineral compositions reveal that Ti-clinohumite is the dominant host of Nb and Ta. Ti-clinohumite inclusions in Triassic zircon domains and Triassic rutile UPb ages suggest that NbTa enrichment resulted from the same carbonate metasomatic event. Collectively, our results suggest that the continental subduction triggers carbonate metasomatism that transfers both carbon and high field strength elements from the subducting slab into the overlying SCLM, enriching it in volatiles and locally elevating its Nb/Ta ratios. These metasomatic domains may later be tapped by post-collisional magmatism, contributing to a protracted recycling pathway that operates on timescales longer than those in oceanic subduction zones.

title: Experimental diagenetic transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in sulfate and/or phosphate-bearing fluids
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Amalia Jiménez, Joel Marcelo Coronel, José Manuel Astilleros
abstract: The transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in phosphate or phosphate-sulfate bearing fluids was investigated through hydrothermal experiments at 60–80 °C up to 90 days. A phosphate-only system (BF) and a phosphate-sulfate system (BFS) were characterized by XRD, FTIR, and aqueous geochemical analyses supported by PHREEQC modelling. In both series, the reaction proceeded via an interface-coupled dissolution–precipitation mechanism, producing a two-stage sequence: hydroxylapatite (HAp) precipitation followed by calcite, consistent with the higher supersaturation of the fluid with respect to HAp. Variations in unit cell parameters are consistent with incorporation of HPO₄2− into HAp and oxyanions into secondary calcite. The contraction of the HAp c-axis and the decrease in dissolved sulfate (11.3% at 90 days), which may involve surface adsorption, are consistent with SO₄2− incorporation into the HAp lattice. Although dissolved P removal was similar in both series, calcite formed earlier and more extensively in BFS system (>83 vs. <30 wt% at 90 days), a difference not explained by the bulk saturation with respect to calcite. We hypothesize an indirect effect of sulfate, through the HAp intermediate and the Ca budget of the system, rather than a direct effect on calcite nucleation. Dissolved phosphate modifies the aragonite-to-calcite reaction pathway by introducing HAp as a reactive intermediate whose non-stoichiometric crystal chemistry may couple mineral replacement kinetics to fluid composition. Carbonate phosphatization may alter primary geochemical signatures in diagenetically altered carbonates from phosphate-rich environments and carbonate-to-apatite replacement is a potential pathway for P sequestration during carbonate diagenesis.

title: A multi-isotopic study to constrain groundwater geochemistry - case study of a quaternary sand and gravel aquifer in Cardiff, UK
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Zhe Dong, Katharine Hendry, David Boon, Ashley Patton, Jamie Lewis, Hong Chin Ng, Fiona Whitaker, Tong Wang, Xiaoning Liu, Tom Kibblewhite
abstract: Chemical alteration of groundwaters has implications for elemental fluxes into rivers, estuaries and coastal oceans. Individual isotope systems offer strong process constraints, while integrating multiple isotopes adds complementary insight that reveals the complexity of coupled geochemical processes. Here, we use multiple stable isotopic systems to investigate the physical and chemical controls on groundwater composition in a Quaternary sand and gravel coastal aquifer from Cardiff, UK. Stable isotopic compositions of silicon (Si), magnesium (Mg), and strontium (Sr), along with radiogenic Sr isotopes reveal significant impacts of anthropogenic interventions on the groundwater system, particularly the construction of a barrage and groundwater extraction. The saltier coastal groundwaters likely reflect contributions from saline estuarine/seawater-derived water and/or localized seepage from the underlying Triassic bedrock. This influx of saline water, combined with reducing conditions, has facilitated calcite precipitation that has removed substantial amounts of dissolved calcium (Ca) from the groundwater. The mechanisms controlling dissolved silicon (DSi) dynamics in the groundwater are complex. In coastal regions, silica precipitation predominantly influences DSi concentrations and isotopic composition, whereas vegetation uptake is the primary control on DSi concentrations and isotopic signatures in inland groundwaters. These findings are crucial for understanding the intricate interplay between natural processes and human interventions in shaping groundwater geochemistry, offering valuable insights for managing coastal water resources and mitigating anthropogenic impacts. By providing a multi-isotopic framework for investigating groundwater systems, this study provides a clearer perspective on the factors controlling modern and palaeo groundwater chemistry and can aid in predicting solute fluxes from groundwater to the ocean.

title: Coupled redox reactions in solution enable incorporation of labile ruthenium in iron (oxyhydr)oxides
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Sebastian T. Mergelsberg, Libor Kovarik, Elaine D. Flynn, Duo Song, Jeffrey G. Catalano, Eugene S. Ilton
abstract: Platinum group elements (PGEs) are substantially enriched in laterite soils formed over ultramafic terrains, where they correlate strongly with Fe and concentrate in Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides. However, the redox kinetics and structural fate of Ru during Fe oxide crystallization remain poorly characterized. Here we combine UV–Vis spectroscopy, high-energy X-ray diffraction, TEM, pair distribution function analysis, and Ru K-edge XANES and EXAFS spectroscopy to probe the coupled behavior of Ru and Fe during the formation and aging of ferrihydrite and goethite. Ferrozine titrations show that dissolved Fe(III) rapidly oxidizes lower-valent aqueous Ru species to Ru(IV) within minutes. Co-precipitation at pH 6.8 and 11 incorporates Ru(IV) into ferrihydrite as a dilute substituent at octahedral Fe sites, with no evidence of RuO₂. Subsequent conversion to goethite via aging at 21 °C (100 days) or 60 °C (3 days) retains Ru(IV) in the solid phase, where it maintains a ferrihydrite -like local coordination environment within the goethite host. Further, STEM shows that Ru is homogeneously distributed through goethite and discrete phases do not form. These results establish that structural incorporation of Ru into Fe (oxyhydr)oxides is both thermodynamically and kinetically accessible under conditions relevant to laterite formation and provide mechanistic constraints on the enrichment of Ru in the Fe oxyhydroxide fraction.

title: Rodingites as archives of Ca-Mg-Fe metasomatism and trace element mobility: Constraints from Mount Orliakas (Pindos Ophiolite, Greece)
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): L. Tsiarsioti, C. Karkalis, A. Sideridis, H. Tsikos, P. Mason, P. Petrounias, P. Pomonis, A. Rogkala, P. Koutsovitis
abstract: Rodingites serve as critical archives of fluid-rock interaction in mafic-ultramafic complexes. In the Mount Orliakas massif (Pindos Ophiolite, Greece), rodingitization of gabbronoritic protoliths occurred through distinct multi-stage Ca-metasomatism within serpentinized ultramafics. Notably, the dykes preserve nearly unaltered gabbroic cores, providing a direct reference for quantifying metasomatic fluxes without relying on extrapolated protolith compositions. Stage-1 (~370 °C, 3–5 kbar) formed prehnite and grossular, while Stage-2 (~300 °C, final exhumation) developed (hydro)andradite, Ti-rich garnet, and vesuvianite. Geochemical trends reveal a two-stage fluid evolution: initial Ca-enrichment coupled with Si, Mg, and Fe depletion (Stage-1), followed by distinct Mg and Fe enrichment in advanced Stage-2 rodingites. This reversal marks a shift to Mg-Fe-rich fluids driven by extensive interaction with surrounding serpentinizing ultramafics. Alkali depletion reflects plagioclase replacement by garnet. Trace elements show early REE depletion and late re-enrichment; Th, Ta, Nb, Cr, and Ni were depleted, while Zr was enriched. Highly mobile elements (Ba, Pb, Cs, U, As) were largely removed. Notably, Ti was immobile in shallow Group-A but mobilized at depth in Group-B rodingites, while Nb and Y showed inverse enrichment, reflecting pressure-dependent fluid mobility. Thermodynamic modeling results (PERPLE_X) validate the P-T path, constraining the Stage-1 to Stage-2 transition as a shift towards oxidizing, low-CO₂, Fe-Mg-rich fluids. These findings highlight rodingitization as a key process in element mobility within mafic-ultramafic complexes, controlled by protolith depth, redox conditions, and evolving fluid composition.

title: Experimental mineral carbonation of three ultramafic rocks in a simplified CO 2 -H 2 O system: Implications for Ni, Co, and Cr mobility
description: Publication date: 20 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 728 Author(s): Błażej Cieślik, Anna Pietranik, Alicja Lacinska, Keith Bateman, Krzysztof Turniak, Jakub Kierczak
abstract: Ex situ single-stage aqueous mineral carbonation experiments were conducted on three ultramafic rocks (UMR), including two serpentinized peridotites (SP I and SP II) and one serpentinite (S), in a simplified CO2-H2O-UMR reaction system at 50 °C and 20 bar CO2, and 185 °C and 150 bar CO2. We examined carbonation efficiency, fluid chemistry, and Ni, Co, and Cr mobility. At 50 °C, Mg-silicate dissolution dominated, but limited carbonate precipitation resulted in negligible CO2 sequestration. At 185 °C, magnesite precipitation yielded carbonation efficiencies up to 43% after 48 h. Although SP I and SP II initially contained similar olivine proportions (≈ 45 and 48 wt%), their carbonation efficiencies differed markedly (≈ 11% and 43%, respectively). The slightly more Fe-rich and Ni-poor olivine in SP II may have promoted dissolution, while inherited alteration may also have influenced reactivity. The olivine-free serpentinite achieved carbonation efficiency comparable to SP I. Fluid compositions showed MgSi decoupling: Mg accumulated during low-temperature dissolution but decreased as magnesite precipitated at 185 °C, whereas dissolved Si increased despite calculated supersaturation with respect to amorphous silica. Ni and Co were mobilized during Mg-silicate dissolution, but their aqueous concentrations were not directly proportional to Mg release. Measured Ni concentrations were lower than estimates based on olivine Ni/Mg ratios; retention in secondary reaction products is plausible but unconfirmed. Chromium concentrations in recovered fluids remained very low, consistent with limited release from Cr-bearing spinels. These findings highlight the importance of reaction conditions and feedstock characteristics for CO2 storage and trace-metal mobility.

title: Fractionation of sulfide and platinum-group minerals in Macquarie Island magmas: Implications for platinum-group element systematics during mid-ocean ridge magma differentiation
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Gyuchan Park, Jung-Woo Park, Vadim S. Kamenetsky, Jiwon Hwang
abstract: Platinum-group element (PGE) behavior in mid-ocean ridge basalt (MORB) magmas is commonly interpreted to reflect the segregation of immiscible sulfide liquid. Nonetheless, experimental studies suggest that under the reduced redox conditions of MORB systems, discrete platinum-group minerals (PGMs) may become stable and influence PGE budgets. However, direct constraints from natural samples on their role during MORB magma differentiation remain limited. Here, we investigate cogenetic MORB glasses and olivine-rich lavas and dykes (picrites) from the Macquarie Island ophiolite (SW Pacific) to evaluate the relative roles of immiscible sulfide liquid and PGMs during early MORB magma evolution. Most glasses and picrites exhibit broadly subparallel, smoothly fractionated PGE patterns with coherent inter-element correlations, indicating that sulfide liquid segregation and accumulation exert a first-order control. This is supported by magmatic sulfide globules showing PGE patterns similar to their host picrites, except for negative Pt anomalies, which can be attributed to Pt-As phase exsolution. The high Fo contents of sulfide-hosting olivine indicate that sulfide saturation occurred in near-primary melts (Mg# = 69–72). Notably, the observation of a Pt-rich alloy within a sulfide globule provides direct mineralogical evidence for discrete PGMs. Such an alloy is likely to have formed by direct crystallization from silicate melt, given the occurrence of a Pt-As phase in a separate sulfide globule from the same sample. The jagged PGE patterns and large discrepancies between duplicate whole-rock analyses of some samples provide complementary geochemical evidence for PGM crystallization during Macquarie Island magma differentiation, further revealing additional Ru-Os-Ir(-Pt)-rich PGMs. Our results highlight that the segregated sulfide liquid in MORB determines the first-order PGE systematics, whereas discrete PGMs exert a second-order, but locally dominant, control during MORB magma differentiation.

title: Marine authigenic–diagenetic processes associated with heavy rare earth element enrichment in early Cambrian black shales, South China
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Ferdon Hamit, Liu Willow Yang, Tao Yang
abstract: Early Cambrian black shales of the Yangtze Block, South China, show anomalous heavy rare earth element (HREE) enrichment, but the mineral hosts and enrichment processes of rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) in organic-rich, redox-stratified black-shale systems remain poorly constrained. We combine TIMA mineral mapping, SEM–EDS observations, and quantitative EPMA analyses with whole-rock major- and trace-element concentrations, total organic carbon (TOC) contents, and Nd-isotope compositions from the Gongxi (GX) and Ganshanpo (GSP) sections of the basal Niutitang Formation. Mineralogical data from three thin sections identify xenotime-(Y) and monazite-(La) as the principal REY-bearing phases observed. Apatite accounts for <0.01 mass% of the mapped mineral assemblages, although a minor fine-grained or unresolved contribution cannot be excluded. Contrasting xenotime textures in GX and GSP suggest different local precipitation and post-depositional modification conditions. HREE-enriched patterns, genuine negative Ce anomalies, and elevated Y/Ho ratios indicate that the precursor REY inventory underwent marine cycling and acquired seawater-like fractionation characteristics, whereas the Ba-corrected GX dataset does not support a dominant high-temperature hydrothermal contribution. Whole-rock εNd(t) compositions provide qualitative constraints on provenance and source mixing, whereas positive ΣREY–lithogenic-element covariation suggests a possible terrigenous influence on the precursor REY inventory but cannot quantify its magnitude or establish detrital hosting of enriched REY. Mo–U systematics and TOC relationships indicate heterogeneous redox-sensitive element sequestration, whereas hydrographic restriction is supported mainly by regional and stratigraphic evidence; V-based ratios provide supplementary constraints. These results support a marine authigenic–diagenetic model in which marine cycling, basin-regulated redistribution, and early-diagenetic phosphate fixation may have contributed to HREE enrichment.

title: Nd-Hf isotopes of clinopyroxene-orthopyroxene couples to decipher geochemical heterogeneity in depleted peridotites (Alpine-Apennine ophiolites)
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): C. Ferrando, V. Basch, G. Borghini, F. Genske, A. Stracke, E. Rampone
abstract: The geochemical heterogeneity of the mantle beneath mid-ocean ridges is documented by the variable radiogenic isotope ratios of abyssal peridotites and basalts. Incompatible element-depleted peridotites also occur in ophiolites of variable ages world-wide. The time when peridotites in ophiolite massifs last melted constrains the evolution of the paleo-ocean basin they originate from. Yet, estimating the ages of peridotites in ophiolite massifs becomes significantly more complicated if the strong geochemical heterogeneity documented in present-day abyssal peridotites also characterizes the ancient mantle of ophiolite massifs. Here, we apply a challenging approach, analysing the NdHf isotopic composition of coupled clinopyroxene and orthopyroxene within single samples to calculate dates for the last melting and melt-rock interaction events in peridotites from the Internal Liguride and Monte Maggiore ophiolites of the Alpine Tethys Ocean. This approach avoids the use of a theoretical average ‘Depleted Mantle’. The time of magmatic processes inferred from the new pyroxenes NdHf isotope data ranges from Late Triassic to Middle Jurassic, contemporaneous to the opening and maturing of the Alpine Tethys Oceanic basin. The NdHf isotope ratios of pyroxene couples in peridotites and pyroxenites indicate that MORB-like (on average εNdi 7.5 ± 2.5 and εHfi from 13 ± 4) to slightly more melt-depleted peridotites (on average εNdi 14 ± 3 and εHfi from 19.5 ± 3.5) coexisted in the subridge mantle of the Alpine Tethys Ocean. Finding remnants of peridotites which were variably melt-depleted prior to the embryonic opening of the Alpine Tethys Ocean (Internal Liguride) agrees well with the ubiquitous isotopic heterogeneity of peridotites from modern mid-ocean ridges, which indicates they have melted once, or several times, before recent processing under modern mid-ocean ridges.

title: A two-population lattice strain model for H + -coupled REE incorporation in zircon: calibration, detection threshold, and implications for LREE anomalies
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Ioan V. Sanislav, Mabrouk Sami
abstract: The classical single-site lattice strain model fails systematically for light and middle rare earth elements (LREE and MREE) in zircons from hydrous, phosphorus-undersaturated magmatic systems, predicting concentrations one to three orders of magnitude below observed values. We develop a two-population model in which the bulk partition coefficient is the mole-fraction-weighted sum of contributions from the ideal ZrO8 site and a second, enlarged site generated by REE3+–H+ coupled substitution. Both sites are parameterised by independent Brice parabolas; the fractional occupancy of the defect site, fd, follows a Langmuir saturation function of water content with half-saturation constant H0 = 422 ppm. Initial calibration of defect-site parameters against the 32 published SIMS spot analyses of Vema Fracture Zone oceanic gabbro zircons reported by De Hoog et al. (2014) gives an unconstrained Nd/Lu optimum of r 0 REE − H = 0.9916 Å, EREE–H = 592.1 GPa, D 0 REE − H = 344.5 (RMSE = 0.154 log10 units), whereas physically constrained weighted global optimisation, within-grain REE-pattern inversion, and DFT-consistent modest site expansion together indicate a preferred effective defect radius near 0.984 Å with an admissible envelope of ~0.975–0.993 Å. Forward modelling defines a detection threshold in temperature–[H2O] space below which the defect-site signal is unresolvable from geological noise, requiring [H2O]zrc > ~30–80 ppm depending on temperature. The model predicts that in hydrous, P-undersaturated systems the REE3+–H+ mechanism alone can produce Lazrc exceeding 0.1 ppm through genuine lattice incorporation, demonstrating that a fixed La threshold is not a universal inclusion-free criterion but depends on temperature, water content, and melt La concentration. The charge-balance ratio f d CB = (REY–P)/REY, recoverable from routine LA-ICP-MS data without water measurement, provides an independent estimate of defect-site occupancy and correlates with water-based estimates where the REE3+–H+ mechanism is active, thereby providing a quantitative test of mechanism activation across natural systems. The model is applicable specifically to P-undersaturated, hydrous, low-temperature magmatic systems where the REE3+–H+ mechanism has been independently confirmed by FTIR spectroscopy and charge-balance analysis.

title: In-situ δ 13 C and δ 18 O isotopic imaging of carbonates via laser-induced calcination and optimized gas transfer
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Alban Petitjean, Olivier Musset, Pierre Sansjofre, Christophe Thomazo
abstract: Laser-induced calcination offers a rapid, reagent-free alternative for generating CO ₂ from carbonates and is particularly suited to in situ isotopic analysis. However, its application with infrared isotope spectrometers has been limited by inefficient CO ₂ transfer and the relatively large amount of carbonate required for analysis. Here, we present an optimized CO ₂ transfer system based on active pumping that substantially improves gas collection efficiency. The new architecture increases the pressure in the transport vial to approximately 3 bar and reduces the minimum carbonate mass required for accurate and reliable isotopic measurements from approximately 30 mg to 5 mg, corresponding to a sixfold reduction. The reduced sample requirement enables localized analyses over areas of approximately 0.3 mm in diameter. In addition, the transfer system was coupled to an automated tube-handling device and an XY scanning stage, allowing sequential sampling and automated generation of spatially resolved δ 13 C and δ 18 O maps. The approach was validated through measurements of carbonate reference materials and applied to a heterogeneous speleothem sample, for which 49 spatially resolved measurements were acquired to produce a millimeter-scale isotopic map. These developments substantially improve the sensitivity, spatial resolution, and automation of laser-induced carbonate calcination, opening new possibilities for high-resolution isotopic mapping and the analysis of small or spatially heterogeneous carbonate samples.

title: Trace element degassing of fumarolic emissions in the Chilean subduction zone: The case of Guallatiri and Callaqui volcanoes
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Manuel Inostroza, Mauricio Aguilera, Cristóbal González, Amiel Nieto-Torres, Jean-Luc Piro, Javiera González, Andrés Vega
abstract: This study presents trace-element enrichments, aerosol contents, and emission rates at two Chilean volcanoes with fumarolic activity: Guallatiri and Callaqui. Sampling techniques included filter packs, ground-based remote sensing, and direct sampling, while analytical techniques involved ICP-MS and SEM. Solid particles in fumarolic plumes suggest erosive processes at the vent, whereas rounded sulfur particles agree with temperatures above the melting point of sulfur. However, unique dendritic salammoniac minerals are found, suggesting evaporative concentration of condensed steam droplets during storage. High chalcophile contents, especially for arsenic, indicate high mobility of these elements in fumarolic emissions, in contrast to the poorly to moderately enriched lithophile and siderophile elements. Arsenic emission rates in Guallatiri reach up to 55 kg/yr (increasing up to 270 kg/yr during periods of high SO2 degassing), while Callaqui's rates are <5.9 kg/yr. These values are modest compared to global emission rates from arc volcanoes like Etna, Stromboli, Masaya, and Ambrym. Nevertheless, Guallatiri and Lascar, the latter with ~110 kg/yr, can be regarded as significant sources of pollution in the Central Andes. Current and past degassing of Andean volcanoes, along with the circulation of hydrothermal solutions through the upper crust, are hypothesized to drive As contamination in this area. Magmatic (magma composition, sulfide saturation) and hydrothermal (variable water/rock ratio in the hydrothermal reservoir) processes are postulated to control trace-element distributions in fumarolic volcanoes. Future research should quantify the total budget of trace elements released by Central Andean volcanoes and deepen understanding of the physicochemical processes governing their transport and dispersal in the surrounding environment.

title: Hydrothermal alteration and time-lagged controls on deep limestone reservoir development: A case study of the Upper Permian Changxing Formation in the Central Sichuan Basin
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Jin Shigui, Song Zezhang, Zhang Benjian, Zhang Ziyu, Wu Meijia
abstract: Deep limestone reservoirs are important hydrocarbon exploration targets, yet their formation and pore preservation remain key issues in carbonate reservoir research; hydrothermal alteration offers an important perspective on these issues. This study investigates deep pore-type limestones of the Upper Permian Changxing Formation in the central Sichuan Basin using petrography, cathodoluminescence, fluid-inclusion microthermometry, U-Pb dating, and geochemical analyses. Cross-stratigraphic comparisons, focused on the Middle Permian Maokou Formation and supplemented by the Upper Sinian Dengying Formation, were used to characterize hydrothermal alteration and fluid sources and to constrain the response of the Changxing Formation to Late Permian thermal–tectonic activity associated with the Emeishan Large Igneous Province (ELIP) and related reservoir controls. Results show that: (1) medium- to coarse-crystalline dolomite (250–750 μm) and calcite occur locally in the Changxing Formation and exhibit petrographic characteristics typical of hydrothermal minerals; (2) geochemical evidence indicates contributions from seawater, meteoric water, and deep thermal fluids but only weak, localized hydrothermal overprinting, with both hydrothermal alteration and thermochemical sulfate reduction (TSR) less intense than in the Maokou and Dengying formations; (3) calcite U-Pb ages from the Changxing Formation (256.2 ± 6.1, 251 ± 7.5, and 244 ± 11 Ma) and relatively low homogenization temperatures (Th; 100–130 °C) constrain fluid activity to the Late Permian–early Early Triassic, indicating an attenuated, delayed response to residual ELIP thermal activity; compared with the Maokou Formation, hydrothermal alteration in the Changxing Formation began later, was shorter-lived, and was weaker; and (4) a “weak hydrothermal alteration–time-lagged reservoir control” model is proposed for deep limestones in the outer zone of the ELIP. High-energy reef-shoal deposition, penecontemporaneous dolomitization, and meteoric dissolution established the effective pore system. During shallow burial, weak hydrothermal activity optimized the reservoir through localized dissolution and recrystallization and, together with fluid overpressure, promoted early pore preservation. This model clarifies how weak hydrothermal alteration modified the Changxing reservoirs, highlights differences among the studied formations, and provides a framework for predicting deep limestone reservoirs in the outer zone of the ELIP.

title: Authigenic carbonate mineralization records episodic methane seepage and redox transitions in cold-seep sediments
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Mohd Sadique, Aninda Mazumdar, Ankita Ghosh, Aditya Peketi, Subhashree Mishra, Kalyani Sivan, Swati Verma, Sai Pavan Pillutla, Supriya G. Karapurkar, Renuka K. Panchal, Rudrajit Joardar
abstract: Authigenic carbonates precipitated during anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) preserve a valuable record of CH4 seepage, fluid-flow dynamics, and diagenetic processes in marine sediments. Here, we investigated a 3.6 m-long gravity core recovered from an active cold-seep site in the Mannar Basin, eastern Indian margin, using an integrated multi-proxy approach combining bulk sediment geochemistry, mineralogy, petrography, isotope geochemistry, and elemental geochemistry of carbonate concretions to reconstruct the CH4 seep evolution since marine isotope stage MIS-3. Alternate occurrences of aragonite and high-Mg calcite (HMC), together with thiotrophic Calyptogena sp. shells indicate temporal variations in CH4 flux and sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ) depths. Aragonite-rich intervals characterized by elevated Sr/Ca, uranium concentrations, negative Ce anomalies, low δ13CTOC values, and abundant seep fauna indicate relatively high CH4 discharge and carbonate precipitation close to the seabed. In contrast, HMC-rich intervals exhibit high Mg/Ca ratios, positive Ce anomalies, lower uranium concentrations, and relatively higher δ13CTOC values, reflecting reduced CH4 flux and carbonate precipitation under deeper, reducing porewater conditions. Mass balance-corrected δ13CTIC of bulk sediment and carbonate concretions indicate contributions from both thermogenic and predominantly biogenic CH4 sources. Petrographic, mineralogical, and elemental evidence further suggest dissolution and recrystallization of aragonite during burial diagenesis. The alternating precipitation of aragonite and HMC records cyclic CH4 seep activation and attenuation likely driven by variations in fluid migration through deep-rooted fracture-chimney systems and gas hydrate dynamics. These findings provide new insight into CH4 seep evolution, authigenic carbonate precipitation, and long-term CH4 cycling in hydrate-bearing continental margins.

title: Oxalate–metal and oxalate–mineral interactions governing heavy metal mobility during ferrihydrite transformation
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Xiaofan Pan, Xin Huang, Ning Deng
abstract: The environmental fate of heavy metals is strongly influenced by ferrihydrite (Fh) transformations. However, the influence of coexisting organic ligands on heavy metal mobility remains poorly understood, due to their complex and multifunctional effects on heavy metal speciation and transformation pathways. Here, we investigated how oxalic acid (Ox) affects Zn2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ fate during Fh transformation. In binary Fh-metal systems, metal mobility was primarily governed by ionic compatibility and mineral crystallography: Zn2+ (0.74 Å) and Cu2+ (0.73 Å) were less mobile and showed greater retention in hematite (Hm), whereas Pb2+ (1.19 Å) exhibited greater release, mainly retained in goethite (Gt). In ternary Fh-Ox-metal systems, Ox reversed these trends through two-stage control over metal speciation and mineral binding. At the Fh stage, Ox decreased metal-mineral affinity for Zn2+/Cu2+ through electrostatic repulsion of bioxalate complexes while enhancing Pb2+ binding via ternary surface complexation. During transformation, Ox reduced Hm's surface energy from 350 to 220 mJ·m−2, increasing nucleation rates ~85-fold over Gt. This kinetic advantage amplified affinity differences, leading to enhanced Zn2+/Cu2+ mobility but strong Pb2+ immobilization through coupled surface complexation and structural retention. These findings establish a mechanistic link between molecular-scale interactions, mineral crystallization kinetics, and heavy metal dynamics, providing insight into ligand-driven processes that govern heavy metal fate in natural and engineered environments.

title: A viscosity model for hydrous andesitic melts: Insights from Sakurajima andesite
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Pedro Valdivia, Jessica Streichert, Dmitry Bondar, Alessio Zandonà, Alexander Kurnosov, Joachim Deubener, Daniele Sonaglioni, Danilo Di Genova
abstract: Magma viscosity governs transport, deformation, and eruptive dynamics. However, accurate predictions of melt viscosity remain challenging for hydrous andesitic systems, which are commonly associated with explosive volcanic activity. Widely used empirical models often fail to reproduce the rheological properties of hydrous volcanic melts because laboratory measurements can be compromised by amorphous nanostructuration, nanocrystallization, and syn-experimental water loss. Here, we present a physically based viscosity model for hydrous andesitic melts using both iron-bearing and iron-free analog compositions representative of the Sakurajima volcanic system. By combining differential scanning calorimetry, viscometry, Raman spectroscopy, and Brillouin spectroscopy, we quantify the effects of temperature, water content, and transition metal concentration (e.g., Fe, Ti and Mn) on melt viscosity through their influence on the glass transition temperature and melt fragility. Flash calorimetry shows that the configurational heat-capacity step at the glass transition, relative to the glass heat capacity, increases with water content, consistent with the increase of melt fragility. Our results indicate that the widely used Giordano et al. (2008) model systematically overestimates melt viscosity under pre-eruptive conditions. For Sakurajima andesitic melt, our model predicts a pre-eruptive viscosity about 9 times lower than the estimate of the Giordano et al. (2008) model; similar overestimations, by up to a factor of 27, are also identified in other andesitic systems. These lower viscosities may affect estimates of magma ascent rates, viscosity gradients during degassing and fragmentation conditions, which remain to be quantified using conduit flow models.

title: Fluid-inclusion-petrography-guided chlorine isotopes in deeply buried continental halite reveal paleobrine and hydroclimate evolution
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Xintao Wang, Yunqi Ma, Pei Ni, Yuqin Sun, Peng Cheng, Hui Tian, Yong Chen
abstract: Halite δ37Cl is a promising proxy for reconstructing paleobrine and hydroclimate evolution in continental evaporite systems, but its reliability in deeply buried deposits depends on distinguishing primary isotopic signals from diagenetic modification. Here, we integrate fluid-inclusion (FI) petrography with targeted Cl isotope analysis of modern halite from the Qarhan Playa and deeply buried Early Eocene bedded halite from the Dongying Depression, China. Paired FI-rich and FI-poor primary crystals from modern halite show absolute δ37Cl differences of 0.01‰–0.54‰ (mean 0.28‰), but no systematic directional offset (mean signed difference = −0.02‰). Together with mass-balance constraints, these results indicate that inclusion-hosted brines exert a limited influence on measured primary-halite δ37Cl without producing a detectable systematic isotopic bias. In contrast, altered crystals from deep-buried halite show larger absolute δ37Cl differences from paired FI-rich primary crystals (0.23‰–2.02‰; mean 0.79‰), with shifts varying in both magnitude and direction. Burial-related closed-system brine–halite re-equilibration may modify the Cl concentration and potentially the δ37Cl composition of inclusion-hosted brines without necessarily resetting bulk whole-crystal δ37Cl, whereas open-system diagenetic fluid–halite interaction can overprint primary isotopic signatures. Petrographically screened FI-rich primary halite from the Dongying Depression preserves coherent δ37Cl trends that, combined with sedimentological evidence, reveal spatially variable brine evolution during the mid- to late Early Eocene Climate Optimum and an overall arid hydroclimate punctuated by short-term dry–wet fluctuations, followed by generally wetter conditions in the late interval. These findings establish petrographic screening as critical for reliable δ37Cl-based reconstruction of paleobrine and hydroclimate evolution in deeply buried continental evaporite systems.

title: Spatiotemporal variations of skarn garnet in the Imog tungsten deposit, South Korea: Constraints from in-situ geochemistry and oxygen isotopes
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Heonkyung Im, Eui-Jun Kim, Jeongmin Kim, Dongbok Shin
abstract: Skarn garnet preserves high-resolution records of hydrothermal fluid evolution and ore-forming processes. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of skarn formation and tungsten mineralization at the Imog W deposit, Taebaeksan Mineralized District, South Korea, using integrated in-situ trace element and oxygen isotope analyses of garnet. Garnets were classified into five textural groups within four spatial skarn zones: anhedral unzoned, irregularly zoned, oscillatory zoned, euhedral to subhedral unzoned, and euhedral zoned garnets. Major element compositions show a spatial transition from proximal andradite-rich to distal grossular-rich garnets, whereas intracrystalline zoning records temporal evolution toward more oxidizing conditions marked by core-to-rim increases in andradite content. Trace element compositions reveal systematic variations in REE patterns and Eu anomalies. Proximal and intermediate garnets show REE patterns broadly consistent with their major-element compositions, suggesting the influence of crystallographic site-size constraints, whereas those in distal zones reflect changes in fluid REE availability. Eu anomalies indicate increasingly oxidizing conditions from proximal to distal zones and toward later-formed garnet rims. Oxygen isotope data indicate magmatic-dominated fluids in proximal zones, locally modified by δ18O-enriched shale-derived hornfels, whereas zoned garnets record core-to-rim increases in δ18O reflecting progressive fluid–rock interaction. Zoned garnets in Zone 2 show W enrichment toward rims, coinciding with increasing andradite content and more oxidizing fluids. These results demonstrate that garnet geochemistry records changes in fluid composition and may provide useful indicators of fluid evolution favorable for tungsten mineralization.

title: Carbon redox processes during magma-fluid evolution recorded by melt and secondary fluid inclusions in Cenozoic nephelinite from eastern China
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Li Wang, Yuanjia Han, Zhiliang He, Xiaowen Guo, Baoqin Liu, Matthew Steele-MacInnis
abstract: Abiogenic carbon reduction has been widely documented in ultramafic and high-pressure metamorphic systems, whereas direct mineralogical evidence from alkaline mafic magmatic systems remains comparatively limited. Here, we document secondary fluid inclusions containing variable combinations of carbonate, CO2, graphitic carbon and CH4 in olivine phenocrysts from Cenozoic nephelinite in eastern China and compare them with melt inclusions hosted by clinopyroxene from the same sample. Integrated petrography and Raman spectroscopy indicate that these two inclusion assemblages preserve texturally and compositionally distinct magmatic and post-crystallization fluid records. The clinopyroxene-hosted inclusions are silicate-rich and are associated with apatite-group minerals and locally with Fe oxides or FeTi oxides, but no reduced carbon phases were identified. In contrast, olivine hosts abundant secondary fluid inclusions, in which CO2 is the most commonly detected volatile species. Graphitic carbon and carbonate are also common, and CH4 is rare. These inclusions occur mainly along healed fractures and are spatially associated with serpentine-group and iddingsite-like alteration in olivine. These observations support an interpretation that distinguishes a regional carbon-rich petrogenetic context from two directly observed inclusion records: silicate melt entrapment in clinopyroxene and a carbon-bearing fluid event recorded along healed fractures in altered olivine. We infer that interaction between the infiltrating fluid and olivine, including serpentine-forming hydration, may have generated localized reducing microenvironments in which partial reduction of oxidized carbon species was possible. The present data do not uniquely establish whether CH4 was present before or during entrapment or formed partly during subsequent post-entrapment re-equilibration within individual inclusions. Graphitic carbon may reflect one or more processes involving co-entrapment, carbon reduction and cooling-related re-equilibration. The contrasting inclusion assemblages therefore indicate that magmatic and secondary fluid processes are recorded separately in this nephelinitic system, with the latter being compatible with localized modification of carbon speciation during fluid-olivine interaction.

title: Mineralogical control on stable Cu and Fe isotopes fractionation during weathering of polymetallic copper ores (Anti-Atlas, Morocco)
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Julien Poot, Nadine Mattielli, Augustin Dekoninck, Mohammed Bouabdellah, Lhou Maacha, Johan Yans
abstract: This study presents the first Moroccan Cu and Fe isotopic data (δ65Cu and δ56Fe) on (hypogene and) supergene minerals from three polymetallic deposits (Tazalaght, Agoujgal, and Bou Skour) located in the Anti-Atlas Copperbelt. By analyzing pure mineral phases across hypogene to supergene zones, we show that isotopic fractionation is strongly governed by mineralogical paragenesis, host-rock composition, and fluid–rock interactions during weathering. Values of δ65Cu cover a wide range (−3.1 to +3.6‰), with extreme fractionation observed in malachite and Fe-(oxyhydr)oxides. The Cu-As(Pb) Agoujgal deposit exhibits unusually light δ65Cu in malachite, likely due to fractionation of heavy Cu isotopes by Cu arsenates, while the supergene pattern in the Tazalaght deposit shows heavy δ65Cu in carbonates. The Bou Skour deposit shows restricted Cu isotopic variation, reflecting site-specific setting due to the poor mobility of the weathering fluid and in situ mineral replacement. The δ56Fe values are deposit-specific, with a strong influence of the primary mineralogy isotopic composition. These findings underscore the importance of detailed mineralogical and geochemical characterization to interpret both Cu and Fe isotopic data, in order to reconstruct ore-forming supergene processes and fluid evolution in weathering profiles.

title: Element transport by saline mobile phases from subducted sediments: Implications for the origin of the slab component in arc calc-alkaline basalts
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Alexander G. Sokol, Olga A. Kozmenko, Alexey N. Kruk
abstract: Calc-alkaline arc basalts form with the participation of a hydrous slab component, but whether this component is an aqueous fluid, a hydrous melt or a supercritical liquid, and how chlorine affects its capacity to transport trace elements, remain debated. To address these questions, element fractionation in the pelite-H2O-CO2-NaCl system was studied experimentally at pressures of 3.0–7.8 GPa and temperatures of 750–1090 °C using the diamond trap method. Experiments on a natural pelite (without artificial trace element doping) with NaCl added simulate the conditions of warm (intermediate) and hot sediment subduction. Runs at 3.0 GPa and 750 °C yield a Cl-bearing, solute-rich fluid coexisting with an eclogitic residue that contains phengite plus accessory rutile, zircon, and monazite. At P ≥ 5.5 GPa and T ≥ 850 °C, the Cl-bearing solute-rich fluid evolves into a Cl-bearing mobile phase whose solute content is intermediate between that of a fluid and that of a supercritical liquid (SCL). With increasing pressure and temperature along a warm-subduction P-T path, the eclogite residue loses phengite, zircon and monazite, while mobile phase becomes markedly enriched in K2O and depleted in SiO2 and Al2O3. At the P-T conditions of hot subduction, the system instead produces a Cl-bearing hydrous melt. The obtained data on partition coefficients between the mobile phase and the residue show that a Cl-bearing, sediment-derived mobile phase transfers LILE and LREE, and under certain conditions also Th, more efficiently than a Cl-free mobile phase does. As a result, a hydrous slab component consisting of a pelite-derived, Cl-bearing (8 wt% Cl) fluid formed at 3.0 GPa and 750 °C can generate a partial melt whose trace element pattern closely resembles that of calc-alkaline basalts. At these conditions, Cl enhances the mobility of U much more than that of Th, so that the fluid has a primitive mantle (PM) normalized Th/U ratio of ~0.2, which is inherited by the partial melt. We infer that the fingerprint of slab-derived, Cl-bearing fluids in calc-alkaline basalts is a PM-normalized Th/U ratio below 1. A hotter, pelite-derived, Cl-bearing melt, formed in the absence of residual monazite, instead leaves a fingerprint with a PM-normalized Th/U ratio above 1, which is not characteristic of calc-alkaline basalts. The same atypical fingerprint would be left by a pelite-derived, Cl-bearing SCL-like phase, which could potentially form at 5.5 GPa where slabs dip steeply (≥60°). Comparison with available data indicates that, among the hydrous slab components that can potentially form under warm subduction conditions at arc depth, only a sediment-derived, Cl-bearing fluid can generate a melt with the trace element pattern of calc-alkaline basalts.

title: What do fluid lithium isotopes record: Insights from long-term water-rock interaction experiments
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Xianyi Liu, David J. Wilson, Alexander J. Krause, Tais W. Dahl, Sneha Ray Sarkar, Wesley T. Fraser, Chunyao Liu, Philip A.E. Pogge von Strandmann
abstract: Lithium isotopes are widely used to trace silicate weathering and its role in the long-term carbon cycle, yet whether fluid δ7Li values track weathering congruency, fluid residence time, or the reaction rate of solids remains debated. Here, we investigate this question using year-long water-rock interaction experiments with a range of lithologies (including gneiss and granite), and two starting-fluid compositions, combined with quantitative Li mass-balance modelling. Across all the experiments, dissolved δ7Li values increased rapidly within days to weeks, reflecting preferential removal of 6Li into rapidly forming Al-bearing secondary phases and/or adsorption sites. The mass-balance results demonstrate that fluid δ7Li values do not uniquely record weathering congruency: both monotonic and hump-shaped relationships emerge from the evolving imbalance between Li supply and removal, without requiring secondary-mineral dissolution. Moreover, δ7Li values show only a subtle relationship with the solid reaction rate. Fluid residence time primarily determines the system's progression towards a quasi-steady-state for Li, beyond which dissolved δ7Li values become buffered and largely insensitive to further increases in fluid residence time. These results suggest that the δ7Li evolution reflects combined effects from weathering congruency, fluid residence time, and solid reaction rate, and thus cannot be a unique tracer for a single factor. In contrast, we propose that Li concentrations at quasi-steady-state retain information on the integrated Li release rate of the weathering solids, potentially providing complementary constraints on rock reactivity and weatherability. Overall, our results provide a new explanation for the restricted range of δ7Li values observed in large rivers, and an updated conceptual framework for interpreting coupled Li concentration-isotope systematics in modern and ancient silicate weathering systems.

title: Carbonate alteration and preservation in hydrothermally active regions and implications for paleoelevation reconstruction in southern Tibet
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Lin Li
abstract: Post-depositional thermal and fluid overprinting in carbonate successions poses a fundamental challenge to isotope-based paleoclimate and paleoelevation reconstructions, particularly in tectonically active intermontane basins affected by intense dike intrusion and hydrothermal circulation. Yet the spatial extent of such resetting, and the conditions under which primary isotopic compositions survive, remain poorly quantified. Here, one-dimensional thermal conduction modeling is used to quantify the spatiotemporal evolution of wall-rock temperature under two endmember scenarios: transient high-temperature heating associated with dike intrusion, and sustained lower-temperature heating driven by fault-related hydrothermal fluid flow. Transient dike heating produces intense but spatially restricted clumped isotope resetting, whereas sustained heating generates a broader thermal perturbation but causes little solid-state reordering over modeled durations of 1–10 ka. These thermal and reordering modeling results are integrated with petrographic observations, stable and clumped isotope data, carbonate UPb geochronology, and fluid–rock interaction modeling to evaluate carbonate diagenesis in the Linzhou Basin, southern Tibet. Mid- to Late Cretaceous marine and lacustrine carbonates record a two-stage recrystallization history during latest Cretaceous crustal shortening, progressing from shallow-burial fluid-buffered alteration to deeper-burial rock-buffered alteration, with complete resetting of primary isotopic signatures. Early Eocene lacustrine and soil carbonates experienced spatially heterogeneous thermal and fluid alteration associated with dike intrusion at ~54–50 Ma, followed by fault-related hydrothermal circulation from the middle Eocene to the middle Miocene. Nevertheless, primary micritic textures and isotopic compositions are still preserved outside localized thermal aureoles and fluid-flow pathways. The preserved low clumped isotope temperatures and stable isotope values are consistent with previous inferences of a high (>4 km) Gangdese arc in southern Tibet during the early India–Asia collision. This study demonstrates that, although carbonate alteration can be extensive in tectonically and hydrothermally active regions, primary isotopic records may still survive and can be identified through integrated petrographic, geochemical, geochronologic, and thermal screening.

title: Deciphering detrital vs. authigenic K Ar clay ages from a Permian–Triassic fluvial deposit of southern Mexico
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Cynthia Bermúdez-Chávez, Teresa Pi-Puig, Jesús Solé
abstract: Understanding diagenetic and hydrothermal processes in continental siliciclastic rocks is challenging because detrital and authigenic minerals coexist. We investigate the Permian–Triassic fluvial Matzitzi Formation in southern Mexico using an integrated approach combining petrography, X-ray diffraction, bulk and in situ KAr dating, LIBS geochemistry, and vitrinite reflectance. KAr ages of clay-size fractions from sandstones and siltstones show three distinct grain-size trends ––constant, increasing, and decreasing with decreasing grain size–– showing variable mixing relationships. Combining grain-size dating with mineralogical information from X-ray diffraction, in situ KAr dating of matrix and some clasts, and chemistry obtained by laser ablation helps decipher the diagenetic history. Vitrinite reflectance values (2–3% R₀) indicate peak temperatures of ~200–250 °C, indicating burial depths of at least ~2–3 km. Post-depositional KAr ages from clay fractions range from ~220 to ~130 Ma. In situ laser-ablation KAr analyses from matrix domains reproduce this age range and show a main peak at ~214 Ma. Ages between 214 Ma and the Matzitzi sedimentation top (~240 Ma) reflect mixed ages between authigenic and detrital minerals, although the onset of diagenesis cannot be excluded. Older ages (~270 to ~900 Ma) correspond to detrital minerals from the basement. The main sericitization pulse near the Triassic–Jurassic boundary is interpreted as reflecting increased permeability and fluid circulation. Younger Jurassic ages record continued fluid flow, likely linked to fault reactivation and localized magmatic activity. This study suggests that combining bulk and in-situ KAr dating with mineralogical and geochemical constraints provides an efficient approach to differentiate detrital and authigenic signals in continental systems.

title: Comparative evaluation of analytical methods for quantifying serpentinization extent
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Xiuqi Shang, Long Li, Weidong Sun, Ruifang Huang
abstract: Accurate quantification of serpentinization extent is essential for determining reaction kinetics and understanding water-rock interactions in hydrothermal systems. X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric (TG) analysis, Raman spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy have been commonly employed in previous experimental studies to determine the extent of serpentinization. Still, their systematic biases have not been assessed. To assess the advantages and limitations of these methods, we established calibration curves using three binary series of standard mixtures (olivine–lizardite, peridotite–lizardite, and peridotite–brucite) and a ternary olivine–lizardite–brucite series in which the lizardite/brucite ratio matches the stoichiometric products of olivine serpentinization. TG analysis gives the highest precision and accuracy for systems containing a single hydrous phase (e.g., serpentine). When serpentine and brucite coexist, however, their dehydration temperature ranges overlap, so that any boundary chosen to separate them causes each phase to capture part of the other's weight loss. The magnitude and even the direction of this bias depend on the lizardite/brucite ratio and on how the weight loss is partitioned between the two phases. XRD-based results appear sensitive to preferred orientation and crystallinity variations, with the Rietveld method showing limited reliability for samples with low serpentinization extents. The XRD peak-height and peak-area ratio methods deteriorate further once a third phase is present. FTIR quantification is highly sensitive to data processing methods, while Raman spectroscopy exhibits high variability due to its limited sampling area and fails for a minor hydrous phase. These calibration curves were then applied to serpentinized products from hydrothermal experiments, where the four methods gave systematically divergent results. The method-dependent discrepancies stem primarily from crystallinity mismatches between experimental products and calibration standards, and are most pronounced at low serpentinization extents. These findings provide practical guidance for method selection to improve the accuracy and comparability of serpentinization extent determination.

title: Cadmium isotopes as productivity proxy during the Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (OAE2): insight from the Trans-Saharan epicontinental seaway
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Usman Abubakar, Simon V. Hohl, Musa B. Usman, Abdulwahab M. Bello, Philipp Gleissner
abstract: The Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (OAE2) caused major perturbations in global carbon and nutrient cycles, characterised by enhanced productivity and organic matter burial under widespread marine anoxia. Cadmium (Cd) isotopes are a useful tool for tracking nutrient utilization by primary producers, yet few sedimentary records from shallow epicontinental seas exist. In this study, we report Cd isotope compositions and concentrations from the Ashaka section deposited in the Trans-Saharan Epicontinental Seaway (TIS) to investigate changes in Cd cycling and their relationship to weathering-derived nutrient supply during OAE2. The Ashaka section comprises a 24-m-thick succession of limestone and shale deposited during the Cenomanian-Turonian marine transgression into the TIS, which connected the proto-Atlantic and Tethys oceans. Elevated Chemical Index of Alteration (CIA) and lower K/Al ratios indicate intensified continental weathering and potentially enhanced nutrient delivery to the TIS. Authigenic Cd isotope compositions (δ114Cdauth) range from −0.92 to 0.21 ‰, with a pronounced negative anomaly during the OAE2. Relationships between Cd and total organic carbon (TOC) indicate that organic matter is the primary host of Cd in shales, while carbonate minerals serve as the dominant Cd host in limestone. Although CdS precipitation is generally considered a negligible Cd sink, mineralogical (XRD) evidence suggests that CdS precipitation may have influenced the Cd isotope compositions of two samples at the top of the section. Reconstructed Cd isotopic compositions of ambient seawater (δ114CdSW) reveal distinct changes in Cd cycling across OAE2. Before OAE2, the average δ114CdSW is consistent with a shallow-water signal potentially influenced by biological Cd uptake, although the extent of biological fractionation cannot be quantitatively constrained. During the initial build-up and recovery stages of OAE2, δ114CdSW approaches modern surface seawater values, consistent with biological uptake. In contrast, the trough and plateau phases are characterised by δ114CdSW values that are significantly lighter, reaching approximately −0.22 ‰, which are below typical modern deep-ocean values. This negative excursion suggests substantial changes in the Cd isotope composition of TIS seawater, potentially reflecting changes in biological Cd cycling, decomposition and recycling of organic matter, and increased input of isotopically light Cd from continental sources. Comparison with records from the Tarfaya Basin and Western Interior Seaway indicates that Cd cycling varied regionally during OAE2, with the shallow, semi-restricted TIS recording a particularly pronounced negative excursion. Our findings show that sedimentary Cd isotope records should not be interpreted exclusively as indicators of global marine productivity, because regional circulation, continental inputs, and nutrient cycling can exert substantial controls on the recorded signal.

title: Transformation from sink to source: Remobilization of Mo in seafloor Fe Mn oxides under oxic to anoxic conditions
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Zhengkun Li, Xiaoming Sun, Yu Fu, Haoyang Zhou
abstract: Molybdenum contents and isotopic compositions (δ98Mo) are important proxies for reconstructing paleo redox conditions, with marine FeMn oxides being one of its main hosts. However, the Mo signals recorded by FeMn oxides in anoxic environments remain poorly constrained. To address this, we performed controlled laboratory desorption experiments on Pacific FeMn nodules and crusts, simulating a range of oxic and anoxic conditions. Our results indicate that when adjusted to in-situ temperatures, the closed steady-state equilibrium Δ98Mo (δ98Mosolution-δ98Mosolid) between the solution and marine ferromanganese oxide samples may be ~2.42‰. The observed Δ98Mo of 3.00‰ between seawater and ferromanganese oxides may result from isotopic disequilibrium. Anoxic conditions, phosphate, and citrate enhance Mo desorption, while oxic conditions, low pH, Fe2+, and Mn2+ suppress it. Throughout desorption, released Mo is isotopically heavier than the residual solid but remains lighter than seawater. Δ98Mo is not a constant value and is negatively correlated with the desorption percentage. FeMn oxides may therefore function not as a stable burial sink, but rather as a dynamic intermediate reservoir. In pelagic sediments, early diagenesis could transform these oxides into a source of isotopically light Mo to seawater, possibly leading to bulk sediment δ98Mo higher than that of fresh FeMn oxides. These findings are applicable to FeMn oxide systems undergoing oxic to anoxic alteration, which may suggest the need to reassess the proportion of Mo hosted in oxic versus anoxic sinks and to better constrain the overall δ98Mo values of anoxic sinks.

title: The triple oxygen isotope compositions of land snail shells: implications for paleo-humidity and precipitation δ 18 O reconstructions
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Wenjie Wu, Rui Bao, Hao Yan, Jiawei Da, Zhengyu Xia, Chenglong Li, Xuefen Sheng, Jun Chen
abstract: The oxygen isotope composition of land snail shells is a valuable proxy for precipitation δ18O and regional hydroclimate, but its utility is often compromised by evaporative effect. Triple oxygen isotopes (Δ′17O) offer a potential means to quantify this effect, yet their application to land snail shell carbonates remains unexplored. Here we present the first investigation of Δ′17O in modern land snails from 21 sites across China, spanning humid coastal to arid inland regions. Δ′17Oshell values range from −104 to −58 per meg and exhibit a distinct spatial pattern: high values along the southeast coast, lower values in central China, and increasing values toward the arid northwest. No significant correlation with any single environmental factor is observed at national scale. Coastal Δ′17Oshell primarily reflects oceanic vapor signals but is modulated by seasonal biases in snail activity, whereas inland values are dominated by evaporative enrichment, with additional contributions from moisture recycling and snow/ice meltwater in the arid northwest. More importantly, we develop a snail-specific triple oxygen isotope framework for the Chinese Loess Plateau that enables reconstruction of ambient humidity and unevaporated precipitation δ18O. Reconstructed humidity is systematically higher than observed values, with offsets of 0.06–0.19. Through sensitivity analyses and Bayesian inversion, we demonstrate that this overestimation arises primarily because snails ingest δ18O-depleted water (e.g., dew) in addition to meteoric precipitation—a bias that must be accounted for in paleoenvironmental reconstructions.

title: Nitrogen-rich earliest Solar System planetesimals revealed by nitrogen measurements in iron meteorites using electron probe microanalyzer
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Debjeet Pathak, Gelu Costin, Rajdeep Dasgupta
abstract: The nitrogen (N) inventory of iron meteorites provides a window into the spatial and temporal distribution of N very early in the Solar System, i.e., predating the formation of chondrites. However, reconstructions of N abundances in the parent bodies of magmatic iron meteorites (IMPBs) that rely on accurate estimates of N concentrations in the meteorites themselves are lacking. Previous studies used a range of bulk and phase-specific analytical techniques to measure N in iron meteorites; however, these methods often yield estimates that differ significantly. To bring new constraints on N abundances in iron meteorites, we measured N concentrations in the kamacite and taenite of a suite of iron meteorites (both magmatic groups: Agoudal – IIAB (NC), Henbury, Boxhole – IIIAB (NC), Gibeon – IVA (NC), Balambala – IIF (CC), Dronino – Ungrouped (CC)) and non-magmatic groups Canyon Diablo, Mundrabilla – IAB-MG (NC), where NC represents the Non-Carbonaceous inner Solar system and CC represents Carbonaceous outer Solar system) using an electron probe microanalyzer (EPMA). Nitrogen concentrations range from 0.07(3) to 0.17(3) wt% in kamacite and from 0.05(1) to 0.13(3) wt% in taenite, where the values in parentheses represent the uncertainties as one standard deviation in the last digit(s). The N contents of coexisting taenite and kamacite follow the expected partitioning based on the Ni content of the phase, with Ni-poor kamacite being richer in N than Ni-rich taenite. The analyzed N contents in this study are more than an order of magnitude higher than previously reported bulk measurements, but are consistent with earlier phase-specific estimates obtained using SIMS. Using literature estimates of the modal proportions of kamacite and taenite, we reconstructed the bulk N contents of the crystallized iron meteorites. Using these new estimates, we reconstructed the N inventories of the bulk metallic cores and magmatic IMPBs. Our results indicate that the parent bodies of magmatic iron meteorites contained substantial N, comparable to those of enstatite chondrites and depleted relative to carbonaceous chondrites by no more than an order of magnitude. Based on the reconstructed N budgets of magmatic IMPBs, we further argue that these bodies most likely did not undergo differentiation through exposed molten surfaces, which would have caused significant N loss.

title: Arc duration and crustal thickness strongly influence the amount of zircon-bearing felsic crust and zircon volume in arc crust
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Paul Sotiriou
abstract: It has been proposed that arc duration and crustal thickness control the compositions of lavas erupted at active arcs, however, little is known about the relationship between the crustal thickness and duration of arcs and how these relate to the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust in arcs and the volume of zircon in arc crust. In this contribution, data were compiled on the duration, crustal thickness, chemical structure and lava and plutonic geochemical compositions of active and fossil arcs to better constrain the relationship between arc duration, crustal thickness and the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust and volume of zircon in arc crust. Longer-lived, thicker arcs have thicker intermediate to felsic plutonic sections than shorter-lived, thinner arcs. Thicker, longer-lived arcs (Kohistan, Gangdese) that were thickened during mid-crustal growth have greater proportions of intermediate to felsic crust than thinner, shorter-lived arcs (Talkeetna). The longer-lived, thicker Kohistan (115 Ma: 55 km) and Gangdese (200 Ma; 60 km) arcs contain up to an order of magnitude more zircon by volume (11.7 and 4.8 km3 of zircon per kilometre length of arc) compared to the shorter-lived, thinner Talkeetna Arc (35 km; 77 Ma; 1.17 km3/km). There are higher volumes of zircon-bearing felsic crust in the longer-lived, thicker Gangdese (233 km3 of zircon-bearing felsic crust per kilometre length of arc) and Kohistan (255 km3/km) arcs than the shorter-lived, thinner Talkeetna Arc (139 km3/km). Arc duration and crustal thickness strongly influence the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust in arcs and the volume of zircon in arc crust.

title: Dissolved inorganic carbon sources and CO 2 budgets in a permafrost-dominated catchment: Insights from stable carbon isotopes
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Zhou Huiling, Li Zongxing, Bai Ronglong, Wang Yunying, Xue Jian
abstract: As Earth's largest low-latitude permafrost domain, the Tibetan Plateau exerts a pivotal control on global carbon cycling. Nevertheless, lateral export of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and the resulting catchment-scale CO₂ balance in permafrost-dominated watersheds remain poorly quantified and understood. Here, we investigated DIC sources and seasonal CO₂ dynamics in the permafrost-impacted headwater catchment of the Shaliu River in the southern Qilian Mountains across the thaw seasons of two consecutive years (2021−2022). The results revealed that riverine DIC concentrations varied from 5.36 to 42.00 mg C L−1, with δ13C-DIC values spanning −10.66 ‰ to 1.68 ‰. MixSIAR modeling indicated that sulfuric acid-mediated carbonate weathering served as the predominant DIC source across the Shaliu River watershed. The contribution of this pathway in the permafrost-dominated upper and middle reaches ranged from 44% to 89%, which was 2–3 times greater than that in the lower reaches (18%–52%). The LOADEST model yielded annual DIC fluxes of 13.45–29.91 Gg yr−1, with 95% confidence intervals ranging approximately from −25% to +32%. Nearly 80% of the annual DIC export was delivered during the peak thaw season. Net CO₂ budget estimation further indicated that CO₂ emission derived from sulfide-induced carbonate dissolution (8.13 Gg yr−1) considerably surpassed the total CO₂ consumption via silicate weathering and carbonation-driven carbonate weathering (4.10 Gg yr−1) during the thaw period. This finding suggests that chemical weathering within the catchment functions as a net atmospheric CO₂ source. This carbon-source effect was most pronounced in permafrost regions. These findings suggest that permafrost thaw may promote sulfide oxidation, thereby enhancing DIC production and lateral export and shifting the weathering carbon budget toward a net CO₂ source. This sulfur-mediated weathering pathway may represent an underappreciated mechanism influencing inorganic carbon budgets in alpine permafrost catchments.

title: Chert as a recorder of diagenesis and paleoredox: Insights from the Early Silurian, SW Yangtze, China
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Yan Zhang, Haifeng Fan
