Here, we projected changes in EPE characteristics and associated cropland and population exposure across CA using daily precipitation simulations from five bias-adjusted ISIMIP3b global climate models under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5. The historical period 1995–2014 was used as the reference, and future changes were assessed for 2021–2040, 2041–2060, 2061–2080, and 2081–2100. The results show increasing extreme precipitation amount, frequency, intensity, and spatial extent toward the end of the century, particularly under SSP5-8.5 and in high-mountain regions. Under SSP5-8.5, cropland exposure increases by 46.4% from 2021 to 2040 to 2081–2100, with cumulative exposure of approximately 190.7 ± 73.7 million km2-days during 2021–2100. Under SSP3-7.0, population exposure increases by 97.2% between the first and last future periods, with cumulative exposure reaching approximately 47.12 ± 18.8 billion person-days during 2021–2100. Exposure hotspots are mainly located in northern Kazakhstan and the tri-border region of Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. Signed decomposition shows that climatic changes dominate most increases in cropland exposure, particularly under SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5, whereas the drivers of population exposure vary strongly among socioeconomic pathways, with demographic changes either reinforcing or offsetting climate-driven exposure changes. These findings highlight increasing exposure of Central Asian populations and croplands to future extreme precipitation and suggest the importance of strengthened flood management, agricultural drainage, early-warning systems, and climate-resilient land-use planning.

title: A hydrological comparability framework for hydropower potential assessment: evidence from China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Ning Xu, Peifang Leng, Qiuying Zhang, Zhipin Ai, Gang Chen, Fadong Li
abstract: Hydropower outputs depend on water availability, hydraulic head, conversion assumptions and the operating rules or constraints applied. Meaningful comparison of reported values requires identifying the specific quantity being assessed and the methodological, spatial, temporal, and operational conditions under which each value was derived. This structured critical review examines 100 China-focused, benchmark, and conceptual studies, linking 362 terminology records and 358 quantitative-output records from 73 papers. Differences in assessment objects, hydrological baselines, spatial aggregation, and operation and feasibility constraints explain why similar terms or units can describe distinct quantities. Source studies illustrate how runoff timing, storage, turbine releases, and ecological requirements enter resource, generation, and risk assessments. The framework connects author terminology, assessment objects, conditioning layers, and metric families to a question-specific comparison procedure. Users align the required quantities and reference conditions, distinguish deliberately varied conditions, and identify the permitted interpretation. Numerical comparison requires compatible quantities and reference bases. Design differences may constrain interpretation, whereas incompatible quantities or missing essential information may preclude meaningful numerical comparison. Contextual values retain their background role and attribution. A conditional reporting table and five-item checklist specify the information needed to apply the procedure in hydrological assessment, basin and cascade planning, and reservoir management.

title: Sedimentary reorganization under sediment starvation and morphological restructuring in a human-modified mega-estuary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Dezheng Liu, Ziyun Xu, Ruiqi Chen, Sihao Mo, Liangwen Jia, Eunji Byun, Yan Miao, Haotian Wu
abstract: Estuaries worldwide are experiencing unprecedented anthropogenic pressures. However, the compound effects of sediment starvation and local morphological alterations on estuarine systems remain incompletely understood. The Lingdingyang Bay (LDB) of the Pearl River Estuary as a case study, this research integrates sedimentary records, long-term hydrological observations, and bathymetric data to reveal the estuarine response to multiple human stressors. Our findings indicate an abrupt and systemic shift in the estuarine hydrodynamic and sedimentary regime during the mid-1990 s. This shift was primarily driven by two concurrent factors: a ∼ 39% reduction in fluvial sediment supply due to upstream damming, which deprived the estuary of its natural sedimentary compensation, and high-intensity localized engineering (e.g., channel dredging and land reclamation). These morphological modifications leading to a persistent increase in the tidal range by over 30%. Driven by these combined impacts, the LDB underwent a source-sink reorganization, transitioning from a naturally efficient sediment sink to a human-regulated state characterized by internal erosion and localized deposition. The sustained increase in coarse-grained fractions and high-energy geochemical indicators in sedimentary records further reflects enhanced sediment reworking and bed-material winnowing. This study provides a observational framework for understanding how the coupled impacts of sediment starvation and localized morphological changes drive persistent shifts in highly modified mega-estuaries.

title: Infiltration dynamics of vegetated soils controlled by drought-induced root-soil interface evolution
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Qing Cheng, Ling-Xin Cui, Qi Zhang, Zhan-Ming Yang, Chao-Sheng Tang, Viroon Kamchoom, Bin Shi
abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of drought events, which can substantially modify soil infiltration by altering root morphology and soil pore structure in vegetated soils. However, how drought-induced root-soil interface evolution regulates infiltration dynamics remains insufficiently quantified. In this study, compacted soil specimens with different planting densities of ryegrass, i.e., 0, 24, and 48 g/m2, were subjected to progressive drying to target gravimetric water contents of 24%, 20%, 16%, 12%, and 8%. Infiltration tests were combined with photogrammetric volume measurements and root morphological analyses to quantify root diameter, root volume, root length density, and root freshness. The results show that the infiltration capacity of bare soil increased continuously as water content decreased. In contrast, vegetated soils showed a two-stage response, in which infiltration capacity and steady infiltration rate first increased and then decreased during drying. This response was controlled by the evolving root–soil interface. In the early drying stage, root shrinkage exceeded soil pore shrinkage, weakening root–soil contact and enhancing preferential flow along the root–soil interface. With further drying, root shrinkage became less pronounced than soil pore shrinkage, leading to closer root–soil contact and reduced hydraulic efficiency of the interface. Root decay and pore clogging further weakened the contribution of the root–soil interface to water flow. A simplified infiltration equation incorporating root diameter was then developed to estimate infiltration rates in vegetated soils under different drying conditions. Model validation showed good agreement between predicted and measured infiltration rates. These findings reveal that drought can reorganize root–soil hydraulic interactions and induce transient changes in infiltration, providing a mechanistic basis for improving predictions of soil–water redistribution and hydrological responses in drought-prone vegetated landscapes.

title: Hydrologic transition pathways shape microbial nitrogen cycling and N 2 O emissions under saltwater intrusion in coastal riparian soils
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Qi Wei, Qi Wei, Junzeng Xu, Zhiheng Huang, Xue Zhou, Peng Chen, Yilina Wu, Jinran Wu, Ziwei Li, Zhiming Qi
abstract: Hydrologic transitions in coastal riparian zones alter soil moisture and solute redistribution, thereby coupling water dynamics with nitrogen cycling. However, how transition direction interacts with saltwater intrusion to regulate N2O emissions remains unclear. This study examined the response of soil N2O emissions, microbial nitrogen-cycling functional genes, and functional microbial communities to the interactive effects of water level changes and salinity. To this end, an indoor soil-column experiment was established with two water-level transition regimes―a regime of non-flooding transitioning through intermittent flooding to continuous flooding (WD), and the reverse regime (WF)―and five salinity levels (0, 2, 5, 10, and 20 g L−1). N2O emissions showed clear differences in peak timing, peak intensity, and cumulative emissions between the two regimes. Under WD, emission peaks occurred during the early non-flooding stage, and low-to-moderate salinity enhanced N2O emissions, reaching 74.6 μg m-2h−1 under treatment with 5 g L−1 on day 1, whereas high salinity (20 g L−1) suppressed emissions. Under WF, emission peaks were delayed until drainage and drying ensued, and were lower in intensity. Water-level transitions shaped the succession of nitrogen-cycling functional genes in soil microbiota: WD favoured the enrichment of denitrification-related nirK and nosZ, whereas WF maintained higher AOB-amoA abundance. Salinity selectively suppressed AOB-amoA and nirK communities, whereas nirS and nosZ communities showed stronger halotolerance. Changes in functional microbial community composition, particularly those involving Pseudomonas, Halomonas, and Paracoccus, may be associated with N2O emission responses to water-level transitions and salinity changes. Structural equation modeling identified significant direct associations between the abundances of nitrogen cycling functional genes and N2O fluxes under WF, whereas the corresponding paths under WD were not significant. These results identify hydrologic transition trajectories as a key control on the timing and microbial pathways of nitrogen cycling under salinization, advancing understanding of coupled hydrological-biogeochemical processes in coastal critical zones.

title: Marked thermal heterogeneity within a small mountain stream network and its response to climate warming
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Luca Bonacina, Valeria Mezzanotte, Riccardo Fornaroli
abstract: Water temperature is a key driver of aquatic ecosystems, yet thermal heterogeneity across river networks at fine spatiotemporal scales remains poorly understood. This study investigates the thermal regime of five mid-altitude streams (500–1400 m a.s.l.) in the Serio River catchment (Orobic Alps, Northern Italy), influenced by contrasting water sources (snowmelt/stormwater vs. groundwater) and hydrological modifications (reservoirs), and evaluates how thermal patterns may change under future climate warming scenarios. Sub-daily temperature monitoring at 16 sites over 2017–2022 enabled the characterization of multiple aspects of the stream thermal regime: magnitude, variability, range, frequency, timing, and duration of thermal events, and catchment-scale thermal heterogeneity in relation to environmental drivers. Watercourses exhibited distinct thermal responses associated with lithology, hydrology, and reservoirs: siliceous, unregulated streams were thermally reactive, closely tracking air temperature, whereas groundwater-fed and reservoir-regulated streams were thermally buffered and less sensitive to warming. Catchment-scale thermal heterogeneity was pronounced (3.6 °C in annual means and up to 8.7 °C across maxima), comparable to that of alpine systems influenced by glaciers, and is projected to change under climate warming. The fine-scale variability of thermal habitats within a small area highlighted the importance of understanding thermal dynamics for interpreting ecological patterns and guiding conservation strategies.

title: Flow velocity drives divergent functional and structural responses in a rheophilic Yangtze fish: implications for aquatic ecosystem management
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Waleed Afzal Naveed, Mian Adnan Kakakhel, Xiaotao Shi, Jiang Zewen
abstract: Altered flow regimes caused by dams and hydropower operations can modify hydraulic conditions experienced by riverine fishes, yet the biological consequences of graded water velocity across multiple levels of organisation remain poorly understood. This study investigated the responses of juvenile Coreius guichenoti to four water velocity regimes (control, low, medium, and high) during repeated exposure over seven days. Swimming performance, behaviour, oxidative status, innate immune responses, inflammatory cytokines, and white muscle histopathology were evaluated, and machine-learning models were used to assess integrated response patterns. Medium velocity increased critical swimming speed, antioxidant enzyme activities, lysozyme activity, and serum immunoglobulin M, whereas high velocity reduced swimming capacity and increased cortisol, lipid peroxidation, pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and refuge-seeking behaviour. In contrast to these non-monotonic physiological responses, muscle pathology increased progressively with velocity. A random forest classifier achieved 90% cross-validated accuracy in distinguishing velocity treatments, while physiological biomarkers explained 36% of the variation in individual swimming performance. These findings demonstrate that altered hydraulic conditions can elicit divergent functional and structural responses in rheophilic fish, highlighting the need to incorporate biological response thresholds and hydraulic refugia into environmental flow assessment and management.

title: Hydrological forcing reshapes nitrogen partitioning under microplastic amendment in hyporheic zones
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Shiqi Liu, Zhenhua Yan, Tao Zhang, Xi Chen, Lan Ma, Yuqiong Yang, Ping Lu, Saiyu Yuan, Guanghua Lu
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as potential modifiers of nitrogen (N) cycling in aquatic sediments. Hyporheic zones (HZs), hotspots for riverine N transformation and important sinks for MPs, are exposed to dynamic hydrological forcing. However, how hydrological forcing structures N transformation responses in MP-amended HZs remains poorly understood. Here, we used field-collected sediments to simulate HZs and examined N transformation responses in sediments amended with conventional polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) MPs under contrasting drying-rewetting alternation (DWA) regimes and hydraulic retention time (HRT) levels. DWA enhanced sediment reoxygenation, weakened dissolved oxygen (DO) stratification, and altered putative nitrification-related taxa, enzyme-associated protein responses, and selected N-cycling functional genes in a polymer-specific manner. In PVC-amended HZs, DWA strengthened the coupling between nitrification-related responses and apparent nitrate reduction, whereas in PLA-amended HZs it promoted oxidative N transformation indicators but reduced apparent nitrate reduction, NO2 − accumulation, and NH4 + accumulation. Longer HRT reduced DO availability and generally increased apparent NO3 − reduction. In PVC-amended HZs, this was accompanied by greater NO2 − and NH4 + accumulation. In PLA-amended HZs, higher dissolved organic carbon (DOC) availability and sustained low-DO conditions coincided with greater apparent NO3 − reduction and stronger NO2 − and NH4 + accumulation. Multivariate analyses identified DO-centered associations under DWA and PVC-HRT, whereas DOC-centered associations emerged under PLA-HRT. These findings show that hydrological regime and polymer identity jointly structure N transformation responses in MP-amended HZs, with distinct patterns associated with oxygen availability, carbon availability, and nitrate-derived N partitioning.

title: Unsupervised transfer learning for cross-condition pipe burst localization in long-distance water conveyance systems
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Pengyu Li, Xiaodong Yu, Xingping Jiao, Jie Zhang
abstract: Concealed small-orifice pipe bursts in buried long-distance water conveyance pipelines are difficult to localize accurately and promptly and can cause sustained water losses and increased risks to water-supply security. Labeled records of real bursts are scarce, and variations in operating conditions can alter the propagation and statistical characteristics of water-hammer transient responses, causing source-domain localization models to degrade when applied to unlabeled target conditions. This study develops an unsupervised domain adaptation framework for cross-condition pipe burst localization. Source- and target-domain multi-channel water-hammer transient datasets are generated using the Method of Characteristics, and localization is formulated as a multi-task problem involving segment classification, within-segment offset regression, and leakage-ratio prediction. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) is first trained as the source-domain backbone and then adapted to the target domain by combining domain-specific batch normalization, adversarial feature alignment, and segment-level pseudo-label constraints. These components address shallow statistical shifts, high-level feature-distribution discrepancies, and weak target-domain segment discrimination, respectively. The framework is evaluated using a long-distance water conveyance project in Xinjiang, China. Without using ground-truth target-domain labels during training, it reduces the target-domain global localization mean absolute error from 1013.77 m under direct transfer to 128.51 m. The results indicate that the proposed method improves pipe burst localization under unlabeled cross-condition scenarios, with potential benefits for rapid field inspection, water-loss reduction, and reliable operation of long-distance water conveyance systems.

title: Cross-scale characterization and controlling mechanisms of fluid migration in structurally heterogeneous rough fractures
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xu Ren, Sida Jia, Quan Gan, Funing Ma, Junjun Chen, Zhenxue Dai
abstract: Fractures govern hydraulic connectivity and fluid migration in deep aquifers and reservoirs. Reservoir models often simplify rough fractures as parallel plates or assign empirical equivalent permeability. These assumptions obscure the effects of local aperture variation on preferential flow pathways. We develop a framework linking rough fracture flow across grid, core, and field scales. At the grid scale, fracture surfaces are represented as local plane cutting units. Upper surface, lower surface, and double surface cutting capture aperture variation and yield 12,000 local flow samples. A hybrid residual network (Hybrid ResNet) maps these geometries to equivalent porosity and permeability. At the core scale, lateral offset between conjugate rough surfaces creates a single fracture. A permeability relation is developed and tested using 416 numerical cases covering aperture scale, relative roughness, and surface offset. Independent validation gives an R 2 of 0.80 and an RMSE of 0.035. The relation is incorporated into a coupled thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, and chemical (THMC) model for reservoir flow simulations. At the core scale, relative roughness reduces connected flow space. Surface offset changes wall matching and redirects the main channels. Sobol analysis of the fitted empirical relation ranks aperture scale highest within the analyzed ranges. Its total-effect index for hydraulic correction is 0.42. At the field scale, rough fractures redistribute interwell flow and delay CO2 breakthrough from 4.20 to 4.71–4.93 years. Rearranging the same hydraulic correction values among reservoir cells also changes breakthrough timing. The framework links local fracture geometry to plume migration. It supports breakthrough risk assessment in fractured aquifers and reservoirs.

title: Multi-section, multi-time reconstruction of water-level and bed-level evolution under oblique-flow bend conditions via multi-stream deep learning
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Song-Yue Yang, Sze-Teng Liong, Shih-Chao Wei, Chiun-Chau Su, Y.S. Gan, Cheng-Jia Li
abstract: Oblique flows at river bends can induce levee-toe scour and threaten flood-protection structures. This study develops a multi-stream deep-learning framework for reconstructing water level (WL) and bed level (BL) conditioned on a known event hydrograph. The laboratory dataset contains 110 hydraulic events, including 80 steady-flow and 30 unsteady-flow tests, with observations at 12 cross-sections and 12 sampling times per event. The model maps time, discharge, and cumulative inflow volume descriptors, together with five static variables, to 288 joint WL/BL outputs. In the implemented Multi-stream CNN–BiLSTM, the sampled event histories occupy the feature dimension and the BiLSTM receives a sequence of length one; its results therefore do not demonstrate recurrent learning across the 12 sampling times. Under the common 76/17/17 event-level split, the Multi-stream model obtained MAE = 0.0233 m, RMSE = 0.0328 m, and R 2 = 0.8046 , compared with 0.0244 m, 0.0349 m, and 0.7738 for the Single-stream model. Paired event-level bootstrap intervals support lower BL errors on this test split but do not establish a clear WL advantage. Separate WL and BL SHAP beeswarm plots describe attribution to the mean predicted response over the sampled sections and times. These attributions are statistical associations and do not establish physical causality. The framework provides a laboratory-scale event emulator; causal forecasting, explicit spatial adjacency, transfer to field conditions, and engineering accuracy for maximum scour remain unvalidated.

title: Spatiotemporal prediction and response-pattern zonation of soil moisture in Shanxi Province using PC-AtlasSM and Self-Organizing Maps
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Wenjie Wu, Xiao Liu, Lijuan Huo, Yun Zhang, Lei Song, Shuai Li, Yuxiang Liu, Gaiqiang Yang
abstract: Soil moisture dynamics in complex terrain are jointly controlled by rainfall inputs, evaporative losses, and topographically mediated redistribution. Existing methods often struggle to simultaneously achieve high short-term predictive accuracy and process interpretability at the regional scale. This study develops an operational framework for 1-h soil moisture prediction at 20 monitoring stations, exploratory response-pattern analysis; inverse distance weighting maps are visualization outputs, not fixed-resolution products. PC-AtlasSM integrates established antecedent-state, rainfall, evaporation, inertia, and bounded-update concepts in an explicit and auditable sequence rather than introducing a new learning principle or process equation. Taking Shanxi Province as a case study, we used soil moisture observations, meteorological variables, and topographic information to investigate regional spatiotemporal prediction and response-pattern zonation of soil moisture. Results show that PC-AtlasSM achieved the best performance for 1-h forecasting, with the lowest RMSE (13.385%) and MAE (4.026%), and the highest R2 (0.713). Relative to the persistence benchmark, the skill score reached approximately 27%. The sample-wise comparison with ExtraTrees supported an error reduction, although temporal dependence among hourly errors limits interpretation of the extremely small p value as evidence of an equally strong practical or generalizable improvement. The component audit identified temporal inertia as the only empirical stabilizer with a measurable aggregate effect; the wetting, drying, and dynamic caps did not alter aggregate test metrics and are retained only as precautionary safeguards. SOM summarized four exploratory statistical response-pattern classes. These classes describe associations in a feature space that includes soil moisture change; they do not independently establish causal controls or verified hydrological regimes. Together, the results support PC-AtlasSM as a transparent operational integration for short-term station-supported forecasting and exploratory response-pattern analysis, rather than as a new standalone algorithm. The framework may support soil moisture monitoring, drought–flood risk identification, and regional water-resources and hydro-meteorological risk assessment.

title: Incorporating physical guidance into deep learning through hard constraints for water transport modeling in unsaturated zone
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Yi Wang, Zhitong Ma, Wenke Wang
abstract: Water transport in the unsaturated zone is a key component of the hydrological cycle, and its accurate modeling is essential for water resources assessment and regulation. Physics-driven models require accurate soil hydraulic properties and fine discretization, whereas data-driven models may lack physical consistency and reliable extrapolation capability. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) incorporate governing equation residuals into the loss function, but soft constraints may inadequately enforce initial and boundary conditions and complicate optimization through competing loss terms. This study proposes a hard-constrained physics-informed neural network (HPINN) to address these limitations. The Richards equation is retained as a residual constraint, while transformation functions embed initial and boundary conditions directly into the network output, ensuring that these conditions are satisfied by construction. Numerical experiments spanning soil types, boundary conditions, and layered heterogeneous profiles evaluated predictions of matric potential, soil water content, hydraulic properties, and water fluxes. HPINN outperformed a standard deep neural network and PINN in predictive accuracy and physical consistency. Field validation under the investigated lysimeter conditions showed improved performance at unobserved times and depths, during heavy rainfall events, and under sparse observations. Reconstructed field-scale water fluxes characterized water transport processes and provided insights into the underlying hydrological mechanisms. By embedding physical knowledge as hard constraints, this study integrates data-driven and physics-driven modeling, providing a framework for simulating unsaturated zone water transport and advancing hybrid hydrological modeling.

title: A regime-specialized mixture-of-experts framework with event-driven case memory for daily multi-step streamflow forecasting
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Jiamu Chen, Jiahua Wei, Minglei Hou, Zhiming Zhang, Jinghao Zhang, Yanqing Shen
abstract: Accurate daily streamflow forecasting is crucial for flood risk monitoring and water resources operation, yet remains challenging due to regime nonstationarity and the scarcity of extreme-high-flow samples. A regime-specialized mixture-of-experts framework (RS-MoE) is proposed, integrating quantile-based regime partitioning, regime-specific experts, and a sparse gating router for streamflow forecasting. An optional event-driven case-memory module (RS-MoE-Mem) is further introduced as a post-routing residual-amplitude correction layer for tail-regime robustness. The framework is first evaluated on four representative stations in the Upper Yellow River for configuration selection and mechanism validation, and is subsequently transferred to 576 CAMELS-US basins for cross-region transferability validation. In the Upper Yellow River, RS-MoE and RS-MoE-Mem improve cross-station mean NSE from 0.860 to 0.863-0.867, raise high-flow NSE from 0.500 to 0.559-0.588 (+11.8% to +17.6%), and reduce high-flow RMSE from 0.064 to 0.059-0.057 (7.8%-10.9%). Lead-time decay is also alleviated, with day-7 NSE increasing from 0.780 to 0.787-0.791. Across 1,728 basin–family pairs, RS–MoE and RS–MoE-Mem achieve statistically significant gains (p ≤ 0.002), raising overall NSE from 0.044 to 0.285–0.295 and high–flow NSE from −0.226 to 0.024–0.070. Relative to RS–MoE, RS–MoE–Mem further improves high–flow NSE by 0.046, reduces high–flow RMSE by ∼0.002, and increases high–flow KGE by 0.039 (all paired differences p < 0.001). Across the three expert families, memory enhancement also reduces peak absolute bias by 0.67–1.21 percentage points and event-volume absolute bias by 1.05–2.10 percentage points. These results extend prior hydrological MoE applications. Attribution analysis and gating-frequency heatmaps reveal that RS-MoE gains tend to be larger in basins with strong streamflow variability, pronounced event-pulse behavior, and sufficient room for improvement, while the routing pattern remains stable and regime-consistent. These results support the transferability and configuration robustness of RS-MoE across regions and expert families.

title: Streamflow prediction in natural ungauged catchments using Temporal Fusion Transformers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Rafael Francisco, José Pedro Matos
abstract: Streamflow prediction is essential for water resources management. Classical hydrological models struggle with predictive accuracy and probabilistic representation in ungauged catchments. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated notable improvements in reproducing complex time series, such as streamflow, with the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) emerging as a promising model. This study explores the potential of TFTs to predict daily streamflow in natural ungauged catchments in Portugal. Streamflow data from 53 catchments were collected from the national database, while meteorological inputs (precipitation and temperature) were derived from the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset. Geomorphological descriptors for each catchment were also included. Results are reported on 46 catchments after screening from the initial set based on objective hydrometric and natural-flow criteria and show strong predictive performance and spatial generalization under ungauged conditions. In the test subsets, TFT models in ungauged conditions outperformed the individually calibrated hydrological model Hydrologiska Byråns Vattenbalansavdelning (HBV), securing an advantage in terms of median NSE (increased from 0.46 to 0.50), median KGE (increased from 0.44 to 0.48) and median CRPS (decreased, which is desired, from 5.51 to 3.70 L s − 1 km − 2 ). Model specialization substantially improved performance, reaching a median NSE = 0.62, a median KGE = 0.65, and the median CRPS decreased to 3.20 L s − 1 km − 2 , in selected test portions for this second task. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were also evaluated as a data-driven benchmark, with TFTs achieving competitive performance under ungauged conditions. Additionally, retraining experiments highlight the model’s adaptability, showing that local data, even if limited in number, can be instrumental in further improving predictions. These findings support the application of deep learning in operational settings, such as flood and drought risk management, and water allocation strategies in catchments without comprehensive measurements.

title: A recursive conditional generative adversarial network for multiphase flow prediction in anisotropic porous media under dynamic constraints
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Tianyu Yang, Xiang Rao, Kang Wang, Shuhui Xu, Wentao Zhan, Zhong Chen
abstract: Permeability anisotropy and time-varying well controls govern oil-saturation evolution during waterflooding, but repeated high-fidelity simulation is computationally expensive. We propose a recurrent conditional generative adversarial network (R-CGAN) for rapid spatiotemporal prediction of oil-saturation fields under anisotropic permeability and dynamic injection-production controls. A permeability-guided feature-adaptation mechanism captures directional flow behavior, while spatial encodings of well locations, types, and time-varying rates drive recurrent state transitions together with the current reservoir state. Conditional temporal discrimination improves the spatial plausibility and temporal consistency of multistep predictions. A continuous-time refinement module combining continuous-time encoding with feature-wise linear modulation reconstructs intermediate states within each control period. Under an identical recurrent protocol, R-CGAN outperformed four baseline architectures, including the Fourier neural operator (FNO). Relative to FNO, the strongest baseline, it reduced mean absolute error and root mean square error by 9.5% and 9.1%, respectively. Over a 240-day recurrent forecast, structural similarity declined only from 0.9821 to 0.9781. At unsupervised within-period times, continuous-time refinement reduced mean absolute error and root mean square error by 31.8% and 35.4%, respectively, compared with linear interpolation. The model remained accurate for unseen anisotropy strengths, well configurations, well counts, and forecast horizons, and achieved an approximately 223.4-fold online inference speedup relative to finite-volume simulation. These results demonstrate an accurate and efficient surrogate for continuous-time reservoir-state prediction, supporting repeated-evaluation tasks such as history matching and production optimization.

title: Long-horizon cascade reservoir scheduling with a multiscale constraint-consistent hybrid transformer
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Changqing Meng, Chunzhe Wang, Yanke Zhang, Yuankun Wang, Chao Wang, Guoyong Zhang, Yongqiang Wang
abstract: Long-horizon cascade reservoir scheduling is challenging because annual release trajectories must satisfy hydraulic consistency and operating constraints across strongly coupled reservoirs, while repeated deterministic optimization is computationally expensive. This study develops a Multiscale Constraint-Consistent Hybrid Transformer (MCC-HT), in which hydraulic consistency is embedded during trajectory generation and reservoir-level operating requirements are further reconciled through an Iterative Cumulative Rebalancing (ICR) mechanism. The framework was evaluated for the lower Jinsha River–Three Gorges six-reservoir cascade using a 64-year ten-day inflow record (1959–2022) under a deterministic hindcast setting, with comparisons against the Progressive Optimality Algorithm (POA), Particle Swarm Optimization, and two ablation variants. Over the 2015–2022 test period, MCC-HT generated annual schedules that remained consistent with the prescribed operating requirements, while reducing the average runtime for full annual schedule generation from 664.55 s for POA to 2.79 s. Under this substantial computational reduction, MCC-HT approximated the annual generation achieved by POA, with a mean difference of +0.12% that varied with hydrological conditions across individual years. Ablation results further indicate that embedded constraint handling contributes more consistently across hydrological conditions, whereas the benefit of multiscale inflow representation is more condition-dependent. These results show that structural embedding of physical constraints can support efficient and physically admissible long-horizon cascade scheduling, providing a practical basis for repeated annual scenario evaluation in strongly coupled hydro-systems.

title: INFO-LAX: an interpretable and uncertainty-aware framework for monthly rainfall erosivity estimation
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Jinhui Yuan, Yuefeng Lu, Zhengqi Song, Liguo Dong, Miao Lu, Weijun Zhao, Zhixiang Lu, Kun Liu
abstract: Rainfall erosivity (R factor) is a dynamic climatic driver of soil erosion, yet monthly estimation is complicated by nonlinear daily rainfall aggregation, strong upper tail behavior, and the limited interpretability and uncertainty characterization of many data driven models. We developed INFO-LAX as an integrated application framework combining two LSTM-Attention encoders, a low weight XGBoost correction branch, and the Weighted Mean of Vectors optimizer. Daily NOAA/NCEI observations from 25 stations across five climate geomorphic regions of China were converted to monthly predictors and daily data derived R factors. Only observed records were used and were partitioned chronologically into training (1975–2008), validation (2009–2014), testing (2015–2020), and temporal holdout (2021–2024) periods. On the independent test set, INFO-LAX achieved R2 = 0.8842, MAE = 95.837, and RMSE = 251.728 MJ·mm·ha−1·h−1, ranking first among RF, GPR, GAM, TFT, and TCN. End-to-end grouped Shapley analysis attributed 55.8% of model contribution to precipitation, followed by dew point (20.5%) and temperature (20.4%). The 95% prediction interval achieved PICP values of 0.952 and 0.978 on the test and temporal holdout sets, respectively. For test Q95 events, Tail MAE was 529.466 MJ·mm·ha−1·h−1 and recall was 0.843, although the peak magnitude ratio of 0.763 indicated conservative estimation of the largest events. INFO-LAX advances monthly R-factor estimation by integrating nonlinear daily-to-monthly representation, model-wide attribution, upper-tail evaluation, and calibrated uncertainty, supporting reconstruction, gap filling, risk assessment, near-real-time updating, and meteorological forcing for future soil erosion digital twins.

title: Interpretable soil moisture drought forecasting using graph attention networks
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Ye Tuo, Moritz Wirthensohn, Hongliang Ma, Francesco Avanzi
abstract: Accurate and interpretable soil moisture drought forecasting supports hydrological management. Capturing spatial and seasonal drought variability while interpreting learned dependencies remains challenging for data-driven models. This study assesses a domain-informed Graph Attention Network (GAT) to forecast soil moisture drought one-week-ahead by representing hydrological response units (HRUs) as a graph. A retrospective ensemble-based benchmark using 200 independently trained models evaluates predictive performance, spatiotemporal drought-pattern reproduction, and interpretability through feature importance and attention analyses. GAT achieves high F1 scores and a modest but spatially coherent improvement over an LSTM baseline, with the largest gains at lower elevations and reduced performance for both models in high-elevation headwaters. In full-record diagnostics, GAT better reproduces observed drought patterns, particularly in summer, with closer agreement in basin-wide drought frequency and reduced bias. Permutation-based feature importance identifies evaporative-demand variables and topographic features as important predictors with distinct spatial and temporal roles. Attention analyses show that HRU-graph connectivity shapes the dominant spatial attention pattern, while attention weights locally and seasonally reweight connected-source contributions in ways consistent with elevation-dependent input dynamics. A complementary assessment combines chronological train-validation-test separation with different soil moisture input configurations. GAT achieves highest F1 scores among the learned models, and soil moisture benefits the graph models more strongly than LSTM. However, none exceeds persistence in basin-level F1 during the withheld test period. These findings support GAT’s diagnostic value for examining reproducible spatiotemporal patterns in model behavior alongside predictive performance, while operational application requires further development and evaluation against persistence.

title: Improving hydrologic prediction and interpretability through physics-informed dual-output LSTM with water and energy balance constraints
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Gopeshwar Sahu, Ashutosh Sharma
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has demonstrated strong predictive skill in hydrological modelling, but often lacks physical consistency and interpretability. The Mass-conserving LSTM (MC-LSTM) overcomes this limitation by enforcing water balance, yet the existing formulations remain restricted to single-variable prediction and simplified representation of hydrological fluxes. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Dual-Output LSTM (PIDuaL) that simultaneously predicts streamflow and evapotranspiration (ET) through a modified mass-balance structure. Three constrained variants are further developed by enforcing water balance, energy balance, and combined water and energy balance within the PIDuaL framework. For fair benchmark comparison, a purely data-driven Dual-LSTM is also implemented. Across 149 human-influenced watersheds in India, LSTM and Dual-LSTM show lower streamflow skill, with a median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.58, whereas MC-LSTM and PIDuaL improve performance to a median NSE of 0.67. Performance gains are most pronounced in hydrologically challenging conditions, including semi-arid and highly human-influenced watersheds, where purely data-driven models struggle. PIDuaL substantially reduces bias, and its constrained variants exhibit the largest improvement in low-flow simulation, accompanied by stronger correlation with baseflow-governing attributes, indicating physically meaningful recession dynamics. Although ET performance is slightly reduced relative to the purely data-driven Dual-LSTM, all physics-informed models maintain satisfactory skill, with median NSE values of at least 0.69 and correlation coefficients of 0.89 or higher. Importantly, PIDuaL internal states exhibit strong correspondence with independent soil moisture and GRACE-based storage anomalies, demonstrating enhanced interpretability. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed physics-informed dual-output framework improves predictive accuracy under hydrologically challenging conditions while enhancing physical consistency and model interpretability.

title: Scale-dependent phosphorus export across rainfall gradients: Hydrological dynamics and storm-event responses
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xinyu Liu, Quan Liu, Tao Wang, Minghua Zhou, Bo Zhu
abstract: Effective control of watershed non-point source phosphorus (P) pollution is often hindered by a lack of understanding of episodic, high-magnitude export events. Specifically, the critical rainfall thresholds triggering these events and their modulation by catchment scale remain unclear. Here, this study investigated P export dynamics across four nested catchments (3.2–1236.4 ha) in the Sichuan Basin of China, employing high-frequency automated sampling across a rainfall gradient. Results identified a critical rainfall threshold of approximately 30 mm. Below this threshold, TP export remained low, with a higher relative contribution of dissolved total P (DTP) during moderate events. Above the threshold, P loads increased sharply and PP was the dominant exported fraction. At Wan’an (WA), the largest catchment, four monitored events contributed 51.1 % and 59.2 % of annual composite TP and PP loads, respectively. PP accounted for 95.6 % of TP at WA during the largest event. This threshold response was strongly scale-dependent, with small headwater catchments exhibiting source-limited, flashy responses (first flush), whereas larger catchments showed buffered hydrographs attributed to network attenuation. Furthermore, PO4-P/DTP ratios were higher in the larger catchments than in SR, indicating scale-dependent differences in dissolved P speciation. These findings suggest a paradigm shift in management strategies away from static annual load reduction towards targeted controls in critical source areas during high-risk storm events identified by specific rainfall thresholds.

title: Internal phosphorus loading control in eutrophic lakes: A meta-analysis comparing remediation strategies across technology categories
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Ruili Xie, Manqi Chang, Qiushi Shen, Yanjin Gao, Yunpeng Zhao, Yasong Chen
abstract: Internal phosphorus loading from lake sediments sustains eutrophication for decades after external nutrient inputs are reduced. While numerous control technologies have been developed, their relative effectiveness has not been systematically quantified across technology categories. This study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of six major internal phosphorus loading control strategies, integrating 613 effect sizes from 120 peer-reviewed studies (155 eligible). Effect sizes were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was explored through subgroup analyses and meta-regression. The overall pooled log response ratio (lnRR) was − 1.25, corresponding to a mean phosphorus reduction of approximately 71%. In-situ capping achieved the highest mean effect size (lnRR = − 1.81), yet this estimate was based on only 2 studies. Chemical inactivation, supported by the largest body of evidence (226 effect sizes), achieved a mean lnRR of − 1.35 (∼74% reduction), followed by aeration and oxygenation (−1.29; ∼72%), combined measures (−1.11; ∼67%), submerged macrophyte restoration (−0.83; ∼57%), and dredging (−0.62; ∼46%). Among combined strategies, chemical inactivation paired with macrophyte restoration was the most extensively studied and achieved peak flux reductions exceeding 99% under optimized conditions. Treatment effectiveness varied 1.4-fold across measurement metrics, with overlying water soluble reactive phosphorus showing the strongest response. Meta-regression identified pH, dissolved oxygen, water depth, and sediment Al:P stoichiometry as significant moderators. Laboratory studies overestimated field performance by approximately 13 percentage points. High heterogeneity (I2 = 89.2%) reflected the diversity of technologies and environmental settings, and funnel plot analysis indicated minor publication bias. These findings provide the first cross-category quantitative comparison of internal phosphorus loading control technologies and support a two-phase staged remediation framework integrating chemical stabilization with ecological restoration.

title: Enhancing water quality in dead-end zones of distribution networks using spoilers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Kunyi Li, Jinliang Gao, Wenyan Wu, Yuan Tian, Shihua Qi, Jingyang Yu, Jianxun Chen, Yanchen Ding

title: High and variable nitrous oxide emissions from human-impacted lentic freshwaters
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Mingliang Jiang, Qitao Xiao, Lei Hong, Yuhang Liu, Xingyu Jiang, Cheng Hu, Ligang Xu
abstract: Inland waters are important but poorly constrained sources of atmospheric nitrous oxide (N2O). Lentic freshwaters including lakes and reservoirs represent key components of inland waters and serve as critical hotspots for nitrogen cycle, yet how anthropogenic disturbances drive their N2O dynamic variability remains unclear. To address this knowledge gap, systematic field measurements in three lakes and one reservoir in China’s eastern plain with intensive anthropogenic activity were conducted to characterize the dynamic variability of N2O emissions and disentangle the key environmental drivers. Results found dissolved N2O concentrations showed uniform vertical distribution but distinct seasonal and spatial variability. These water bodies acted as significant and variable N2O emissions sources, with the emissions flux ranging from 0.25 to 69.27 µmol m−2 d-1 (mean value 7.98 ± 9.12 µmol m−2 d-1). The N2O emissions exhibited strong seasonality, peaking (hot moments) in warm seasons (spring and summer), and N2O emissions of warm seasons were 3.8 times those in cold seasons (autumn and winter). Hot moments of N2O emissions were likely linked to temperature and precipitation-derived hydrological regimes. Inflow-affected zones were hot spots of N2O emissions, with emissions about twice those of pelagic zones (12.47 versus 5.76 µmol m−2 d-1). While regulating factors differed among water bodies and zones, anthropogenic-derived nutrient loadings and associated environment change substantially promoted N2O production and emissions, particularly in inflow-affected zones. Our findings likely deepen insights into N2O biogeochemistry in lentic freshwaters under anthropogenic disturbances and underscore the need to account for waterbody heterogeneity in aquatic N2O emissions estimate.

title: Effects of droughts and warm months on phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations in surface waters globally
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Duncan J. Graham, Arthur H.W. Beusen, Marc F.P. Bierkens, Michelle T.H. van Vliet
abstract: Phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N) concentrations in surface waters are substantially affected by droughts and warm months. However, previous studies of phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations under these hydro-climatic extremes are limited to a small number of regions, mainly in parts of North America, Europe and Australia. Here we perform the first global-scale analysis of phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations in surface waters under droughts, warm months and compound drought-warm months for the period 1980–2010. To achieve this, we developed an approach to downscale existing simulation data of total phosphorus (TP) and total nitrogen (TN) concentrations from annual to monthly level with machine learning at 0.5 × 0.5 degree resolution. The results indicate generally mixed responses in phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations under drought, with some regions showing increases in the concentrations of phosphorus and nitrogen due to drought and others showing decreases. Additionally, the results show more consistent increases in phosphorus (P) concentrations during warm months (average change: +21%) and compound drought-warm months (average change: +10%), which was mainly attributed to less dilution during periods of low flow and high temperature. Furthermore, there is a general decrease in the N:P ratio observed globally during warm months (average change: −11%). The results from this study provide a broader understanding of the effects of droughts and warm months on phosphorus and nitrogen in surface waters compared to previous local-scale studies. Furthermore, the results highlight the significant changes in phosphorus and nitrogen ratios during droughts and warm months, which may significantly influence freshwater ecosystem health worldwide.

title: Enhancing lake dissolved oxygen retrieval by integrating process-based model with machine learning: maximizing the utility of multi-source monitoring data
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xuemei Pan, Qixin Lin, Gang Li, Xinfa Xu, Zhangjun Liu, Jingqiao Mao
abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is critical for lake ecosystem health. Although satellite remote sensing (RS) coupled with machine learning (ML) has emerged as an effective approach for DO monitoring, the stringent requirement for temporal synchronization between in-situ measurements and satellite overpasses often limits the availability of viable training samples. This scarcity significantly constrains both the retrieval accuracy and the generalizability of ML models. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel framework integrating a Process-Based (PB) model with ML algorithms for lake DO retrieval. Within this framework, the PB model assimilates multi-source data of diverse types and varying frequencies to generate high-frequency simulated DO. These simulations serve as substitutes for in-situ measurements to augment “DO–surface reflectance” training pairs, thereby promoting the utilization of ground monitoring data and RS imagery to enhance ML model training. Taking Poyang Lake as a case study, we constructed ML training datasets by pairing RS surface reflectance with three distinct DO data configurations: in-situ measurements only, PB-simulated DO data only, and a hybrid of both. The retrieval performance of six ML algorithms was evaluated across these configurations using rigorous spatial and temporal cross-validation comprising 72 independent scenarios. Results indicate that the PB model achieves high-frequency DO simulations with satisfactory accuracy, with R2 ranging from 0.63 to 0.92 across seven stations. Furthermore, augmenting training samples with PB-simulated data significantly improved the retrieval performance across all ML models. Under the hybrid training sets configuration, the six ML models achieving a mean R2 of 0.40 across 21 spatial cross-validation scenarios and 0.52 across 3 temporal cross-validation scenarios, significantly outperforming traditional methods relying solely on limited in-situ measurements (mean R2 of 0.26 and 0.17, respectively). The proposed framework effectively fuses multi-source heterogeneous monitoring data and maximizes historical RS imagery usage, providing a novel technical pathway for high-precision water quality retrieval in inland lakes, especially under data-scarce conditions.

title: Decoupled ammonia nitrogen and total nitrogen exports under hydroclimatic variability in an alpine headwater catchment of the central Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xueping Wang, Xiaolin Shui, Yujie Zhang, Xiaohong Zhao, Zhoufeng Wang, Bo Hu, Haixia Zhu
abstract: As the “Asian Water Tower” with a fragile alpine ecosystem, nitrogen loading in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is critical to the water security of the downstream Yangtze River. This study elucidated the spatiotemporal dynamics and potential factors of nitrogen export in the Tongtian River through long-term monitoring (2015–2024) and seasonal sampling, coupled with Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) analysis. The results revealed a distinct temporal decoupling between ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) and total nitrogen (TN). TN concentration and flux exhibited a persistent upward trend (p 0.05), whereas its flux exhibited a significant upward trend (p < 0.01), a signal captured only after controlling for intra-annual variability. TN concentrations were highest in the spring campaign (1.71 mg/L), while the NH3-N campaign mean was highest in summer (0.26 mg/L) and close to the autumn and winter means. OPGD identified cropland as the factor with the highest explanatory power for NH3-N concentration (q = 0.54) and pH as the primary explanatory factor for TN concentration (q = 0.53). Suspended sediment concentration had the highest explanatory power for NH3-N flux (q = 0.56), whereas TN flux was predominantly associated with pH and suspended sediment concentration (q = 0.74 and 0.71, p < 0.001). Interaction analysis further indicated joint associations of land-use, hydro-meteorological, and suspended sediment variables with temporal variability in nitrogen export. The contrasting nitrogen patterns may reflect differences in catchment inputs, hydrological transport, and temperature-dependent transformations. Therefore, management strategies must shift from passive concentration monitoring to actively decoupling anthropogenic practice from peak hydro-sedimentary windows.

title: Irrigation water abstraction as a hidden amplifier of river pollution: observation-based empirical evidence from a dual-river system in central China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Guoshuai Zhang, Peng Zhang, Min Xu, Yanxue Xu, Yue Zhao
abstract: Irrigation abstraction reduces dilution capacity for loads entering below an offtake. In China’s Yiluo River Basin, we quantified this loss using the Amplification Factor (AF), the ratio of no-diversion to residual discharge, computed from measured river and diversion discharges without hydrological modeling. AF equals a concentration ratio only for a fixed load entering below the offtake and not removed by diversion; it does not by itself estimate actual concentration change. Irrigation-season AF averaged 2.33 (Yi River) and 2.53 (Luo River), with single-day maxima of 12.6 and 11.9. Concentration responses were assessed using evidence not algebraically derived from AF. On irrigation-season dry days, the NH3-N coefficient was positive under all seven seasonal specifications (temperature-adjusted primary model: β = +0.115 per unit log(Qdiv + 1), p = 0.016) but weakened under calendar-based controls (p = 0.06–0.21), so we regard it as supportive rather than confirmatory evidence; residual seasonal confounding cannot be excluded. Absolute specific conductance was positively associated with abstraction (p = 0.0024–0.0042), whereas the downstream/upstream ratio was not significant (p = 0.119); these results are consistent with dilution-capacity loss but do not independently validate the mechanism. The Yi River, with concentrated abstraction, is least affected by known return-flow pathways; the Luo River is a composite multi-diversion system. Assumed gauging errors yielded AF uncertainty of ±11–12%, excluding structural and scenario uncertainty. Lagging diversion discharge by 1–3 days changed irrigation-season mean AF by less than 3%, whereas daily AF differed by more than 10% on 12–39% of days.

title: Phosphorus composition in urban estuarine sediments: similar spatial patterns, distinct seasonal drivers, transformation pathways and risks
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Zhaoying Chen, Zhaokui Ni, Shuaishuai Zhou, Taotao Sun, Yue Wu, Yu Ma, Jixin Yang, Shuai Liu, Andrea Critto, Shengrui Wang
abstract: Estuaries are global biogeochemical hotspots threatened by phosphorus (P)-driven eutrophication. Although sediments serve as major P reservoirs, its molecular composition, influencing factors, transformation pathways, and environmental risks remain poorly understood. This study analyzed these aspects in the Shenzhen Estuary using 31P NMR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, EEM fluorescence, and microbial high-throughput sequencing. Results showed a consistent river-to-bay gradient, with the content of total P (TP), inorganic P (IP), Ortho–P, Mono–P (myo–IHP, scyllo–IHP, α–Gly, RNA–nmp), and Di–P (DNA–P) decreasing seaward, while the proportion of organic P (OP, 17.6 ± 7.3%) increased in both dry and wet periods. Despite similar spatial patterns, influencing factors, transformation pathways, and environmental risks differed markedly between seasons. Dry-period P components were primarily associated with microbial communities and organic matter (OM) properties, whereas wet-period patterns were closely related to OM properties and sources, as well as to microbial α-diversity. Spatially P transformation pathways were identified: river sediments favored OP mineralization (Mono–P/Di–P → Ortho–P), while bay sediments showed net assimilation (Ortho–P → Mono–P/Di–P) in the dry period; Ortho–P was converted to OP via biological uptake in the wet period. We developed a novel Phosphorus Environmental Risk Index (PERI) integrating P components and biotic/abiotic influencing factors. PERI values were significantly higher in river zones than bay regardless of season, and consistently higher in the wet period. These findings establish a framework for understanding sediment P dynamics and provide a risk–assessment tool for P management in estuaries.

title: Biogeochemical controls on N 2 O emission factors across a river-estuary continuum: nonlinear nitrate dependence and an underrecognized role of phosphorus
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Sibo Zhang, Lei Gu, Xinxiao Wu, Xiaokang Li, Chunming Li, Jie Zhang, Zhihao Xu, William H. McDowell, Xinghui Xia
abstract: The IPCC framework assigns the same default emission factor of 0.26% to the riverine and estuarine components of indirect N2O emissions, despite substantial biogeochemical variability within these aquatic systems. We examined EF5 along the Pearl River-estuary continuum during three seasonal sampling campaigns and evaluated its environmental predictors using machine learning, supplemented by winter N2O isotopocule and metagenomic analyses. Winter isotopocule-based estimates indicated that denitrification-related processes accounted for > 89% of N2O production. EF5, defined as the dissolved N2O-N:NO3 –-N concentration ratio, ranged from 0.02% to 0.38% (median 0.06%), and nitrate emerged as its leading predictor. EF5 declined sharply with increasing nitrate at low concentrations but more gradually at higher concentrations. At higher nitrate concentrations, increasing N2O concentration evidently weakened the EF5 decline expected from denominator coupling alone. This concentration dependence helps explain the greater predictive contribution of nitrate in estuarine waters, where nitrate concentrations were lower. TP and TN:TP were also important EF5 predictors, with the TN:TP ratio exceeding the Redfield molar ratio of 16:1 in 99.1% of observations. Higher TP was associated with lower predicted EF5 and positively correlated with the relative abundances of genes involved not only in denitrification but also in nitrate assimilation and DNRA, suggesting greater potential for nitrate utilization through pathways that do not directly produce N2O. The positive TN:TP-EF5 relationship in riverine waters may partly reflect wastewater-related N:P imbalance and dissolved N2O inputs. A global compilation comprising 3,560 riverine and 254 estuarine observations revealed broadly comparable median EF5 values (0.08% and 0.11%, respectively) between these two systems, both below the IPCC default, but river-estuary contrasts varied with latitude. These findings support EF5 parameterizations incorporating nitrate concentration dependence and phosphorus-related nutrient conditions.

title: From pollution-driven to process-regulated: A decade of ecological restoration reshapes CO 2 fluxes in a heavily polluted urban stream
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Yingxue Pu, Xiaofeng Wang, Yuewei Zhang, Yixin He, Tingting Liu, Shuangshuang Liu, Jilong Wang, Honglin Chen, Yuan Zeng, Zuolin Xiao
abstract: Heavily polluted rivers are significant hotspots of CO2 emissions, yet how long-term ecological restoration alters these emissions and their biogeochemical drivers remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a decade-long field investigation of CO2 concentrations and fluxes in a heavily polluted urban stream in Chongqing, China, spanning successive restoration periods: baseline polluted stage (2014), point-source wastewater interception stage (2018) and ecological restoration stage (2023). Integrating hydrochemical monitoring, machine-learning modeling, and a normalized mitigation-efficiency framework, we evaluated CO2 flux dynamics and underlying control mechanism shifts throughout long-term eco-restoration. Over the ten-year restoration period, dissolved CO2 concentrations and fluxes decreased by 76.0% and 72.4%, respectively, demonstrating substantial climate co-benefits alongside water-quality restoration. This reduction was primarily driven by substantial decreases in organic carbon and nutrient loads alongside improved dissolved oxygen and pH. Crucially, CO2 fluxes in this urban stream shifted from being driven by excessive organic carbon supply (carbon-overloaded regime in 2014) to pH and nitrogen constraints after wastewater interception (2018), and ultimately to phosphorus limitation and oxygen regulation following ecological restoration (2023). This result highlights that controlling mechanisms of urban stream CO2 emissions exhibit clear stage-dependent and shift from carbon-saturated, heterotrophic regime to nutrient-limited internal metabolism. Normalized mitigation-efficiency analyses further revealed that reductions in organic carbon and nitrogen yielded higher CO2 mitigation benefits per unit pollutant removed than phosphorus reduction. Although residual CO2 emissions remain higher than those in less disturbed rivers due to legacy effects from historical pollution, these findings demonstrate that restoration not only suppresses urban river CO2 emissions but also fundamentally restructures their biogeochemical controls from substrate-driven to process-regulated systems, providing a scientific basis for optimizing co-benefits of water quality and climate mitigation.

title: Molecular compositions and hydrological features govern dissolved organic phosphorus transport and transformation in rivers across different climate zones
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Peipei Zhang, Qibiao Yu, Fenfang Wang, Jianing Wang, Dongsheng Wang, Weijin Yan, Dingjiang Chen
abstract: Dissolved organic phosphorus (DOP) is a potentially bioavailable component of riverine phosphorus export, yet the molecular controls on its uptake and their coupling with hydrological transport remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrated Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry, incubations, and nutrient-spiraling metrics across heterogeneous rivers and estuaries spanning five river basins of eastern China. DOP accounted for 5.79–86.6% (mean: 31.6% ± 13.2%) of total phosphorus, with concentrations and molecular composition varying with river size and land use. DOP concentrations decreased from headwater streams to mainstems and rose with agricultural and urban land proportions; forest rivers were relatively enriched in highly unsaturated compounds, whereas agricultural and urban rivers were enriched in labile peptides and CHOP-class compounds. We developed a molecular lability index (LI-DOP) integrating H/C, O/C, and molecular mass. LI-DOP explained 60% of the observed variation in uptake velocity (Vf, 0.19–0.79 m d-1) and was retained in the optimal model of riverine turnover rate (k, 0.02–0.28 d-1) together with discharge and DOP concentration. These quantitative relationships indicate that DOP processing reflects molecular composition in conjunction with hydrological and chemical conditions and cannot be adequately characterized by DOP concentration alone. Moreover, DOP conversion potentially contributed 9.61–40.2% (20.9 ± 8.26%) of dissolved inorganic phosphorus at river scales. These estimates suggest in-river DOP conversion may constitute an important internal source of bioavailable phosphorus, while DOP escaping conversion may be exported downstream and support phosphorus availability in estuaries. These findings support incorporating DOP molecular composition and transformation into river-estuary phosphorus assessments.

title: Groundwater-lake interactions in a high-altitude terminal lake: uncertainty, hydrogeological constraint and climate change
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Joaquín Aravena, Francisca Aguirre-Correa, Alberto de la Fuente, Carolina V. Giraldo, Amanda Peña-Echeverría, Pedro Bonacic-Vera, Sarah Leray, Francisco Suárez
abstract: In endorheic basins of the Andean Plateau, shallow lakes are influenced by groundwater-surface water exchange, which regulates water availability in these fragile terminal wetland ecosystems. However, quantifying lakebed exchange ( Q lb ) remains challenging because of difficult access, limited data availability and uncertainty in the dominant water-balance terms. Here, we evaluate groundwater-lake interactions in the terminal lake of the pristine Salar del Huasco basin by reconstructing the long-term monthly lake water balance for 1987–2019 using multiple data sources for precipitation, evaporation, spring inflow, lake area, and bathymetry. This approach generated 600 plausible realizations of Q lb , which was inferred as the residual required to close the monthly water balance. After applying a hydrogeological consistency constraint based on piezometric observations, 222 realizations were selected and the median Q lb ensemble was 21 l/s, indicating a tendency toward groundwater inflow to the lake. Sensitivity analyses across alternative piezometric-classification and the hydrogeological consistency filter thresholds retained a positive ensemble median, while the estimated magnitude remained threshold-dependent. Across the ensemble, evaporation and spring inflow were the dominant sources of uncertainty, whereas precipitation, lake-area detection, and bathymetry played secondary roles. The hydrogeologically plausible subset was then used to train a probabilistic Quantile Regression Forest model forced with bias-corrected CMIP6 projections. Future simulations under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 indicate progressive weakening of net groundwater inflow and a transition toward near-neutral or intermittently lake-to-aquifer exchange under SSP5-8.5, and a reduction in lake area by 20–40% at the end of the century. Sensitivity experiments further show that projected lake persistence is strongly conditional on spring-flow persistence and on whether future predictor states remain within the historical QRF training domain. Overall, this study provides a framework for evaluating groundwater-lake interactions and the hydrological vulnerability of remote high-altitude wetlands while explicitly accounting for uncertainty.

title: Fate and retention mechanisms of nitrate across the vadose–saturated continuum in a typical agricultural irrigation area of the North China Plain: evidence from hydrogeochemistry and microbiome analyses
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Gongyu Zhou, Kehan Yuan, Chengyi Zu, Ruihua Shang, Xiaoyang Liu, Liuzhu Chen, Lili Liang, Teng Ma
abstract: Thick vadose zones are widely regarded as buffers against agricultural nitrate leaching, yet nitrate-enriched groundwater remains common beneath intensively irrigated regions. Sediment retention can delay nitrate migration, whereas effective attenuation largely depends on microbially mediated transformation and the electron-donor conditions required to sustain it. How these coupled processes govern nitrate fate across the vadose–saturated continuum remains poorly understood. We integrated groundwater hydrochemistry, multi-borehole sediment profiles, 16S rRNA and metagenomic analyses, and a laboratory sediment incubation experiment at a representative site in the North China Plain. Groundwater nitrate enrichment co-occurred with strongly heterogeneous sediment nitrate pools, with generally higher KCl-extractable than water-extractable concentrations, showing that deep storage did not provide uniform protection of the aquifer. Microbial community composition varied among samples, while the LC02 metagenomic gene catalog contained nitrate-reduction and DNRA-related genes together with components spanning all four denitrification steps at all four sampled depths. The summed abundance of non-overlapping nitrogen-cycle categories reached 8.70% of total metagenomic gene abundance at 50.1 m, where nirK, nirS, norB, norC, and nosZ reached their highest abundances among the four sampled depths. Laboratory sediment incubations showed carbon-source-dependent nitrate removal and nitrite accumulation, consistent with differences in the balance between nitrate reduction and subsequent nitrite consumption. Together, these findings suggest that nitrate persistence across the thick vadose–saturated continuum reflects the coupling of heterogeneous deep storage, hydrological transport, and spatially distributed microbial transformation potential. This integrated mechanism helps explain the coexistence of persistent nitrate enrichment and a substantial nitrogen-cycling gene reservoir and provides scientific evidence for groundwater vulnerability assessment in intensively irrigated agricultural regions.

title: A structure-constrained inverse distance weighting framework for stochastic simulation of multi-lithofacies sedimentary aquifer architecture
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Wanli Ren, Yue Fan, Heng Dai, Mohamad Reza Soltanian, Ming Ye, Zhenxue Dai
abstract: Characterizing multi-lithofacies aquifer architecture from sparse borehole data is essential for groundwater flow and solute transport modeling, yet remains challenging because categorical lithofacies fields must honor hard conditioning data while representing realistic proportions, anisotropic continuity, and connectivity. Conventional inverse distance weighting (IDW) is transparent and computationally efficient but primarily produces a single deterministic estimate and does not provide stochastic categorical realizations or categorical uncertainty. This study develops a bias-corrected inverse distance weighting (BIDW) framework for conditional stochastic simulation of heterogeneous aquifer architecture. At each unsimulated cell, anisotropic IDW support is used to construct a local categorical sampling distribution, from which lithofacies are sampled sequentially to generate borehole-conditioned stochastic skeletons. Subsequent structural organization and refinement uses lithofacies proportions and directional mean lengths as soft constraints, with tunable structural-reinforcement settings. Based on a three-lithofacies 3D synthetic aquifer benchmark, the staged workflow progressively improved grid scale agreement, with mean overall accuracy increasing from 0.668 to 0.716. The high-proportion background lithofacies was reproduced with a largest connected component fraction of 0.999 and directional mean lengths close to those of the reference model. For the low-proportion lithofacies, the number of connected components decreased from 423.4 to 18.4, close to the reference value of 16, while the largest connected component fraction increased from 0.401 to 0.747. These results demonstrate that BIDW effectively extends IDW from deterministic interpolation to stochastic structural simulation, providing a transparent, data-efficient, and geologically constrained alternative for borehole-based aquifer architecture modeling.

title: N 2 O production pathways along a subtropical river headwater to confluence continuum: synergistic regulation by NH 4 + supply and redox conditions
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Yuesheng Xiao, Bin Ma, Zhiping Yuan, Yizhen Wang, Wenchang Wei, Hong Niu
abstract: Rivers are an important source of atmospheric N2O. However, the synergistic regulation of N2O production pathways along the river continuum by nitrogen supply, redox conditions, and hydrological characteristics remains poorly understood. Surface water samples were collected in summer (n = 27) and winter (n = 33) along a subtropical river continuum from headwaters to its confluence with the Yangtze River, with an elevation difference > 1500 m. Water chemistry, stable water isotopes (δ2H, δ18O), nitrate nitrogen and oxygen isotopes (δ15N-NO3 −, δ18O-NO3 −), ammonium nitrogen isotopes (δ15N-NH4 +), and N2O isotopomers (δ18O-N2O, SP) were analyzed. Results showed that N2O concentrations were higher in summer than in winter and higher in the downstream agricultural plain than in mountainous and transitional reaches. Low NO3 − supply limited the overall intensity of NO3 −-based denitrification in river water. NH4 + source type and supply, together with DOC-DO-regulated redox microenvironments, jointly controlled N2O production in river water. In summer, higher exogenous NH4 + and DOC inputs and lower DO in the plain area promoted N2O production and accumulation. An SP-δ18O-N2O mixing model indicated that nitrification dominated basin-wide N2O production, contributing 55.34%–69.74% after correction for N2O reduction, while the denitrification contribution increased progressively from the mountainous headwaters to the downstream plain. These findings reveal that longitudinal shifts in nitrogen substrate supply and DOC-DO redox conditions from the headwaters to the confluence jointly shaped a N2O production pattern dominated by nitrification but with increasing denitrification downstream, providing new insights for N2O assessment in subtropical agricultural rivers.

title: A data-space inversion framework for uncertainty-informed monitoring network design in a regional coupled SWAT–MODFLOW model
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Nasrin Badrzadeh, Patrick Ray, Mohamad Reza Soltanian
abstract: Groundwater head is a key indicator of aquifer storage and surface water–groundwater interactions in managed watersheds. However, its prediction remains uncertain because hydraulic properties are spatially heterogeneous, hydrogeologic data are limited, and groundwater responses reflect coupled processes. Reducing this uncertainty requires identifying the most informative observations; however, streamflow and groundwater-head observations constrain different aspects of coupled systems, and their relative worth is less commonly quantified in regional models. Data-worth (DW) analysis provides this quantification, but its application to computationally demanding coupled models remains limited. Accordingly, this study asks which existing and prospective observations most effectively reduce groundwater-head predictive uncertainty in a heterogeneous river–aquifer system, and which parameter uncertainties control the remaining predictive uncertainty. We apply a data-space inversion (DSI)-based DW framework using an ensemble of coupled SWAT–MODFLOW simulations for the Great Miami River Watershed. Regional hydrogeologic information informed the conceptualization of aquifer geometry and lateral hydraulic-property contrasts, which were implemented in a single convertible groundwater model layer. Topographic, soil, land-use, climate, and groundwater-withdrawal data supported construction of the coupled model. DSI uses ensemble-derived observation–prediction relationships, allowing monitoring scenarios to be evaluated without rerunning or reconditioning the coupled model.
