description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yawen Yuan, Jiawei Cheng, Zihao Li, Yuhe He, Kenneth M.Y. Leung, Yunsong Mu, John P. Giesy
abstract: Fluorinated liquid crystal monomers (FLCMs) constitute the largest and most widely used subgroup of liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), accounting for more than half of known LCMs. They are important components of high-performance liquid crystal mixtures used in displays because of their excellent dielectric anisotropy, low viscosity, and thermal stability. With the large-scale production, use, and disposal of liquid crystal displays, FLCMs are continuously released into the environment and have been widely detected in air, dust, water, sediments, wastewater, biota, and human samples. Compared with non-FLCMs, FLCMs generally exhibit stronger environmental persistence, higher bioaccumulation potential, and greater ecological and health risks, and therefore represent potential emerging contaminants. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on the sources, environmental occurrence and fate, transformation, bioaccumulation, exposure, and toxicity of FLCMs, and compares their PBT characteristics with those of non-FLCMs to assess the relative priority of FLCMs and non-FLCMs as two groups. Overall, FLCMs show risk characteristics similar to persistent organic pollutants, but knowledge gaps remain regarding their environmental behavior, transformation-product toxicity, actual exposure hazards, and life-cycle risk assessment. Future studies should strengthen multimedia monitoring, mechanism-based toxicology, exposure assessment, and green molecular design to support risk identification, priority control, and sustainable management of FLCMs.

title: Quantitative analysis of geochemical boundaries for controlling mobile cadmium speciation in soil of high geological background regions
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kunling Zheng, Bingtao Li, Yinxian Song, Tengjie Cui, Junfeng Ji, Zhongyao Chen, Godwin A. Ayoko
abstract: Accumulation and mobilization of cadmium (Cd) in high geological background regions threaten agricultural and ecological security, yet the dynamic evolution and quantitative thresholds of mobile Cd during weathering pedogenesis remain unclear. This study, for the first time, coupled the PROFILE with multi-surface model, together with machine learning, to conduct a comparative analysis of karst and black shale high geological background regions, with the Yangtze River Delta for comparison. Results show that Cd leaching risk is highly region specific: water-soluble Cd dominates black shale (46%) and non-high geological background regions (51%), whereas karst regions exhibit a stronger mineral bound buffering. Although the critical pH range governing Cd immobilization and mobilization generally falls within the classical geochemical range of 6.0–7.0, it varies with parent material and pedogenic processes. Critical dissolved organic carbon thresholds show a decreasing gradient of black shale (250–300 mg/kg) > karst (200–250 mg/kg) > non-high geological background (150–200 mg/kg), correlating positively with indigenous soil DOC levels to optimize organic fertilizer dosage. Weathering pedogenesis induces seasonal Cd “release and mineral re-immobilization” dynamics, and high temperature and precipitation in summer significantly enhance Cd leaching. This study provides a quantitative basis for differentiated Cd risk management in comparable high geological background regions.

title: Field-deployable ZnO/ZIF-67 heterostructure sensor: Enabling rapid, highly sensitive, and humidity-tolerant NO 2 detection
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Huimin Chen, Xiangyi Deng, Li Lv, Shuyan Cao, Liang Yin, Xiangqun Chu, Shicai Yan, Pinhua Zhang, Bin Liu
abstract: Real-time nitrogen dioxide (NO2) detection is critical for both environmental monitoring and ecological agriculture, but its practical deployment is still limited by low sensitivity, slow response speed and severe humidity interference. Herein, a porous p-n heterostructure based on ZnO/ZIF-67 was prepared via in-situ growth of ZnO on ZIF-67. Benefiting from the synergistic effect between the porous structure and the built-in heterogeneous interface, the as-prepared composite material delivers exceptional NO2 sensing performance. The optimized ZnO/ZIF-67 sensor exhibits a high response of 8.29 ( | I g / I a | ) to 10 ppm NO2 with fast response/recovery times of 5/6 s (25℃). The sensor also enables clear detection down to 200 ppb and maintains stable sensing performance over 35 days. Furthermore, it displays excellent humidity tolerance: as relative humidity increases from 45% to 85%, the sensing response toward 1 ppm NO2 only varies by 18.51%. To investigate the practical application performance of the sensor in real-world scenarios, a portable sensing platform was constructed for real-time NO2 monitoring in humid agricultural environments. Experiments verified that the sensor system can effectively detect nitrogen-derived gases in the soil. This work supplies a feasible material design methodology for low-power NO2 sensing and ecological agriculture monitoring application.

title: Engineered titanium-coated iron oxide nanocomposites alleviate nickel-induced phytotoxicity in maize through integrated physiological, ultrastructural, and transcriptomic protection
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Muhammad Rehman, Sajid Muhammad, Bahar Ali, Zulqarnain Haider, Abdul Salam, Yinbo Gan
abstract: Nickel (Ni) contamination of agricultural soils threatens crop productivity, food safety, and human health. Although individual nanomaterials have been explored to alleviate Ni stress, little is known about the integration of complementary oxides within a single core-shell platform, and the transcriptomic basis of such protection remains poorly understood. We engineered titanium-coated iron oxide core-shell nanocomposites (Ti@Fe3O4 NCs), combining the redox-modulating capacity of the Fe3O4 core with the ROS-scavenging properties of the Ti-based shell, and evaluated their foliar application against Ni toxicity in maize. Relative to Ni-stressed plants, NCs + Ni improved shoot length (36%), root length (54%), and biomass, reduced Ni accumulation, and restored shoot Ca (65%), P (45%), Mg (29%), and Zn (35%). NCs + Ni re-established redox homeostasis by lowering H2O2 (29%), O2•− (33%), and malondialdehyde (24%) and by increasing SOD (35%), POD (42%), CAT (42%), and APX (14%) activities. Transcriptome profiling showed that, instead of hyper-activating stress signaling, NCs + Ni buffered Ni-induced transcriptional disruption, reducing differentially expressed genes from 2462 to 1654 and downregulated known genes from 425 to 146. NCs + Ni also enhanced photosynthesis-, cell wall-, and phenylpropanoid-related pathways. Collectively, Ti@Fe3O4 NCs alleviate Ni toxicity through redox protection, ultrastructural preservation, and transcriptional regulation, offering a nano-enabled strategy for crops in Ni-contaminated agroecosystems.

title: Structural insights and mutational validation of a novel α/β hydrolase acting on oxidized polyethylene-derived substrates
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yanzi Sun, Yi Xiao, Sufang Wang, Dunpeng Liu, Yishu Wang, Lina Qiu, Yixin Liu, Haihong Jia, Feng Ding, Dengyue Sun, Mingguan Yang, Piwu Li
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accumulates environmentally due to its inertness and recalcitrance. PE biodegradation is generally considered a multistep process in which abiotic or enzymatic oxidation generates oxygen-containing intermediates subsequently transformed by downstream enzymes. However, the structural basis and catalytic roles of hydrolases in these downstream processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identified a novel α/β-hydrolase (HvH) from Vreelandella venusta, investigated using UV-oxidized and native PE films. Physicochemical characterization revealed that active HvH altered surface morphology, hydrophilicity, crystallinity, and molecular-weight distribution, whereas heat-inactivated controls showed substantially reduced effects. Site-directed mutagenesis of computationally predicted key residues further highlighted their contributions to catalytic activity and the observed changes in the UV-oxidized PE system. The crystal structure of HvH, determined at 2.71 Å resolution, revealed a canonical α/β-hydrolase fold containing a catalytic triad (S122–D223–H252) and a flexible loop–helix lid region regulating access to the substrate-binding pocket. Molecular dynamics, Markov state model analysis, and QM/MM simulations suggested a dynamic substrate-recognition mechanism and provided hypotheses regarding substrate recognition and catalysis that may guide further investigation. Collectively, these findings indicate that HvH may contribute to the transformation of materials associated with UV-oxidized PE and provide structural and mechanistic insights into hydrolase-mediated plastic biodegradation pathways. Synopsis This work provides structural and functional insights into a novel α/β hydrolase involved in the transformation of oxidized polyethylene-derived fragments.

title: Unravelling PFAS disruption of thyroxine transport by transthyretin using machine learning-augmented modelling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Aikaterini Theodori, Konstantinos D. Papavasileiou, Haralampos Tzoupis, Danae Zareifi, Andreas Tsoumanis, Francesco Dondero, Georgia Melagraki, Iseult Lynch, Antreas Afantitis
abstract: Thyroid-disrupting chemicals (TDCs) pose a significant risk to human health and are associated with adverse neurological and cardiovascular effects. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been shown to bind to transthyretin (TTR), disrupting thyroid hormone homeostasis and leading to adverse outcomes. We present a refined workflow for modelling and predicting PFAS activity toward TTR, where training compounds were labelled Active or Inactive based on experimental activity values (binding affinities) exceeding 50% relative to the control, thyroxine (binding partner of TTR). Curation of experimental datasets from published studies resulted in 131 unique PFAS structures for modelling. The dataset was augmented with molecular descriptors and molecular docking-derived scores, followed by model optimisation and evaluation through an automated machine learning (AutoML) approach. Among the tested classification algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the strongest overall performance, achieving a held-out test accuracy of 0.818. Structure-activity insights, molecular docking calculations and Shapley value analysis indicated an association between higher PFAS lipophilicity and Active predictions, consistent with the hydrophobic nature of the TTR binding pocket and previous experimental observations. In accordance with the FAIR principles for data and models, the curated dataset is publicly available through ChemPharos (https://db.chempharos.eu/datasets/Datasets.zul?datasetID=ds21). The final model is implemented as a user-friendly web application (https://enaloscloud.novamechanics.com/scenarios/thyrotox/).

title: Interpretable machine learning assessment of morphological traits and genetic factors associated with cadmium transfer to rice grains during grain filling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhong Tang, Meng-Jie Fu, Chuan-Jun Zhang, Bing-Ying Zou, Yi-Bo Wu, Min Liang, Peitong Wang, Qing Zhu, Jianlong Xu, Fang-Jie Zhao, Xin-Yuan Huang
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice grains threatens food safety and human health. Although root uptake and root-to-shoot translocation have been extensively characterized, the aboveground processes that determine Cd delivery to the grain remain poorly resolved. Here we combined in vitro detached panicle tracer-based transport phenotyping, aboveground morphological analysis, genetic haplotype analysis, and interpretable machine learning to dissect the determinants of grain Cd transfer capacity. Grain Cd transfer capacity varied 303-fold (phloem) and 233-fold (xylem), revealing extensive natural variation in aboveground Cd allocation. Twenty morphological and organ transfer traits of the node I, flag leaf and panicle and haplotypes of seven Cd allocation genes provided 27 input features for four machine learning models trained on 264 observations. The multilayer perceptron achieved the highest predictive accuracy with R2 = 0.67 and R2 = 0.63 for grain Cd transfer capacity relative to phloem and xylem transport, respectively. SHAP analysis ranked the flag leaf and panicle Cd transport capacity, seed-setting rate, and OsDEF8 haplotypes as the most influential predictors. Our results highlight that aboveground translocation processes, rather than organ morphology, are central to grain Cd loading. This integrative framework offers potential mechanistic insight and practical tools for breeding low-Cd rice, reducing dietary Cd exposure and improving food safety.

title: Sonic hedgehog pathway activation mitigates the anti-neurogenic effects of Bisphenol-A in the rat brain hippocampus
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ranjeet Kumar Yadav, Shraddha Tiwari, Phoolmala, Saurabh Tiwari, Tanya Jamal, Rajnish Kumar Chaturvedi
abstract: Bisphenol-A (BPA) causes neurochemical and neurobehavioral abnormalities in humans. Our previous studies showed that BPA inhibits hippocampal neurogenesis. Our current in-silico studies suggest that BPA interacts with key proteins of the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway. Postnatal BPA exposure caused alterations in Shh pathway associated gene expression and protein levels (RGMA, NEO1, and Gli1) in the rat hippocampus. BPA significantly reduced neural stem cells (NSCs) proliferation (reduced co-localization of NEO1 and Gli1 with Sox-2 and nestin) and neuronal differentiation (reduced co-localization of NEO1/β-Tubulin-III in the hippocampal NSCs-derived neuronal cultures and Gli1/NeuN and RGMA/NeuN in the hippocampus. Pharmacological inhibition of Shh pathway transcription factor (Gli1) by cyclopamine caused reduced NSCs proliferation and neuronal differentiation in NSCs culture. Pharmacological activation of canonical Shh signalling by Smoothened agonist SAG mitigated BPA-mediated inhibition of NSCs proliferation and neuronal differentiation in-vitro and in-vivo. Shh pathway activation reduced inhibitory effects of BPA on dendritic spines, mitochondrial and synaptic ultrastructure, and apoptosis in the hippocampus. Activation caused improved NSCs proliferation (increased number of neurospheres and size, and Gli1&Sox2/nestin co-localization), neuronal differentiation (Gli1/NeuN co-localization), neuronal growth cone formation (MAP2/GAP43 co-localization), and synaptic markers (MAP2&SYP/PSD95) co-localization leading to improved learneing and memory. Thus, activation of the Shh pathway mitigates the deleterious effects of BPA on neurogenesis, and cognitive impairments.

title: Integrated multi-omics and molecular modeling analyses of indaziflam distribution, ecological risks, and biological responses in a water–sediment system
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaoqian Song, Ruolin Wu, Hongyuan Zhang, Lei Zheng, Xiuguo Wang, Yiqiang Li, Tong Liu
abstract: Indaziflam is an alkylazine herbicide that inhibits cellulose biosynthesis, yet its environmental safety remains poorly understood. Indaziflam concentrations decreased in water under static exposure but remained relatively constant under semi-static exposure, while its concentrations in sediment increased under both exposure conditions. It exhibited moderate acute toxicity to zebrafish, Daphnia magna, and Chironomus kiiensis. During the 28-day exposure at 0.1 and 0.5 mg/L, indaziflam induced oxidative stress, disrupted antioxidant and detoxification enzyme activities, and affected neurochemical responses in zebrafish. Sediment microbial richness and diversity were significantly reduced, with altered community composition. Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analyses showed increased relative abundances of Pontibacter, Lysobacter, and Flavisolibacter following indaziflam exposure, indicating that these genera responded to indaziflam exposure. Zebrafish transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses showed altered pathways related to energy and nucleotide metabolism, cellular homeostasis, and neuroactive ligand–receptor interactions, alongside differential expression of neuronal signaling and detoxification genes. Molecular docking based on AlphaFold2 models and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a stable association between UGT5G2 and indaziflam, identifying UGT5G2 as a candidate detoxification protein. Collectively, this study characterizes the distribution and biological effects of indaziflam in a water–sediment system and identifies UGT5G2 as a candidate detoxification protein, providing evidence for its environmental risk assessment.

title: Thiram exposure impairs tibial chondrocyte maturation and ECM synthesis by disrupting the NAD+/Sirt1-driven glycolytic checkpoint
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kai Liu, Xiaomei Wu, Junhong Hou, Yuanliang Li, Ying Li, Zhaoxin Tang, Quazi T.H. Shubhra, Yung-Fu Chang, Hui Zhang
abstract: Thiram, a dithiocarbamate pesticide, induces tibial dyschondroplasia (TD) in broilers, but its metabolic toxicity mechanism remains unclear. Using thiram‑exposed broilers (100 mg/kg feed) and primary chondrocytes (10 μM thiram), we investigated whether thiram disrupts chondrocyte maturation and extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis by impairing NAD+‑dependent glycolysis. Thiram reduced the NAD+/NADH ratio and Sirt1 activity in tibial growth plates and downregulated glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and glycolytic enzymes (HK2, ENO1, LDHA). This metabolic crisis, evidenced by decreased glucose uptake, lactate production, ATP, and sulfated glycosaminoglycan synthesis, was accompanied by impaired chondrogenic markers (Sox9, Runx2, Aggrecan, Col2A1) and abnormal cartilage histology. Rescue experiments showed that GLUT1 overexpression partially reversed glycolytic defects and chondrocyte dysfunction caused by Sirt1 knockdown; Sirt1 knockdown attenuated, but did not abolish, GLUT1-mediated protection, and GLUT1 inhibition aggravated these impairments, indicating GLUT1 is a downstream mediator of Sirt1-driven glycolysis. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), an NAD+ precursor, elevated NAD+, reactivated Sirt1, upregulated GLUT1‑mediated glycolysis, and reversed thiram‑induced ECM loss and maturation arrest. We identify the NAD+/Sirt1/GLUT1 axis as a critical checkpoint that thiram targets to suppress chondrocyte glycolysis and differentiation, revealing a novel toxicological pathway, and suggest NAD+ replenishment may mitigate pesticide‑associated skeletal disorders, with implications for environmental health risk assessment.

title: Environmentally relevant imidacloprid impairs juvenile scallop growth via a dual constraint on energy acquisition and utilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qiaoqiao Wang, Xianming Tang, Wenhao Zhang, Lu Wang, Manni Wu, Luqing Pan, Jingjing Miao
abstract: Neonicotinoid insecticides are now ubiquitous in coastal waters, yet their chronic hazard to non-target marine invertebrates remains poorly defined. Juvenile scallops (Chlamys farreri) were exposed to imidacloprid (IMI) at environmentally relevant concentrations (0.5 and 5 μg/L) and a high level (50 μg/L) for 21 days, and growth, feeding physiology, neuroendocrine signalling, energy reserves and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to resolve the basis of growth inhibition. IMI severely suppressed the scope for growth and condition index at concentrations as low as 0.5 μg/L, at tissue burdens of 13.6–28.3 μg/kg. Mechanistically, IMI disturbed cholinergic, serotonergic, and insulin/NPY neuroendocrine circuits, leading to feeding suppression. Unexpectedly, this feeding suppression did not cause classical energy reserve depletion. Instead, IMI induced abnormal lipid accumulation together with reduced ETS activity and pronounced late-stage AMPK activation. Growth impairment may thus have arisen from a dual constraint, coupling suppression of energy acquisition with restricted energy utilization, a pattern consistent with cellular energy imbalance despite abundant stored lipids. This study reveals an overlooked hazard of sublethal neonicotinoid contamination to the growth performance of juvenile bivalves, emphasizing the need to incorporate early-life-stage energetic endpoints into ecological risk assessment.

title: Serendipita indica reshapes early metal allocation and root-associated transcriptional responses in Sedum alfredii under combined cadmium-lead stress
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Siyi Li, Jie Zhao, Xiaoqi Zhu, Yiming Ma, Xiaorui Zhang, Baoping Xie, Qianwen Fei, Yuanyuan Shao, Kuan Xu, Xini Liu, Yabei Qiao, Meng Fan, Shengke Tian
abstract: Mechanistic studies of plant-microbe interactions under heavy metal stress have focused predominantly on single metal exposure, whereas contaminated soils commonly contain multiple metals whose combined effects cannot be predicted directly from responses to individual contaminants. Here, we investigated how the root endophytic fungus Serendipita indica (S. indica) influences metal acquisition, allocation, and root transcriptional responses in the hyperaccumulator Sedum alfredii (S. alfredii) exposed to individual or combined cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) stress. Metal quantification was integrated with RNA sequencing, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and RT-qPCR validation. Under combined stress, S. indica increased root Cd and Pb concentrations, enhanced root-normalized shoot metal accumulation, and promoted root-to-shoot translocation. Combined Cd-Pb exposure elicited a transcriptional response distinct from those induced by either metal alone, while fungal inoculation further reshaped gene expression patterns associated with metal detoxification, redox regulation, protein homeostasis, and energy metabolism. Co-expression analysis identified gene modules associated with fungal inoculation and combined metal exposure, and RT-qPCR supported the RNA-seq expression trends of CSP4, atp2, SPBP35G2.11c, and RPS21. These findings demonstrate that S. indica modifies both metal acquisition and host stress responses under Cd-Pb co-stress, providing mechanistic insight into microbe-assisted phytoremediation of multi-metal-contaminated soils.

title: Occurrence, temporal trends, and associations of tetrabromobisphenol A/S and their analogs with fatty-acid profiles in cetaceans from the Northern South China Sea
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhenhui Xie, Yanling Gan, Bin Sun, Qiang Xie, Xiyang Zhang, Yuping Wu
abstract: Despite the increasing concerns about the health risks arising from the continuous detection of TBBPA/S and their analogs in biota, studies on their occurrence and potential risks in marine cetaceans remain limited. Here, we investigated the bioaccumulation characteristics and potential risks of 10 TBBPA/S and their analogs in 9 cetacean species (n = 40) from the NSCS during 2006 −2023. All target compounds were detected in at least one cetacean species, with the summed concentrations of the 10 target compounds ranging from 39.6 to 278.4 ng/g ww, indicating their widespread occurrence in the NSCS. Compared with TBBPA, its analogs, such as TBBPS-BME, TBBPS-BDBPE, and TBBPA-BHEE, predominated in these cetaceans. Target compound concentrations in N. phocaenoides showed no significant age- or sex-related differences. Although TBBPA concentrations remained stable from 2006 to 2023, its analogs (i.e., TBBPA-BHEE and TBBPA-BME) increased significantly. These trends are consistent with changing use patterns of BFRs, but cannot presently be attributed to a specific cause. Preliminary results suggested significant associations of TBBPA/S and their analogs with several individual FAs and/or FA group ratios (e.g., ∑n-6/∑n-3 PUFAs and SCD-16). These findings highlight the need for continued monitoring of these compounds to protect this vulnerable species.

title: Field-deployable sensors for PFAS detection: Current advances, emerging trends, and future opportunities
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Minshu Chen, Xin Lu, Tyler Maddox, Chujun Zhou, Shang Jia, Lei Guo
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants whose effective analysis, characterization, and remediation heavily rely on sensitive, reliable, and field-deployable monitoring technologies. Although liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) remains the benchmark for PFAS analysis, its reliance on centralized laboratories, specialized instrumentation, and extensive sample preparation limits its utility for rapid screening and on-site decision making. This review critically evaluates recent progress in non-mass-spectrometry PFAS sensors from the perspective of field deployment. We first define key design criteria for practical PFAS sensing, including regulatory-relevant sensitivity, selectivity, matrix tolerance, stability, and portability. We then summarize optical, electrochemical, and other sensing modalities that achieve limits of detection (LODs) at or below current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) drinking water limits for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), highlighting the recognition and signal-transduction strategies that enable ultralow PFAS detection. Beyond regulatory-relevant sensitivity, we discuss emerging trends in PFAS sensing, including emerging PFAS recognition mechanisms, detection of emerging, short and ultrashort chain PFAS, ratiometric quantification, PFAS differentiation, and smartphone-assisted readouts. Finally, we highlight persistent barriers to on-site PFAS sensing, including inconsistent LOD/LOQ reporting, limited assessment of specificity and selectivity, and challenges in translating laboratory proof-of-concept sensors into credible tools for routine field monitoring. Rather than replacing LC–MS/MS, field-deployable PFAS sensors are best positioned as complementary tools for rapid screening, source tracking, treatment monitoring, and early-warning detection. Future advances will require standardized performance evaluation, mechanism-guided sensor design, realistic field validation, and integration with portable data-processing platforms.

title: Distinguishing groundwater quality degradation from potentially toxic element risks in coastal aquifers: An integrated hydrogeochemical analysis and risk assessment framework
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhibin Li, Chengpeng Lu, Guangdong Wu, Bo Liu, Longcang Shu
abstract: Coastal plains are highly vulnerable to groundwater quality degradation driven by natural processes and human activities. Yet links among hydrochemical evolution, groundwater quality degradation, and potentially toxic element (PTE) risks remain poorly understood. This study integrates hydrogeochemical analysis, positive matrix factorization (PMF), the entropy water quality index (EWQI), partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), and an integrated potentially toxic element risk index (IPTE-RI) to investigate groundwater quality evolution in a coastal plain in eastern China. Groundwater hydrochemical evolution is primarily controlled by water-rock interaction, ion exchange, evaporation, and seawater intrusion. Hydrogeochemical processes associated with water-rock interaction and ion exchange account for up to 80% of the solute sources. Groundwater quality is favorable, although alternative weighting schemes produce an average difference of 51.34% in EWQI results. IPTE-RI reveals that groundwater quality degradation and PTE risks represent distinct dimensions of groundwater deterioration. All samples with IPTE-RI of 0.5–1.0 fall into the “medium” EWQI, while samples classified as “poor” or “very poor” have IPTE-RI values below 0.5. As, Cr (Ⅵ), and Ni are the major risk-contributing elements. This study provides a transferable approach for distinguishing groundwater quality degradation from specific toxic element risks, offering broad applicability for groundwater management in coastal plains.

title: Physiological and molecular responses of Enterococcus faecium IB-1 to Cd stress: Insights from transcriptional regulation and extracellular immobilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Min Zhu, Jing Sun, Ruobing Ren, Feng Zhao, Xinqi Lv, Juntao Cui, Yu Zhang, Kai Sun
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a highly toxic, mobile, persistent, and bioaccumulative heavy metal pollutant of major concern in agricultural environments. In this study, Enterococcus faecium IB-1, which has environmental adaptability and heavy metal tolerance, was selected as the target microorganism to explore its Cd tolerance mechanisms and immobilization potential. The results showed that Cd inhibited bacterial growth and induced adaptive responses. Specifically, visible colonies decreased by 63.9% in the 10 mg/L Cd2+-treated group, while a proportion of cells remained viable. Particulate deposition and cellular morphological alterations were observed under Cd stress. At the transcriptional level, 70 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 34 upregulated and 36 downregulated genes, were identified in E. faecium IB-1 treated with 10 mg/L Cd2+, while urea cycle and pyrimidine metabolism were enhanced. Oxygen-containing functional groups, carbonate-related species, and phosphate-associated components participated in Cd2+ binding and immobilization. Consistently, the highest Cd removal efficiency reached 44.72% under the conditions of this study. Moreover, CaCO3, CdCO3, and Ca4.03Cd0.97(PO4)3OH were formed and stabilized in localized alkaline microenvironments. Overall, Cd tolerance and immobilization involve physiological adaptation, cell-surface adsorption/complexation, urea production and hydrolysis, and carbonate/phosphate-associated mineral formation. This study provides mechanistic insights into Cd stress adaptation and biomineralization-associated Cd immobilization in E. faecium IB-1.

title: Geogenic Ni redistribution and soil-to-rice transfer during flooding and drainage in a basalt-derived paddy soil
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiupei Zhou, Wenting Chi, Kaiyi Huang, Shan Wang, Feng Gong, Zebin Hong, Guojun Chen, Shiwen Hu, Qi Wang, Guoyong Huang, Dandan Pan, Yang Yang, Xiaomi Li, Tongxu Liu
abstract: Geogenic nickel (Ni) in basalt-derived paddy soils is redox-responsive, but its redistribution and soil-to-rice transfer remain unresolved. A full-season pot experiment combined sequential extraction, interfacial characterization, and stage-specific kinetic modeling. During flooding, labile Ni (exchangeable and specifically adsorbed), Fe/Mn oxide-bound Ni, and organic matter-complexed Ni decreased from 2.70% to 1.55%, 5.74% to 3.82%, and 2.64% to 2.23%, respectively, whereas residual Ni increased from 84.47% to 86.82%, indicating net immobilization. These shifts coincided with reductive transformation of Fe-bearing phases, mobilization of mineral-associated organic matter, and altered mineral–organic interfacial properties. Plaque-associated Ni rose from 1.24 to 2.50 mg kg–1, and tissue Ni remained concentrated in roots. Modeling suggested a labile Ni → Fe/Mn oxide-bound Ni → residual Ni redistribution pathway during flooding, with possible transfers from organic matter-complexed and sulfide-bound pools to residual Ni. During drainage, labile Ni recovered to 1.82%, whereas organic matter-complexed and sulfide-bound Ni increased, indicating limited remobilization. Unified soil–plant modeling suggested apparent redistribution pathways, although several were weakly constrained. Interfacial changes and root-surface retention were associated with limited Ni transfer to grain; grain Ni was 0.34 mg kg–1, providing context for assessments of geogenic Ni mobility and soil-to-rice transfer across a flooding–drainage sequence.

title: Redirecting sulfur metabolic flux by Fe(II) in a simulated composting system: From H 2 S emission to oxidative immobilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qinghao Han, Yali Zhang, Junxing Zhu, Jingwen Jia, Qianhan Liang, Caihong Song, Zimin Wei
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) from food waste composting is a major odor pollutant. This study investigated H2S source reduction via iron regulated sulfur metabolism during food waste composting. Using a quartz-sand simulation system, two Fe(II) (ferrous chloride) concentrations (0.05%, 0.5%) were tested. In the blank control (CK), H2S peaked at 812 mg/m3, cumulatively emitting 2454 mg/m3 over 21 days. The optimal 0.5% Fe(II) completely suppressed H2S emission. Mechanistically, Fe(II) precipitated sulfide as FeS (partially converted to pyrite, 8.81 mg/kg) and may form a microbially mediated Fe(II) regeneration cycle, enabling continuous sulfide immobilization without inhibiting microbial activity. Functional gene analysis revealed that 0.5% Fe(II) suppressed dissimilatory sulfate reduction genes Sat and Apr (peaks falling to 47.3% and 27.3% of CK), reducing sulfide ion content by 94.5%. Conversely, sulfide oxidation gene Sqr was upregulated 212.4%-258.3% (days 3–5), shifting sulfur metabolic flux from reduction to oxidation. Metabolomics identified 210 differential metabolites, with reduced intermediates downregulated (e.g., bisulfite, thiosulfate) and oxidized/stable compounds upregulated, with significant enrichment in cysteine/methionine, sulfur, and taurine metabolism. In conclusion, 0.5% Fe(II) efficiently reduced H2S by redirecting sulfur flux toward oxidative immobilization, establishing a benign Fe(II) cycle.

title: Carbon composite derived from pyrolyzing polyamide microplastic-loaded biochar for peroxydisulfate activation and oxytetracycline removal
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Jia Li, Liming Dai, Meiting Guo, Min Cui, Jin Yin, Shengsen Wang
abstract: Widespread plastic usage triggers microplastics (MPs) accumulation and associated ecological risks. Magnetic biochar (MBC) can effectively adsorb aquatic MPs, yet desorption of captured MPs may cause secondary pollution. Herein, MP-laden MBC was pyrolyzed to prepare a carbon composite catalyst (MPBC@PA), which was applied in peroxydisulfate (PDS) system for oxytetracycline (OTC) removal. MPBC@PA exhibits superior catalytic activity than pristine biochar and MBC, achieving over 94% of OTC removal within 80minutes. The enhanced performance may originate from the abundant Fe–O groups and nitrogen doping induced by pyrolysis with PA-MPs, which facilitate PDS adsorption and electron transfer. MPBC@PA maintains > 89.63% even after five cycles, and exhibits robust catalytic activity across broad initial pH (3.0–9.0) and OTC concentration (1.0–40mg/L) ranges. Non‑radical pathways (primarily direct electron‑transfer with a minor contribution from 1O2) governed OTC degradation in the MPBC@PA/PDS system. QSAR predictions indicate partial transformation products have mitigated intrinsic acute lethal toxicity to fathead fish and Daphnia magna relative to OTC, while real effluent exhibits high toxicity to luminescent bacteria. This strategy of converting waste MP-loaded biochar into functional catalysts realizes the concept of “treating waste with waste”; thereby contributing to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

title: PFAS in Land Applied Biosolids: Occurrence, Environmental Fate, Plant Uptake, and Sustainable Management Strategies
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Tayyab A. Qureshi, Ramesh Goel, Rhonda Miller, Zhang Weilan, Donald M. Reeves, Ananda S. Bhattacharjee, Hongxu Zhou, Wei Zheng, Ethan S. Coffin
abstract: Biosolids are of concern because they are frequently applied to agricultural land, creating a potential pathway for per and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) get into the environment, and ultimately into the food chain. This review provides a synthesis of PFAS occurrence, fate, transport, and plant uptake following land application of biosolids. While previous studies have largely focused on PFAS occurrence, treatment technologies, or environmental distribution, this review examines the mechanisms governing PFAS behavior in biosolid-amended systems, the mechanisms of PFAS uptake by plants in land applied biosolids, and future directions as opposed to other reviews. This review highlights the risks of PFAS contamination, including disruptions to soil health, nutrient cycling, and ecosystem services, thereby improving our understanding of the long-term effects of PFAS-laden biosolids. A systematic literature review, bibliometric analysis, and quantitative synthesis of published data were also conducted to evaluate the influence of biosolids management practices, soil characteristics, environmental conditions, and PFAS properties on their environmental behavior. Key knowledge gaps related to PFAS transport, soil–plant interactions, precursor transformation, and long-term behavior, and future regulatory frameworks are identified. The findings provide a detailed understanding of PFAS behavior in biosolid-amended systems and identify priorities for future research and sustainable management strategies.

title: Aging-dependent pathogen loading and intestinal toxicity discrepancies between petroleum-based and biodegradable microplastics in zebrafish
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Yuhang Dou, Ke Ye, Boyan Nie, Jie Liu, Lei Wang, Zhenghua Duan
abstract: Although biodegradable plastics are widely promoted as eco-friendly alternatives to conventional petroleum-based plastics, their ecological risks following environmental aging remain poorly understood. Herein, microplastics (MPs) of conventional polyethylene (PE) and biodegradable PLA/PBAT were prepared from commercial packaging plastic bags via mechanical and insect-mediated fragmentation, yielding two groups of MPs subjected to mechanical aging and biological aging, respectively. All aged MPs were incubated in kitchen waste leachate to compare biofilm formation and pathogen enrichment profiles, followed by toxicological tests using zebrafish. The results demonstrated that the pathogen-loading capacity and biological toxicity of aged MPs were jointly shaped by aging patterns and polymer types. Compared with mechanically aged MPs, biologically aged MPs facilitated the colonization and intestinal transfer of pathogenic microbes in zebrafish, thereby triggering stronger inflammatory responses. Aged PLA/PBAT MPs accumulated more in the gut but caused milder histological damage, lower mortality, and weaker developmental inhibition than aged PE MPs. A possible explanation involves energy compensation, whereby fish may utilize their degradation products. This study offers novel insights into the aging- and material-dependent risks of MPs, supporting ecological safety assessment and rational application of biodegradable plastics in aquaculture ecosystems.

title: vsFreeze-thaw aging enhances microplastic phytotoxicity in rice via root metabolism and DNA methylation
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Zongyu Wang, Zikun Gao, Zhong Wang, Mengjun Wang, Zhangchao Yao, Zhixu Huang, Tanke Yu, Jiahui Li, Huijun Liu, Zhiheng Li, Jie Chen
abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling (FTC) accelerates microplastic (MP) aging in cold-region soils, yet the mechanisms underlying their amplified phytotoxicity remain elusive. This study integrated physicochemical characterization, metabolomics, and DNA methylation sequencing to evaluate the root toxicity of pristine and FTC-aged polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene in rice (Oryza sativa). FTC aging induced surface oxidation and structural fragmentation, increasing hydrodynamic diameters by 8.8-26.7% and elevating negative surface charge by 5.17-5.36mV. The aged PVC elicited the most severe phytotoxicity, disrupting root membrane integrity and suppressing superoxide dismutase activity by up to 54%. Metabolomic profiling revealed pronounced malate depletion coupled with lactate accumulation, indicating alterations in central carbon metabolism consistent with a potential shift toward glycolysis-associated metabolism, alongside significant perturbations in branched-chain amino acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing demonstrated that DNA methylation reprogramming was dominated by the CHH context, accounting for > 96% of all differentially methylated regions. Correlation network analysis revealed that aged PVC induced targeted CHH promoter hypermethylation in key redox hubs (e.g., NTRC, Trx M3), effectively decoupling antioxidant defense signaling from core energy metabolism. The work pinpoints that FTC-aged MP induced CHH methylation could connect to root metabolic reprogramming, establishing a basis for assessing risks of MPs in cold-climate agriculture.

title: Biofilm-Mediated Accumulation and Release of Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Potable Water Pipes: Experiments and Kinetic Modeling
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Atif Bashir, Dibya Kanti Datta, Chao Luo, Binbin Wang, Maryam Salehi
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) are increasingly detected in tap water; however, the role of biofilms in their retention and release within premise plumbing remains poorly understood. This study investigated the accumulation and release of polystyrene MPs (15µm) and NPs (500nm) in 15-month biofilm-laden and initially virgin PEX-A pipes under flow and stagnant conditions. Significantly more MPs accumulated on biofilm-laden pipes. After 48h accumulation under flow, MP loading was 4.7 ± 0.3 versus 2.9 ± 0.2µg/cm2 on biofilm-laden and initially virgin pipes, respectively; the corresponding 120h cumulative release fractions were 45.3 ± 4.3% versus 92.1 ± 8.1%, indicating enhanced retention by the heterogeneous biofilm matrix despite unfavorable electrostatic interactions. In contrast, NPs accumulated more on initially virgin pipes, while a greater fraction of retained NPs was released from biofilm-laden pipes. Thus, MPs and NPs exhibited contrasting accumulation and release behaviors, although interactions between particle populations cannot be excluded. Greater MP accumulation was found under flow and greater NP accumulation under stagnation exposure conditions. Langmuir attachment–detachment and multi-rate release models reproduced the observed accumulation and release trends and provided a quantitative framework for comparing particle–surface interactions across pipe and hydraulic conditions.

title: Linoleic acid secreted by maize root system regulates endophytic bacterium Serratia sp. NS8: Enhances nicosulfuron degradation by upregulating dadA and katG
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Kuo Liu, Yulin Wu, Yubo Ding, Fuqiang Guo, Qibing Yan, Donghui Liu, Hao Zhang
abstract: Nicosulfuron residues threaten maize growth and ecological sustainability, whereas plant–endophyte-mediated remediation represents a promising strategy, but the regulatory mechanisms linking host metabolites and bacterial degradation remain poorly understood. Here, an endophytic bacterium Serratia sp. NS8 was investigated to elucidate the interaction between maize metabolic responses and bacterial degradation of nicosulfuron. Metabolomic analysis revealed that nicosulfuron stress induced metabolic reprogramming in maize roots and promoted linoleic acid accumulation. Chemotaxis assays and functional analyses demonstrated that linoleic acid enhanced NS8 chemotactic response and promoted D-amino acid metabolism by upregulating dadA, thereby improving nicosulfuron transformation efficiency. Heterologous expression and enzymatic characterization further confirmed that KatG participated in nicosulfuron degradation through sulfonylurea bridge cleavage, producing an ASDM-like transformation product. In planta experiments showed that NS8 inoculation reduced nicosulfuron residues, alleviated oxidative stress, and improved maize growth performance. Integrated microbiome and metagenomic analyses indicated that NS8 modified rhizosphere microbial composition, functional potentials, and species-level co-occurrence patterns associated with degradation-related functions. This study reveals a metabolite-mediated regulatory mechanism linking maize, endophytic bacteria, and rhizosphere microbiota, providing an ecological framework for enhancing microbial remediation of herbicide contamination.

title: Coupled sulfur cycling and bioelectrochemical regulation of lead in carbon-limited constructed wetlands: Immobilization pathways and microbial responses
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Fengxiang Zhu, Jiale Li, Dongmei Cai, Haiying Yu, Jianjun Lian, Shanshan Hu, Bo Hu, Zhongbing Chen
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) are important nature-based systems for sustainable wastewater management, but simultaneous removal of lead (Pb) and conventional pollutants under low C/N conditions remains limited by electron donor deficiency and Pb-induced biological stress. This study investigated the effects of integrating microbial fuel cells (MFCs) and elemental sulfur on nutrient purification, Pb transformation, microbial responses, and bioelectricity generation in CWs planted with Iris pseudacorus. Results showed that coupling MFCs with sulfur overcame electron donor limitation under low C/N conditions, achieving removal efficiencies of 90.7%, 82.2%, and 82.7% for total phosphorus, total nitrogen, and chemical oxygen demand, respectively, and enhancing Pb removal to 87.9%. Pb was predominantly associated with the root cell wall fraction, and its extraction profile shifted toward the acetic-acid-extractable Pb fraction, consistent with restricted translocation to shoots. Microbial analyses showed that MFC and sulfur reshaped microbial community assembly and enriched functions related to carbon transformation, denitrification, sulfur cycling, and Pb immobilization. Sulfur amendment also improved bio-electrochemical performance by reducing internal resistance and increasing maximum power density. These findings indicate that integrating sulfur-driven metabolism with bioelectrochemical regulation provides a hybrid low-carbon strategy for simultaneous nutrient removal and Pb stabilization in carbon-limited wastewater treatment.

title: Inhibitory effects of polyethylene microplastics on biochar-mediated cadmium immobilization in farmland soil: Insights from a 120-day artificially spiked microcosm experiment
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Yingbo Dong, Lin Bai, Hai Lin
abstract: Polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs), widely derived from agricultural plastic mulching films, are critical contaminants in agricultural soils and may compromise remediation efficiency of biochar toward Cd-contaminated farmland. A 120-day microcosm experiment evaluated the effects of PE-MPs concentrations (0.1% and 1%) and particle sizes (50 and 500 μm) on biochar-mediated Cd immobilization. Compared with biochar application alone, the coexistence of PE-MPs increased TCLP-extractable Cd content by 0.68-0.87mg/kg and reduced Cd passivation efficiency by 41-52%. On day 120, 1% 50 μm PE-MPs decreased catalase activity by 0.45mg/(g·h) and elevated urease activity by 0.23mg/(g·24h). PE-MPs also altered bacterial community composition, and these shifts covaried with Cd fractionation. Mantel analyses associated Cd fractions with EC, CAT, CEC, and SOC. At 1%, 50 μm PE exerted a stronger inhibitory effect on TCLP-extractable Cd than 500 μm particles, whereas no significant size effect occurred at 0.1%. Characterization of recovered biochar showed that coexistence with 50 μm PE decreased specific surface area and total pore volume by 43% and 39%, respectively. SEM and FTIR results suggested that PE-MPs attachment and aggregation may cover external biochar surfaces and reduce the accessibility of oxygen-containing Cd-binding sites. Overall, PE-MPs weakened biochar mediated Cd immobilization under the experimental conditions.

title: Enhanced CH 4 -SCR performance over core–shell-like In/H-SSZ-13@CeZrO x via bifunctional InO + sites and CeZrO x -promoted reactive NO x surface speciation
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Guanyu Chen, Mei Hong, Ning Zhao, Lingnan Xie, Lei Lu, Shanlan Xu, Xixi Wang, Rongshu Zhu
abstract: The selective catalytic reduction of NO x with CH4 (CH4-SCR) offers a promising strategy for simultaneous harmful NO x and CH4 abatement, but its practical application is hindered by severe activity loss under humid conditions. Herein, a core–shell-like In/H-SSZ-13@CeZrO x (CZO) catalyst was fabricated through a self-assembly strategy. The optimized catalyst achieved nearly 90% NO x removal at 5 vol.% H2O and a high GHSV of 100,000 h−1, outperforming In/H-SSZ-13, CZO, and In/H-SSZ-13@CeO x counterpart. Structural characterizations showed that CZO coating increased the external surface area and mesoporosity without damaging the CHA framework, forming a porous outer layer while maintaining accessibility to the inner zeolite. Zr incorporation increased the Ce 3+ fraction and oxygen-defect density of this outer layer. In situ DRIFTS demonstrated that InO + oxocations act as bifunctional sites for both NO oxidation and selective CH4 activation, while the CZO layer promotes NO oxidation and the formation of NO-derived reactive intermediates. The enhanced CH4-SCR performance of In/H-SSZ-13@CZO therefore originates from CZO-promoted NO-related surface speciation with an InO + -mediated reaction cycle. This work highlights rational oxide–zeolite interface engineering as an effective strategy for coupling promoted NO oxidation and reactive NO x speciation with selective CH4 activation, enabling robust CH4-SCR under humid conditions.

title: Metagenomic and Mineralogical Evidence of Microbial Community Restructuring across a Natural Radiological-Geochemical Gradient.
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Rashmi Priya, Santosh K. Sahu, Owais M. Bhat, P.R. Vivek Kumar, Divyalakshmi Saini, Rohit Verma, Rakesh Shukla, Vinita Grover, Sangeeta J. Sartandel, Prateek Chandrani, Vinay Jain, Santosh K. Sandur, Deepak Sharma
abstract: Naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM), including thorium and uranium, together with associated heavy metals, represent persistent environmental contaminants that exert chronic radiological and chemical stress on soil ecosystems. To investigate microbial adaptation under long-term exposure, we integrated mineralogical characterization with metagenomic-sequencing of monazite-rich soils from the High-Level Natural Radiation Area (HLNRA) of Kerala, India, spanning a natural radiation gradient of 0.6-150 mGy/year. Mineralogical analyses revealed enrichment of thorium and uranium with elevated titanium, aluminium and iron concentrations, while X-ray diffraction indicated lattice disorder in high-radiation soils. Despite >1000-fold variation in radionuclide concentrations, microbial alpha diversity remained stable. However, significant community reorganization and species-level turnover were observed, although dominant bacterial phyla remained conserved. Fourteen species, including Egicoccus halophilus and Woeseia oceani, were positively associated with radiation dose, whereas 44 species linked to carbon degradation and nitrogen transformation were negatively associated. Functional profiling revealed shifts along the radiological-geochemical gradient. Taxa enriched in high-radiation soils were associated with aromatic-compound degradation, heavy-metal resistance and oxidative-stress tolerance. BacMet annotation identified resistance determinants for arsenic, copper, and oxidative stress-related compounds. These findings indicate that microbial community restructuring can occur without substantial changes in overall diversity across a natural radiological-geochemical gradient. The observed patterns provide insights into microbial resilience in NORM-contaminated environments.

title: Systemic coordination underpins wheat cultivar-specific tolerance to oxytetracycline: a multi-omics perspective
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Xiaojun Wu, Songyan Wei, Gan Li, Weihua Ding, Hao Jiang, Tiezhu Hu, Xiangdong Chen, Zhengang Ru
abstract: Oxytetracycline (OTC) readily accumulates in agricultural soils, threatening wheat productivity and food safety; however, the mechanisms underlying cultivar-specific OTC tolerance remain unclear. In this study, we used the relatively tolerant cultivar Bainong 4199 (BN) and the relatively sensitive cultivar Yannong 21 (YN) as experimental materials. Integrating phenotypic, physiological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, we elucidated the differential regulatory mechanisms underlying their responses. OTC primarily inhibited root growth in both cultivars, more strongly in YN, whereas BN showed hormetic shoot stimulation at low OTC concentrations. In both cultivars, reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde levels increased with increasing OTC concentration. Multi-omics suggested YN had less concordant cross-omics patterns, while BN maintained coordinated regulation of energy, protein, antioxidant, and secondary metabolism. Specifically, BN showed greater citrate accumulation with coordinated glycolysis-TCA upregulation, likely supplying intermediates for protein repair and defense. Under stress, energy compensation was limited, with skewed secondary metabolites and reduced signaling-metabolism coupling, potentially contributing to cellular damage. Multi-omics analyses revealed that OTC tolerance in the two tested cultivars involved multi-layered metabolic coordination, not single-pathway activity. This study characterizes cultivar-specific adaptive strategies, offering insights into assessing antibiotic risks in farmland, breeding OTC-tolerant wheat, and safe crop production in contaminated soils.

title: Selenium-doped red carbon dot nanozymes for dual-mode tetracycline detection and synergistic antibacterial inactivation
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Shan Huang, Silin Li, Wei Ni, Guixin Li, Yutong Zhao, Fuxiang Wei, Yi Fang, Qi Xiao
abstract: Multifunctional nanozyme platforms integrating pollutant detection and antibacterial action are highly desirable for environmental monitoring and food safety. Herein, red-emissive selenium-doped carbon dots (Se-CDs, λ em = 615 nm) were synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal strategy. The Se-CDs exhibit excellent photostability and pronounced peroxidase-mimetic activity. A dual-readout colorimetric/fluorescence platform was thus constructed for total screening of tetracycline-class antibiotics, achieving detection limits of 0.22 μM and 0.23 μM, both reaching the maximum residue limit for tetracycline in milk (approximately 0.22–0.23 μM) stipulated by the EU and China’s GB 31650–2019. Density functional theory calculations, including implicit solvation and pH-relevant protonation states, revealed that tetracycline adsorption in the Se-associated catalytic environment was protonation-state-dependent, suppressing catalytic oxidation and enabling dual-channel signaling. The method was applied to tetracycline quantification in commercial milk with recoveries of 93.74%–107.60%. Moreover, the Se-CDs showed low cytotoxicity and potent antibacterial efficacy against both Gram-negative Escherichia coli and Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus, achieving 97.98% and 99.93% inactivation within 30 min via synergistic peroxidase-like reactive oxygen species generation and membrane disruption. This method is intended as a rapid screening tool for total tetracycline-class antibiotics, and provides an integrated paradigm for rational design of CD-based nanozymes with dual-functional capabilities in hazard monitoring and antibacterial applications.

title: AI-assisted High-Throughput Screening of MOFs for Formaldehyde Capture
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Kevizali Neikha, Amrit Puzari
abstract: Formaldehyde (FA) is a hazardous indoor volatile organic compound that poses risks to human health, demanding efficient adsorbent materials. Functionalized Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) offer structural tunability; however, functionalization can alter the framework, increase heterogeneity, cause pore blockage, and increase cost. Identification of pristine MOFs for FA adsorption is crucial for understanding adsorption mechanisms, framework topology, chemical composition, and unfunctionalized structures. In this work, we present an AI-assisted high-throughput screening framework that combines Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)-based text mining, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations, and Machine Learning (ML) to accelerate the discovery of MOFs for FA capture. Four MOF features were extracted using GAI text mining, and 1208 MOFs were selected from the CoRE MOF 2019 database. GCMC simulations evaluated FA uptake, while atomic, geometric, chemical, and thermodynamic descriptors were extracted for ML analyses. Seven regressors were developed to predict FA uptake based on these descriptors. An SVR-based denoising method was introduced during preprocessing to reduce simulation noise and improve predictions. The SVR model showed the best performance with an R² value of 0.94 and predicted FA uptake in 500 hMOFs. Validation of GAI responses, feature analyses, and experimental data for HKUST-1 and MIL-101 confirmed reliability of this approach.

title: Microplastics, Endocrine Disruption, and Hormone-Responsive Cancers
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Destiny Tiburcio, Jon Swedenborg, Kalise Coffee, Michal Toborek
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging concern in human health as plastic production continues to accelerate, resulting in increased global pollution. Exposure to MPs spans the entire lifetime, from ingestion and inhalation to more indirect contact through placental barriers. The endocrine system and hormone-responsive organs, including breast, endometrium, thyroid and prostate could be especially vulnerable to the harmful effects of MPs as they carry additives with endocrine-disrupting activity. Furthermore, the highly metabolic nature of these organs, which are often enriched in lipids, supports the retention of hydrophobic MP-associated additives, and creates a pro-oxidative environment, which favors genotoxicity and carcinogenesis. This review examines emerging data on the potential association between MP exposure and the onset of hormone-responsive cancers, such as breast, endometrial, thyroid, and prostate cancers. The reported findings aim to inform future research directions in endocrine-related cancer etiology and population health, and may help prioritize research and exposure reduction.

title: Deriving a Proxy for Highly Reactive VOCs from Satellite Formaldehyde: Application to a Chinese Megaregion
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Heng Yao, Saisai Chen, Fuhua Mao, Chunyan Zhou, Ruizhi Chen, Wei Wei
abstract: Formaldehyde (HCHO), a key volatile organic compound (VOC) oxidation intermediate, is a proxy for VOC reactivity, yet substituting ΩHCHO for VOCs is uncertain. We propose a novel satellite-based approach to estimate highly reactive VOCs (HRVOCs) over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region, a global HCHO hotspot, during July 2018-2022. Our approach first extracts secondary HCHO (ΩHCHO_SEC) by subtracting primary (ΩHCHO_PRI) and background (ΩHCHO_BACK) HCHO from ΩHCHO; then simulates the HCHO yield coefficient from HRVOCs using a box model considering composition, NOx, and meteorology; finally derives ΩHRVOCs via a steady-state equation for secondary HCHO. For July 2018-2022, ΩHRVOCs were 12.71–16.57 × 1015 molecules·cm-2 in urban areas, 2.42–5.41 × 1015 molecules·cm-2 in mixed areas, and 0.95–1.45 × 1015 molecules·cm-2 in vegetation areas. The retrievals show expected mechanistic relationships: ΩHRVOCs variation in vegetation areas correlates with temperature, and ΩHRVOCs exhibits a positive spatial association with surface ozone; uncertainty propagation shows CVs of ΩHRVOCs ranging from 23.26% to 43.64% across regions. This study bridges the spatial gap between surface VOC concentrations and space-based observations, offering novel insights into spatiotemporal quantification of VOCs.

title: Legacy and emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances profiles in the two largest tributaries of the Yellow River: roles of industrial structures and hydrodynamical condition
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Yawen Li, Wenjing Lv, Yanan Li, Yitao Pan, Fengfeng Dong, Qiusheng He, Yang Cui, Xiang Ren, Yanfeng Zang, Jiayin Dai, Jianhui Tang
abstract: Seasonal hydrology regulates contaminant transport and fate, yet hydro-sedimentary controls on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in sediment-rich rivers remain poorly understood. This study investigates how industrial structures and hydro-sedimentary dynamics shape PFAS distribution, phase partitioning, and transport in the Fen (FR) and Wei (WR) Rivers, the two largest tributaries of the Yellow River. PFAS concentrations in water, suspended particulate matter (SPM), and sediments generally increased from upstream to middle reaches before declining downstream. ΣPFAS concentrations were higher in WR (1.12–8873.6ng/L; mean: 441.8ng/L) than in FR (3.55–415.1ng/L; mean: 53.5ng/L), with traditional PFAS dominating FR (82.5%) and perfluoroalkyl ether carboxylic acids (PFECAs) contributing 43.1% in WR, reflecting distinct industrial signatures. In FR, wet-season hydrology reduced dissolved-phase concentrations but increased SPM-associated PFAS. With increasing downstream streamflow and sediment flux, partition coefficients (Kd) and particle-associated fractions (f particle) decreased for short-chain PFAS but increased for long-chain homologues. This reveals chain-length-dependent SPM behavior, characterized by particle dilution of short-chain PFAS and enhanced transport of long-chain homologues under intensified sediment transport. Statistical analyses further showed that dissolved PFAS were primarily influenced by meteorological and socioeconomic factors, whereas SPM-associated PFAS were predominantly controlled by hydro-sedimentary processes.

title: Air Quality Benefits and Carbon Reduction Potential of Future Ultra-Low Emission Retrofits in the Chinese Coking Industry
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Fen Liu, Shu Xu, Yufei Tan, Zongshuang Wang
abstract: China, the world’s largest coke producer, emits substantial air pollutants and CO₂ from coking. Although ultra-low emission standards are being implemented, their emission reductions, remaining mitigation potential, and air quality benefits remain unclear. This study developed a nationwide, plant- and sector-level emission inventory of air pollutants and CO2 for China’s coking industry for 2023. Compliance rates for particulate matter (PM) and sulfur dioxide (SO2) concentrations exceeded 99.6% across all emission stages, whereas the nitrogen oxides (NOx) compliance rate at the coke oven stack stage was 86.52%. In 2023, coking industry emitted 16.01, 26.55, 88.16, and 129.33kt·yr-1 of PM, SO2, NOx, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), respectively, and 227.80 Mt·yr-1 of CO2. Under the synergistic air pollutant-CO2 mitigation scenario, emissions of PM, SO2, NOx, VOCs, and CO2 would be reduced by 43.3%, 4.1%, 18.0%, 77.9%, and 54.7%, respectively. Air quality simulations indicated that the coking industry’s contributions to ambient PM2.5, SO2, NO2 and O3 concentrations could be reduced by 53.5%, 20.7%, 40.0%, and 15.8%, respectively. These findings reveal substantial differences in emission characteristics and remaining mitigation potential across coking processes and pollutants, providing new sector-specific insights for developing targeted air pollutant and CO2 mitigation strategies in China’s coking industry.

title: Reductive Bioleaching of Metals from Spent Lithium-ion Batteries using Corn Silage Slurries
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Qu Wen, Angela Gil, Xu Li
abstract: Recovery of metals from the cathode materials of spent lithium ion (Li-ion) battery is important to achieve circular economy and environmental sustainability. The objective of this study was to explore the feasibility of using corn silage (CS) to leach metals from spent Li-ion batteries in a two-stage process, fermenting stage and bioleaching stage. Lactic acid and acetic acid were the dominant carboxylic acids in the CS slurry during the fermenting stage. Increasing CS content in the slurry enhanced metal recovery, achieving max leaching efficiencies of 96.70±3.22% for Li, 89.47±4.09% for Ni, 70.55±4.95% for Co, and 83.65±6.25% for Mn after 31 days of bioleaching with 6% CS. Following the addition of the cathode materials to the CS slurry, reducing sugars were released from CS solids. The consumption of reducing sugars, along with the detection of the potential oxidation products of the reducing sugars (e.g., glyceric acid), coincided with the release of metals from the cathode materials, suggesting that reducing sugars might contribute to metal leaching as reductants during bioleaching. Overall, this work demonstrated corn silage as a novel and effective bioleaching agent to recover valuable metals from spent Li-ion batteries.

title: Divergent Fates of PAHs During Reductive Soil Disinfestation: Activation Versus Sequestration Dictated by Biochar Pyrolysis Temperature
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Siyi Hu, Ran Wei, Weifeng Chen, Jinzhi Ni
abstract: Reductive soil disinfestation (RSD) and biochar amendment are established strategies for soil improvement and pollution remediation, respectively, but their combined effects on polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) fate remain unclear. A 56-day RSD incubation was conducted on PAH-spiked, pre-aged Anthrosol amended with wheat straw- and pine sawdust-derived biochars produced at 300 ℃ and 750 ℃. By combining sequential extraction with density fractionation, we separated soil PAHs into available, extractable, and alkaline-extractable bound (AE-bound) fractions to characterize PAH redistribution and mechanisms. Biochar pyrolysis temperature exerted stronger control on PAH redistribution than feedstock. Within 7 days, RSD lowered redox potential, increased pH, promoted metal oxide dissolution, and disrupted aggregates, thereby remobilizing a previously sequestered PAH pool. Low-temperature biochars (LT-BCs, 300 ℃) promoted an activation pathway, decreasing AE-bound PAHs by 39.26–52.70% and increasing the extractable fraction by 15.46–54.37%; remobilized PAHs associated with LT-BCs transferred into the light fraction. In contrast, high-temperature biochars (HT-BCs, 750 ℃) promoted a sequestration pathway, with decreased available PAHs accounting for most of the total extracted PAH reduction and HT-BC particles incorporating into the heavy fraction, rendering associated PAHs non-extractable. Collectively, these findings reveal pyrolysis-temperature-dependent activation and sequestration pathways during RSD, with LT-BCs increasing PAH extractability and potentially facilitating biodegradation.

title: Shared anthropogenic drivers of nitrate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons: Implications for terrestrial-aquatic source tracing and integrated watershed management
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Zihan Zhao, Jiayu Zhao, Hao Sun, Xueyi Yuan, Wenhao Li, Zucong Cai, Yanhua Wang
abstract: Nitrate (NO3 −) contamination in surface water and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in soil pose environmental challenges in the rapidly urbanizing upstream watershed of Taihu Lake. However, pollutants are commonly investigated independently, limiting understanding of their shared anthropogenic controls. Here, isotopic analysis, Bayesian mixing models, receptor modeling, and risk assessment were integrated to investigate aquatic NO₃⁻ and soil PAHs across three contrasting river-network regions. NO3 − concentrations peaked in the industrial-agricultural area (TGRA; 1.81 ± 0.33mgL−1), followed by the agricultural lakeside area (LRA) and highly-urbanized area (CDRA). Soil ΣPAH16 concentrations exhibited spatial heterogeneity, ranging from 989.14 to 8184.38ngg−1, with the highest value observed in the TGRA. Beyond co-occurrence, aquatic NO3 − and soil PAHs exhibited regionally corresponding source profiles, indicating overlapping anthropogenic pressures across environmental compartments. Fertilizer-derived NO3 − (66.0% ± 13.8%) and coal/coke combustion-derived PAHs dominated the TGRA, which exhibited the poorest water quality and highest ecological and health risks. In LRA, manure-derived NO3 − (72.1% ± 16.8%) and biomass-burning PAHs predominated, whereas the CDRA was characterized by mixed NO3 − sources and traffic/petroleum-related PAH. Soil erosion further provided a potential terrestrial-aquatic linkage for PAH transport. These findings highlight the value of cross-media source tracing for integrated, region-specific watershed pollution management.

title: Bacillus paranthracis YB‑11 loaded biochar and biochar enhances cadmium detoxification effect in tobacco
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Ran Wang, Chuandong Jiang, Minghui Liu, Xidong Peng, Yan Zhang, Qiang Zhang
abstract: Owing to their remarkable plant-growth-promoting effects, strong rhizosphere colonization capacity, and environmental adaptability, Bacillus strains are widely used for the remediation of heavy metal (HM)-contaminated soils, and heavy metal toxicity to crops is alleviated via the regulation of rhizosphere microenvironments. Nevertheless, the survival and colonization of Bacillus strains in soil were severely inhibited under Cd stress, and remediation efficiency was limited accordingly. Biochar serves as an eco-friendly material, providing suitable habitats for microorganisms and improving the survival of strains in HM-contaminated soils. Most previous investigations have focused on Cd-tolerant Bacillus strains. Strain YB-11, a Bacillus isolate obtained from tobacco rhizosphere, was inactivated under Cd contamination at 40mg/kg. The survival of this Cd-sensitive strain was effectively maintained by the combined application of YB-11 and biochar, as demonstrated in plate assays. The plant detoxification mechanism of the combined Bacillus and biochar treatment was further analyzed via pot experiments. Compared with single treatments, significant enhancements in the antioxidant capacity and photosynthetic performance of tobacco were recorded under the combined treatment. Direct measurements of tobacco tissues showed that Cd concentrations in tobacco leaves and roots were reduced by 49.26% and 48.76%, respectively. Meanwhile, available soil nutrients and enzyme activities were elevated to accelerate soil fertility transformation. Moreover, the combined treatment improved soil available nutrients and enzyme activities to accelerate soil nutrient transformation. Furthermore, the rhizosphere microbial community was reshaped by the combined treatment, characterized by enrichment of cadmium-tolerant and nutrient-optimizing taxa, including Acidobacteriota, Pseudomonadota, Sphingomonas, and Acrophialophora. Partial least squares path model (PLS-PM) analysis demonstrated that the combined treatment regulated purine metabolism, lysine degradation, and flavonoid synthesis pathways, which in turn influenced the antioxidant system, photosynthesis, and soil microecology to inhibit cadmium uptake. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the regulation of tobacco cadmium stress responses and the synergistic interaction between biochar and Bacillus for enhancing contaminated farmland remediation efficiency.

title: Heavy metal contamination of industrial soil revealed by Cu, Zn, and Pb isotopic ratios of sequential extraction fractions
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Dae-Gyu Im, Duk-Min Kim, Nok Il Kwak, Seong-Taek Yun
abstract: The sources and mobility of metals in contaminated industrial soils are difficult to resolve from total concentrations alone. Four of the 11 soils from a railway maintenance facility in Seoul, South Korea, were sequentially extracted, and Cu, Pb, and Zn isotopes were measured in each fraction of the most contaminated soil (S5). S5 contained 7130 mg kg−1 Pb, and As, Cd, Cu, and Zn also exceeded the Korean Worrisome Levels for Area 1. Its Fe-oxide spherules, anomalous magnetic susceptibility, and thermally refractory carbon are consistent with a waste input from metallurgical operations. Less than 1% of Cu, Pb, and Zn was exchangeable in all four soils. The 207Pb/206Pb of all five fractions (0.889–0.894), including the residual, fell outside Korean stream-sediment and subsoil ranges, so anthropogenic Pb dominated every fraction. These ratios differed from coal-combustion and urban Pb but overlapped Korean smelter emissions, consistent with imported ore. In contrast, δ65Cu and δ66Zn varied among the fractions. Relative to the mass-balance bulk, carbonate-bound Zn was heavy (Δ66Zn = +0.29‰) but Cu light (Δ65Cu = −1.29‰). Because Pb varied less among fractions than its offset from geogenic Pb, these differences are interpreted as in-soil partitioning rather than a distinct source for each fraction.

title: Novel Insights into BPS-induced Neurodevelopmental Toxicity in the Octopus: Excitation/Inhibition Imbalance Associated with GRM5 Dysregulation Potentially Impairs Learning and Memory Function of Amphioctopus fangsiao
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Lihua Wang, Jian Zheng, Penglong Zhang, Yifan Huangfu, Xiaodong Zheng
abstract: Bisphenol S (BPS) is widely detected in aquatic environments, yet its neurodevelopmental toxicity mechanisms in marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. Octopuses, the most intelligent invertebrates with sophisticated nervous systems, serve as ideal model organisms for neurodevelopmental research. In this study, Amphioctopus fangsiao embryos were exposed to 1, 10, and 100μg/L BPS to evaluate its neurodevelopmental toxicity. The results showed that BPS exposure reduced hatching rates, and induced structural atrophy in the vertical lobe, a core region responsible for learning and memory, accompanied by oxidative stress, neuronal apoptosis, and synaptic damage in brain tissue. Behavioral assays confirmed that 10μg/L BPS was associated with altered light habituation behavior, suggesting a potential impact on non-associative learning. Through transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking, we prioritized glutamate receptor 5 (GRM5) as a candidate neurotoxic target. BPS was predicted to interact with GRM5 and to upregulate its expression, which was associated with disruption of neuronal excitatory/inhibitory balance, inhibited the ERK/CREB pathway phosphorylation and downregulated synaptic plasticity-related genes. These findings propose a putative mechanistic framework linking GRM5 dysregulation to potential learning and memory impairment, providing an integrated assessment of BPS-induced developmental neurotoxicity in a cephalopod with complex cognition and a basis for future risk assessment.

title: Micro-nano bubbles enhanced n -hexane removal in biotrickling filters: performance, biofilm regulation, and clogging alleviation
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Minmin Zhang, Xingyu Ma, Yixuan Ji, Min He, Yuying Jiang, Jianmeng Chen, Dongzhi Chen
abstract: n-Hexane, a hydrophobic VOC and photochemical smog precursor, exhibits poor water solubility that severely limits its biodegradation in conventional biotrickling filters (BTFs) due to insufficient gas-liquid mass transfer and packing clogging. In this study, a micro-nano bubble (MNB)-coupled BTF was constructed to enhance n-hexane biodegradation, and its effects on reactor performance, biofilm architecture, and microbial stress responses were systematically investigated. Under continuous operation, MNBs improved n-hexane removal by approximately 22 percentage points at low-to-medium inlet concentrations via intensified mass transfer and sustained microbial activity. At 700mg∙m-3, this enhancement diminished due to combined substrate inhibition and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) stress. At 15 ºC, MNBs partially alleviated low-temperature suppression. Notably, MNBs reversed the conventional bottom-heavy biomass distribution, increased hydrophobicity and antioxidant capacity in the upper biofilm, and reduced pressure drop by two to threefold. This work demonstrates MNB-coupled BTF as a sustainable, chemical-free intensification strategy for hydrophobic VOC treatment.

title: Combining Target and Nontarget Screening to Reveal PFAS Contamination Profiles and Health Risks in Aquatic Products
