description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Shuai Wu, Xiao Liu, Shuang Liu, Dawei Chen, Jianwen Li, Sheng Wen, Jiaying Liu
abstract: Despite global restrictions reducing legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), the prevalence of emerging alternatives continues to escalate. This study employed target and nontarget screening to assess PFAS in market aquatic products from Hubei Province, China. A total of 41 PFAS were detected, 15 with detection frequencies (DF) > 50%, with the ∑15 PFAS concentration ranging from 1.07 to 49.2ng/g dry weight (dw). Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) was the most abundant, with a geometric mean (GM) concentration of 2.55ng/g dw, accounting for 54% of ∑15 PFAS. Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA; GM concentration: 0.38ng/g dw) exhibited higher contamination than perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NTf2; GM concentration: 0.015ng/g dw), an emerging PFAS used in lithium-ion batteries, showed high DF. Monte Carlo simulation-based dietary exposure model indicated children aged 3-6 and 7-12 years had significantly higher estimated daily intake (EDI) of ∑15 PFAS than other age groups, and their median EDI of ∑PFOA + PFNA + PFHxS + PFOS via aquatic products exceeded tolerable daily intake. For the general population, the median risk quotient of perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) was 50. Of the 15 highly detected PFAS, 8 still lack reference doses for risk assessment.

title: Microbial and geochemical controls on selenium methylation and volatilization by bacteria from Hg–Se contaminated paddy soils
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Qingqing Wu, Hua Zhang, Chaofa Chen, Haiyan Hu, Chuanyu Chang, Kang Mao, Xuefeng Yang, Baolin Wang, Kevin Bishop
abstract: Selenium (Se) is essential at trace levels but can become hazardous when accumulated in mining-impacted soils. Microbial Se volatilization offers a potential remediation strategy, but its efficacy under mercury (Hg)–Se cocontamination remains uncertain. We compared Se(IV) methylation among 20 aerobic bacterial isolates from Hg–Se-impacted paddy soil in Wanshan and examined the effects of Se loading, temperature, sulfur species, and Hg coexposure in Aeromonas hydrophila D15. All isolates produced dimethyldiselenide (DMDSe) as the only detected volatile methylated species, with recovered amounts varying by approximately 86-fold. In independent D15 experiments, DMDSe production responded nonlinearly to Se(IV), was inhibited by sulfate, and was stimulated by 0.01mM methionine. At 37 °C, DMDSe production decreased by 87% relative to 30 °C. Hg coexposure at a Hg molar ratio of 2:1 reduced recovered DMDSe by 98% and coincided with Hg–Se-rich particles whose XRD features were compatible with an HgSe-like phase. These observations motivate a testable, non-exclusive hypothesis that Hg-associated solid formation may compete with microbial Se volatilization for transformed Se, while direct metabolic inhibition remains possible. The findings identify factors constraining Se volatilization in controlled bacterial cultures and a potential trade-off between volatile and solid Se products, informing evaluation of remediation strategies for Hg–Se-cocontaminated soils.

title: Intrinsic phytate and minerals lower arsenic bioaccessibility in brown rice: Mechanistic insights via machine learning
description: Publication date: Available online 16 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Guobing Lin, Wenjie Dong, Yuan-Chen Zhang, Chenjing Liu, Lena Q. Ma
abstract: Whole-grain diets are promoted by substituting white rice with brown rice, which confers health benefits but increases arsenic (As) exposure. Based on 104 paired samples, brown rice exhibited 51% higher total As but 19% lower As bioaccessibility than white rice. Machine learning models identified As, S, Mg, and phytate contents as key determinants of bioaccessible As. Sequential extraction showed that 88–96% of As was associated with proteins, while 54−92% of P existed as phytate. While phytase-induced phytate hydrolysis elevated As bioaccessibility by 33–54%, exogenous phytate reduced it by 7.5–22%. Similarly, in an aqueous system, phytase increased water-soluble S and As by 16–35% and 12–19%. Conversely, supplementing phytate and Mg reduced water-soluble As. These results suggest that phytate and minerals may contribute to As retention in rice grains, probably through the phytate-mineral-protein ternary association, which potentially makes As-bearing proteins less available to enzymes and thereby restricts As release. In this context, 90−300% greater phytate and Mg contents in brown rice than white rice may enhance its As retention, contributing to its lower As bioaccessibility. Overall, this study proposes a working model to evaluate As release from rice grains and provides a possible explanation for lower As bioaccessibility in brown rice.

title: Efficient Solar Spectrum Partitioning in a Photoelectrochemical-Fenton Process for Synergistic Hydroxyl Radical Generation Solely from Water
description: Publication date: Available online 16 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Seungmok Han, Ho-Sub Bae, Seok Kim, Sukhwa Hong, Chang Won Yoon, Kangwoo Cho, Wonyong Choi
abstract: We herein propose a solar-irradiated photoelectrochemical (PEC) system that achieves synergistic ·OH radical generation both from anodic and cathodic reactions for advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) in ambient air-equilibrated conditions. This system, based on a self-doped blue TiO2 (BT) nanotube photoanode, a carbon paper cathode and an infinitesimal Fe redox mediator (50μM), achieves outstanding aqueous pollutant degradation efficiencies. The complex reaction mechanisms were disentangled by quantitative ·OH measurements in single- and divided-cell with comparison to an electrochemical system with boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode. The ·OH generation by BT was exclusively ascribed to trapped holes oxidizing water, while the oxygen reduction to H2O2 on carbon cathode (utilizing O2 generated by BT) was comparable ·OH source via Fenton reaction in an ambient condition. The hole-driven Fe2+ oxidation on BT elevated the photocurrent and H2O2 generation on the carbon paper, while elongated the service life of photoanode. In parallel, the residual solar photons after absorption by the BT could effectively induce facile photolysis of Fe(OH)2+ to regenerate Fe2+ to continue the Fenton reaction. Accordingly, the PEC BT-Fe-Carbon system without external chemicals except for a minute Fe (50μM) exhibited a rapid aqueous pollutants degradation efficiency, irrespective of the initial Fe valency. This system demonstrates efficient pollutant mineralization in both synthetic and real wastewater matrices without a gas purging, along with sustained durability enabled by Fe redox cycling. These advancements broaden the practical applicability of PEC AOPs with homogeneous redox mediators for diverse (waste)water remediation applications.

title: Interception Efficiency and Driving Mechanisms of Bioretention Facilities for Microplastics in Urban Road Rainwater Runoff
description: Publication date: Available online 16 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Wang Xiaojuan, Zhou Jianqiang, Song Xichen, Li Hao, Yan Yaping, Liu Xiuyun, Yue Cheng, Zhang Tingting, Gao Suxia, Ma Fengfeng, Yao Guirong, Liu Jianlin, Li Wei, Wei Bigui
abstract: Bioretention facilities are important measures for urban stormwater management and runoff pollution control. To elucidate the interception efficiency and driving mechanisms of bioretention facilities for microplastics (MPs) in urban road rainwater runoff. In this study, the on-site bioretention facilities were taken as the research object. By collecting rainwater runoff and substrate soil samples, the response of the facilities to rainwater runoff MPs was analyzed, the key driving factors affecting the interception efficiency were identified, and its mechanism was clarified. The removal rate of MPs (20-500 μm) by bioretention facilities was 46.51%-73.56%. Among them, the substrate soil interception rate was 20.33%-43.89%, and the non-substrate pathway interception rate was 2.62%-45.55%. pH, Urease, Sucrase, Verrucomicrobiota, Myxococcota, and Basidiomycota are potentially important internal factors affecting the retention of MPs in facilities. Maximum rainfall intensity, rainwater runoff microplastic input, particle size (20-100 μm) and polymer type (PE, PU, ACR) are potential important external factors. In the future, the research on the migration and removal of MPs under continuous rainfall and long-term operation conditions should be strengthened to provide a scientific basis for the continuous control and optimal operation of microplastic pollution in bioretention facilities.

title: Ambient air pollution exposure before and during pregnancy and risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a large cohort study in Sichuan, China
description: Publication date: Available online 16 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Ning Ma, Wangnan Cao, Jie Yin, Furong Wang, Chunrong Li, Shengzhi Sun
abstract: Evidence linking ambient air pollution to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains inconsistent, particularly regarding exposure timing and pollutant mixtures. We examined associations between six pollutants (O3, SO2, NO2, CO, PM2.5, and PM10) and HDP in a multi-center retrospective cohort of 1,330,109 singleton pregnancies in Sichuan, China (2013–2022). Residential exposures from 13 weeks before pregnancy through gestational week 20 were estimated using geocoded addresses and gridded pollution data. Multivariable logistic regression and quantile g-computation assessed predefined exposure windows; distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNMs) assessed weekly associations. For O₃, each interquartile range increase was associated with higher HDP risk during the 13-week pre-pregnancy period (OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.29–1.42) and gestational weeks 1–4 (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.26–1.34). The air pollution mixture was associated with increased HDP risk during the pre-pregnancy period (OR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.46–1.60) and gestational weeks 1–4 (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.21–1.30). DLNM analyses indicated that exposure during some pre-pregnancy weeks was associated with increased HDP risk for all six pollutants, with associations during early gestation also observed for O₃, SO₂, and PM₂.₅. Overall, pre-pregnancy and early-gestation air pollution exposure was associated with higher HDP risk, with associations varying by pollutant and exposure window.

title: Deepening insights into the interaction between acidic water and pyrite enriched waste rocks
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Da–Mao Xu, Hai–Bin Wang, Rong–Guang Xie, Bai–Hong An, Kai–Kai Zhang, Xue–Qiang Zhu, Lai Zhou, Yu–Xiang Shi, Hai–Hui Xin
abstract: The exposure of pyrite enriched waste rocks (PWR) to acidic water can result in acid mine drainage (AMD) generation. Therefore, this study revealed acidic water − PWR interaction mechanism, combining with ion concentration variation and multidisciplinary characterization. The results demonstrated that Fe(III) (1638.5 mg/L), Fetotal (2485.8 mg/L) and SO4 2- (5649.2 mg/L) concentrations were found to be greatest in static (ST), oscillation (OT) and freeze-thaw (FT) treatment, respectively. The surface roughness of pyrite decreased in OT treatment, while that increased in OT and FT treatment. Compared with original pyrite, the characteristic peaks of SO4 2- and Fe(III)-sulfate disappeared and the peak intensity of S-O stretching vibration decreased in ST, OT and FT treatments. FeOOH were found in ST treatment, while FeOOH and Fe3O4 were present in FT treatment. These results indicated that Fe oxide passivation layers formed from the static interaction between acidic water and PWR. Surface oxidation products shed from the dynamic interaction between acidic water and PWR. Crucially, the oxidation transformation of Fe(II) to Fe(III) were restricted under periodical temperature difference effects, ultimately resulting in crystalline Fe3O4 formation. This work would provide the scientific reference for the safe disposal and risk management of PWR in mining areas.

title: Molecular-level decoding of gallium geochemical cycling: From coal sequestration to soil humic acid effects via fluorescent carbon dot tracking
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Shuyu Liu, Yilei Chen, Ruiying Du, Jiali Xia, DingJiang Chen
abstract: This study investigates gallium (Ga) migration from coal during leaching and combustion and its subsequent interaction with soil humic acid (HA), using a previously developed N-CDs fluorescence assay together with thermodynamic modelling, adsorption experiments, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS). Dynamic leaching produced the strongest Ga response under strongly acidic conditions (pH ≈ 2), whereas pH 4 and 7 produced consistently much lower responses that were used only for relative trend comparison. Coal particle size affected the leaching pattern more clearly than density, with greater time-dependent variation among particle-size fractions. Standard-state thermodynamic calculations indicate that chlorination can favor volatile GaCl₃ formation, whereas nonvolatile oxide/sulfide forms remain associated with ash. In soil, HA altered apparent Ga retention non-monotonically, with the later-time order HA-20 > CK > HA-40, reflecting a concentration-dependent balance between interfacial Ga retention and Ga–HA complexation. UV-Vis/2D-COS analysis indicates that phenolic- and conjugated-carboxyl-associated spectral regions respond sequentially to Ga³ ⁺ and that this sequence changes with pH and ionic strength. Together, these results provide an integrated view of Ga migration along the coal-combustion-soil pathway and identify HA-controlled complexation and interfacial retention as coupled processes governing Ga distribution in soil.

title: Who is maintaining community stability in drilling fluid-grade sulfonated asphalt contaminated sediments: Linking structural and functional keystone taxa dynamics to life-history strategy trade-offs
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Jichen Qiu, Jiaguo Yan, Liangxing Cao, Xuehui Zhang, Junhong Bai, Yujia Zhai, Yongkang Zhao, Yue Liu, Yaqi Wang, Guangliang Zhang
abstract: Sulfonated asphalt (SA) can persist in drilling wastes and pose potential environmental risks, yet microbial compositional and functional responses to it remain unclear. In this study, we explored microbial adaptive mechanisms in SA-contaminated sediments from the perspective of structural keystone taxa (SK) and functional keystone taxa (FK). Results showed that changes in the community composition of both SK and FK were significantly associated with inorganic nitrogen following SA exposure, with FK exhibiting a higher response threshold along the inorganic nitrogen gradient. SK relative abundance was negatively associated with network stability at the late stage, while FK relative abundance was positively associated with network stability and life-history traits. Microbial Y- and A-related functional potential showed a significant trade-off at the early stage, while both Y-A and Y-S trade-offs were observed at the late stage. FK relative abundance was more closely associated with variations in Y-, A-, and S-related functional potential than SK relative abundance. Analysis of metagenome-assembled genomes further identified a prominent Y-related component in the functional profiles of Bacillota. Together, these findings provide new insights into microbial adaption to SA exposure from the perspective of SK and FK, highlighting the strong association between FK dynamics and life-history strategies under SA contamination.

title: Disruption of BnPHT5;1a reduces arsenic accumulation through Pi-dependent restriction of arsenate uptake in Brassica napus
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Bei Han, Aosheng Jiang, Junjun Yan, Tao Wu, Bingbing Zhang, Yajie Wang, Xinyu Yang, Sheliang Wang, Zhuqing Zhao, Lei Shi
abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination threatens crop production and food safety, yet the role of vacuolar Pi transporters in arsenate [As(V)] acquisition remains unclear in polyploid crops. Here, we investigated BnPHT5;1a, a vacuolar Pi influx transporter in Brassica napus. Double mutants of the two B. napus homeologs BnA09PHT5;1a and BnC09PHT5;1a (BnPHT5;1a DM), generated by simultaneous CRISPR/Cas9 editing, exhibited enhanced As(V) tolerance. Under 400 μM As(V), mutant shoot and root fresh weights were 11.0–30.1% higher and root As concentrations were approximately 28% lower than those of wild-type W10. Heterologous overexpression increased As(V) sensitivity in Arabidopsis. Yeast growth assays provided no clear evidence of direct As(V) transport by BnPHT5;1a. Its disruption reduced the expression of several plasma membrane PHT1 genes and limited As(V) uptake under Pi-sufficient conditions, with these effects diminishing as external Pi availability decreased. Mutant plants displayed an attenuated transcriptional response to As(V), consistent with a lower As burden. These findings support an As(V)-avoidance mechanism in BnPHT5;1a DM and suggest possible functional differences between BnPHT5;1a and BnPHT5;1b, whose disruption was previously associated with increased As accumulation and shoot cell wall retention. This study highlights the role of vacuolar Pi partitioning in As(V) acquisition and provides a potential genetic target for breeding low-As rapeseed.

title: Mechanism insights into synergistic inactivation of pathogenic Aspergillus niger via UV-LED-activated electrochemical chlorination
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Qiqi Wan, Yan Meng, Shaolan Du, Ruihua Cao, Gehui Wu, Jingyi Wang, Tinglin Huang, Gang Wen
abstract: This study proposed a novel ultraviolet light-emitting diode/electrochemical chlorine (UV-LED/EC–Cl2) disinfection strategy for decentralized water supply with ruthenium dioxide–iridium dioxide (RuO2–IrO2), iridium dioxide (IrO2), and boron-doped diamond (BDD) anodes, and comparatively evaluated inactivation performance against typical pathogenic fungal spores, Aspergillus niger (A. niger). The UV-LED265 nm/RuO2–IrO2-Cl2 (UV265 nm/RuO2–IrO2–Cl2) system achieved the highest inactivation efficacy, attaining 5.25-log reduction within 13 min under static conditions, and exhibited the strongest photoreactivation suppression. This performance was attributed to the superior chlorine evolution activity of the RuO2–IrO2 anode and the synergistic activation of in situ generated chlorine by UV265 nm irradiation, with [ Cl • ]ss of 1.17 × 10−14 M compared with 7.36 × 10−15 M in the UV265 nm/BDD–Cl2 system. The UV265 nm/RuO2–IrO2–Cl2 system induced severe membrane damage, rapid intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and ATP depletion. It also maintained effective inactivation in real water matrices under both static and flow-through conditions, with energy consumption for 2.0-log reduction of 1.68 kWh/m3 and 2.34 kWh/m3, respectively, lower than that of the UV265 nm/BDD–Cl2 and UV265 nm/IrO2–Cl2 systems. These findings provided a theoretical basis for developing low-chemical, efficient, and energy-saving decentralized water disinfection technologies.

title: Elucidating the neurotoxic mechanism of phthalates: Targeting PKM2 conformational changes to initiate metabolic reprogramming based on machine learning and metabolomics
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Ying-Xin Zhao, Ke-Tian Zhu, Yu-Xuan Tong, Mu-Zi Li, Yi-Zhao, Jin-Long Li
abstract: Phthalates (PAEs), widely employed as plasticizers, have garnered significant attention due to their multiple entry pathways into the environment, posing substantial threats to human health. Although previous studies have implicated PAEs in neurocognitive disorders, it remains unknown whether PAEs affect brain function through altering cellular metabolism and specific molecular programs. Here, we systematically investigated the mechanisms underlying PAEs-induced neurotoxicity by integrating network toxicology, machine learning, metabolomics, in vitro and in vivo validation. 13 overlapping candidates were identified via intersecting 305 PAEs (DEHP and MEHP)-associated targets with 470 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) related to cognitive impairment. Machine learning prioritized five core genes, including GABRG2, HSPA1A, CDK5, JUN, and MITF. Enrichment analysis indicated that neuroactive ligand signaling and metabolic pathways represented key impact pathways underlying PAEs-induced cognitive impairment. In vivo, PAEs (DEHP) exposure resulted in cognitive impairment. Metabolomics and in vitro knockout experiments suggested that PKM2 contributed to metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction under PAEs (DEHP and MEHP) exposure. Molecular docking and co-IP assays confirmed that CDK5 and GABRG2 (downregulated in both disease and mouse models) bind PKM2 with good affinity. Live cell imaging demonstrated that PKM2 impaired axonal growth by regulating CDK5 and GABRG2 under PAEs (MEHP) exposure. The monomers and dimers of PKM2 increase, while the expression of tetramers decreases under PAEs (DEHP and MEHP) exposure. PKM2 knockdown restored the expression levels of CDK5 and GABRG2, and prevent axonal shortening. This study broadens the mechanistic understanding of PAEs-induced neurotoxicity and supports the identification of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic intervention targets for cognitive impairment disorders.

title: Species-specific adaptations to cadmium or zinc stress in the pseudometallophytes Arabidopsis halleri and Arabidopsis arenosa
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Michał Szopiński, Krzysztof Sitko, Cédric Delporte, Audrey Le Cabec, Massimiliano Corso, Eugeniusz Małkowski, Nathalie Verbruggen
abstract: Trace metal elements (TMEs), such as Zn and Fe, are essential for plant growth and development but can become toxic at high concentrations. In contrast, Cd is a non-essential element that is toxic to plants even at low concentrations. Arabidopsis halleri is a pseudometallophyte plant species that has long been used to study the regulation of TMEs homeostasis and adaptation to metalliferous sites. Its close relative, Arabidopsis arenosa, also occurs on metalliferous soils but has been much less studied in this context, providing an interesting comparative model to investigate species-specific adaptation strategies. We compared metallicolous (M) and non-metallicolous (NM) populations of both species under Cd or Zn exposure, combining physiological, molecular, and metabolomic analyses. Higher Cd and Zn accumulation was observed in shoots of A. halleri compared with A. arenosa. Both species showed contrasting and constitutive accumulation of many specialised metabolites, including glucosinolates and flavonoids. Expression of HMA2, HMA3, NRAMP3, and FRD3 in roots, as well as ZIF1, F3H, and LDOX in shoots, was higher under Cd treatment in A. arenosa than in A. halleri. Notably, we identified the triplication of HMA4 in the M A. arenosa population, a key factor in the Cd and Zn hyperaccumulation of A. halleri, whereas this triplication was absent in the NM population. Unlike in A. halleri, genes implicated in metal tolerance and accumulation were induced by metal treatments in A. arenosa. These results suggest that adaptation to metal excess may be older in A. halleri, where responses appear constitutive rather than inducible.

title: Soil-specific coupling of cadmium immobilization and carbon stabilization by bio-based composites in acidic and alkaline soils
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Xiaojia Zhou, Haonan Lv, Tao Sun, Shihang Wu, Huijuan Yu, Yuebing Sun
abstract: Contrasting geochemical conditions in acidic and alkaline cadmium (Cd)-contaminated soils create a need for soil-specific remediation composites. Here, different molecular weights biomass humic acid-sulfhydryl-grafted palygorskite (BSGP) composites are added to acidic and alkaline soils for 120-day incubation. We integrate soil properties, carbon components, microbial traits and communities, and dissolved organic matter (DOM) to identify optimal formulations and response mechanisms. Optimal formulations are 0.05% BSGP 100 kDa for alkaline soil, which reduced DTPA-extractable Cd by 70.0% and 80.1%, respectively. BSGP also increases microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE), decreases metabolic quotient of the microbial community (qCO2), and enhances carbon stabilization by increasing carboxyl/amide carbon of soil organic carbon (SOC) pool. They facilitate DOM humification, oxygenation and dealkylation reactions, driving DOM transformation into thermodynamically stable and less bioavailable fractions. BSGP alters specific carbon fixation and oxidation pathways, with increased abundance of related microorganisms and their contributions to functional genes. Overall, Cd regulation is primarily DOM-driven with microbial support in acidic soil, but shifts to microbial dominance with indirect DOM involvement in alkaline soil. These findings provide mechanistic insights for Cd-contaminated farmland remediation and bio-based composite design.

title: Dissolved organic matter influences mercury accumulation and photochemical transformations in eutrophic shallow lakes: Insights from mercury isotopes
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Chan Li, Xiang Liang, Honglin Li, Yue Su, Juncheng Li, Ju Zhang, Chengjing Li, Zexiang Wei, Jing Wang, Wenwu Zhong, Liyuan Zhang, Guangle Qiu, Liqiang Chen
abstract: The accumulation of methylmercury (MeHg) in plankton is a significant pathway for mercury (Hg) into aquatic food webs. Dissolved organic matter (DOM) can regulate MeHg bioavailability and Hg photochemistry, but its role in eutrophic shallow lakes remains unclear. We investigated DOM optical and fluorescence properties, Hg concentrations, and Hg isotopic compositions in samples from three eutrophic shallow lakes in Yunnan Province, southwestern China. MeHg concentrations and bioconcentration factor (BCF) were generally higher in zooplankton than phytoplankton, whereas THg accumulation varied among lakes. The Δ199Hg–Δ201Hg slope of plankton reflected a mixed photochemical imprint involving Hg2+ photoreduction and MeHg photodemethylation before biological uptake. MeHg concentrations in phytoplankton and zooplankton showed consistent negative correlations with dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations across the three lakes. DOM composition was also associated with Hg odd-mass-independent fractionation (odd-MIF). Microbial humic-like and tyrosine-like components were positively correlated with Δ199Hg, whereas terrestrial humic-like and tryptophan-like components were negatively correlated with Δ199Hg. These findings suggest that elevated DOC concentrations were associated with lower planktonic MeHg accumulation, while DOM components may be associated with differences in Hg photochemistry. This study improves our understanding of Hg cycling in eutrophic shallow lakes and supports Hg risk assessment under the Minamata Convention.

title: Polymer density and thermal mobility as predictors of plastic degradation rates
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Kevin P. Hickey, Sarah J. Ziemann, Boya Xiong, Margaret M. MacDonell
abstract: Understanding what drives the persistence of plastics in the environment is essential for risk assessment and materials design, yet the extreme disparity and scarcity of degradation data has hindered mechanistic insight. Environmental persistence amplifies the impacts of plastic pollution through fragmentation, transport, and accumulation effects in ecosystems worldwide. To identify the factors governing surface mass loss, we compiled a dataset of specific surface degradation rates (SSDRs, μm/yr) from literature spanning mechanical, photo-oxidative, and biological mechanisms across air and water media and multiple polymer types, covering seven orders of magnitude. We assess every model under study-grouped cross-validation, in which no study contributes to both training and test sets, to account for cluster effects. Under this assessment a seven-parameter linear model using polymer density, the difference between system and glass transition temperature (Tdiff), and mechanism-medium intercepts predicts with a root mean squared error of 1.09 log10 units against a no-knowledge baseline of 1.94, and outperforms random forest, support vector and Gaussian process regression. Intrinsic polymer properties therefore support order-of-magnitude screening of plastic persistence, and the limiting factor is the comparability of the published literature rather than the choice of model.

title: Efficient and stable hydrogen production from waste plastics via oxygen vacancy enhanced plasma catalysis
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Haijun Wu, Xianggang Zhang, Dianhang Wei, Fuzheng Fu, Shenggui Ma, Quanwei Lv, Xinrui Wang, Xia Jiang
abstract: Plasma-catalytic reforming of plastic pyrolysis oil for hydrogen production has significant advantages but designing an efficient and stable catalytic system remains a challenge. This study proposes a strategy that uses oxygen vacancies (Ov) to facilitate the transport of reactive oxygen species generated in the plasma gas phase, thereby enhancing hydrogen production and anti-coking. In a simplified reaction system, the effects of different oxygen-containing components on hydrogen production from reforming mixed olefins and alkanes were investigated. The designed Ov-rich catalytic system exhibited satisfactory performance (100% conversion, ∼75% hydrogen yield) reforming plastic pyrolysis oil model compounds, operating stably for 1600 min without significant deactivation. Furthermore, experiments with plastic-derived pyrolysis oils confirmed efficient hydrogen production, demonstrating the applicability of this catalytic system to different feedstocks. Comparisons across multiple reaction modes and kinetic experiments identified C2H4 as a major intermediate. Combined in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and optical emission spectroscopy (OES) revealed the cascade pathway from plasma gas-phase dissociation to catalytic surface reforming, elucidating the role of Ov in the coupled process. This study reveals the microscopic mechanism of synergy between plasma chemistry and catalytic surface reactions, providing guidance and a theoretical basis for designing high-performance catalysts.

title: Ultrashort-chain PFAS in a large drinking water reservoir: Occurrence, dynamics, potential sources, and risk prioritization
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Danni Wu, Hao Wu, Xiang Zhou, Can Huang, Liping Yang, Xiuping He, Junhui Chen, Lei Dong, Letian Zhang, Lei Chen
abstract: Although per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have attracted global attention, much less is known about ultrashort-chain PFAS (USC-PFAS). Here, we investigated six USC-PFAS and 26 other PFAS in surface water from the Danjiangkou Reservoir, the largest man-made freshwater lake in Asia and a critical drinking-water source in China, together with effluents from surrounding wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). Twenty-one PFAS were detected in surface water, including five USC-PFAS, with trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) being the most abundant (median 209.54 ng/L). PFAS profiles in effluents were similar to those in surface water and were dominated by USC-PFAS, indicating WWTPs as major point sources. The total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay revealed substantial precursor loading during the flood season, followed by potential transformation within the reservoir, which may have driven marked increases in several USC- and short-chain PFAS during the recession and dry seasons. The annual PFAS outflow load exceeded the inflow load by approximately 89%, further supporting potential in-situ PFAS generation. Finally, TFA and perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) were identified as high‑priority compounds owing to their high exposure potential. This study presents the first report on USC‑PFAS occurrence and precursor transformation within the Danjiangkou Reservoir, revealing the role of large reservoirs in PFAS dynamics.

title: Coupling conductive media with low-voltage electrochemical stimulation in anaerobic fluidized bed membrane bioreactors for diclofenac removal and bioenergy recovery
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Zulqarnain Aqeel Bazmi, Soojin Park, Jeonghwan Kim
abstract: Diclofenac (DCF), a widely used non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, is a persistent pharmaceutical contaminant of emerging environmental concern. To overcome this limitation, an electro-assisted anaerobic fluidized bed membrane bioreactor (E-AFMBR) was developed, incorporating magnetite-coated granular activated carbon (MGAC) as a conductive fluidized biocarrier to combine adsorption, electrochemical transformation, and anaerobic biodegradation in single treatment system. Batch experiments were first conducted to isolate the individual contributions of removal mechanisms. The MGAC only achieved 90% DCF removal via adsorption, compared to the 75% for unmodified GAC. Langmuir isotherm analysis confirmed higher adsorption capacity and affinity for DCF. Biomass itself removed only 43% of DCF under anaerobic environment, whereas electrochemical treatment itself achieved 96%, identifying electrochemical transformation as the predominant removal pathway. Combining biomass, MGAC, and an applied electric field together in anaerobic batch reactor raised removal significantly to 99%. During 150 days of continuous E-AFMBR operation, the DCF removal declined progressively without external voltage due to the adsorption-site saturation, whereas applying 1.0 V sustained more than 98% of removal efficiency. The E-AFMBR system fed with DCF produced biogas containing 67.4% methane, with a methane yield of 0.328 L CH₄ g⁻¹ SCOD removed and energy balance of + 432%.

title: Damming-altered dissolved organic matter (DOM) molecular reactivity influences nitrogen metabolism potential in super-deep reservoirs
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Nan-ping Wu, Yufei Bao, Yuchun Wang, Ji Lu, Jiyuan Lu, Hao Chen, Shanze Li, Jie Wen, Qian Zhang
abstract: Damming fundamentally alters dissolved organic matter (DOM) transformation and microbial nitrogen cycling in river–reservoir systems, yet how changes in DOM molecular reactivity regulate nitrogen transformation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated two deep cascade reservoirs, Xiaowan (XW) and Nuozhadu (NZD), along the Lancang–Mekong River by integrating seasonal hydrochemistry, FT-ICR MS, PMD-based reactomics, metagenomics, and machine-learning approaches. Compared with riverine DOM, release-water DOM reactivity increased by 1.73% ± 0.62% in XW and 12.43% ± 2.01% in NZD, accompanied by enhanced nitrogen metabolic potential. Assimilatory nitrate reduction genes (norC, norB, and nirK) increased by ≥ 1.1-fold in XW and ≥ 2-fold in NZD, while Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) genes (nirB, nrfA, and nrfH) increased by ≥ 1.2-fold and ≥ 3-fold, respectively. Hypolimnetic waters exhibited higher DOM reactivity and intensified nitrogen metabolism, with persistent enrichment of nitrification and nitrogen-fixation genes. A random forest model trained on a global DOM dataset (n = 1104) explained 86.6% of DOM-reactivity variation, identifying lignin/CRAM-like compounds as key molecular predictors. These findings reveal that dam-induced shifts in DOM molecular reactivity reshape microbial nitrogen transformation pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding nitrogen retention, removal, and downstream water-quality risks in regulated river networks.

title: Numerical simulation of radionuclide dispersion in coastal waters considering atmospheric deposition following a hypothetical nuclear accident: The case of Daya Bay nuclear power plant, China
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Luqiang Li, Huiming Bao, Yankai Pan, Yang Su, Xiaobo Zeng, Songjing Li, Jiyun Zhao
abstract: Since the Fukushima accident, numerous simulations have investigated radionuclide dispersion in coastal waters following hypothetical accidents at operating nuclear power plants, providing essential information for risk assessment and emergency management. However, most studies have focused on liquid leakage, while the contribution of atmospheric deposition has received limited attention, particularly in complex coastal environments where its influence may be more pronounced. This study quantitatively investigated radionuclide dispersion in seawater under the combined effects of atmospheric deposition and liquid leakage in a hypothetical accident at the Daya Bay Nuclear Power Plant. A coupled atmospheric-hydrodynamic dispersion model was developed and validated against Fukushima measurements and reference water levels and currents. The simulations demonstrate that radionuclides released into the atmosphere rapidly disperse and deposit, with the deposition patterns governed by seasonal prevailing winds. Under certain meteorological conditions, radionuclides can bypass terrestrial barriers and reach semi-enclosed coastal waters, substantially expanding the contaminated area. At the monitoring point near the DBNPP, the relative increase in concentrations caused by atmospheric deposition is small (below 4.41%), whereas in downwind areas where marine transport is hindered, atmospheric deposition can lead to a substantial increase, resulting in committed effective doses from seafood ingestion exceeding 1 mSv within 60 days.

title: Synergistic MOFs/POMs boost activity, photostability, and residue-degradability of biogenic insecticides for high-efficiency and residue-free pest control
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Xiao Qing Zhou, Huafeng Li, Rui Tang, Yunxuan Wu, Guodong Zhao, Nannan Lv, Jianting Fan
abstract: Biogenic insecticides pose lower environmental risks but are limited by poor control efficiency and insufficient stability. We present a hybrid nanosystem (NU-1000/MN/Ru4) in which the biogenic insecticide matrine (MN) and Ru4-bridged polyoxometalates (Ru4) are electrostatically assembled and co-encapsulated within the hierarchical pores of the MOFs (metal-organic frameworks) NU-1000. NU-1000/MN/Ru4 exhibits excellent insecticidal activity against a broad spectrum of pests. The porous architecture of NU-1000 allows efficient loading and controlled release of MN, contributing to the sustained control efficacy. The antibacterial activity of Ru4 enables it to serve as a synergist for MN, disrupting pest gut bacteria and suppressing detoxification metabolism. Moreover, NU-1000/MN/Ru4 is better suited for field application because NU-1000 enhances penetration, foliar adhesion, and photoprotection, thereby improving targeting, deposition, and photostability of MN. Beyond efficient pest control, NU-1000/MN/Ru4 leaves no residue, as Ru4 catalyzes the degradation of MN immediately after its insecticidal action. Importantly, both NU-1000 and Ru4 show short-term biosafety, highlighting their eco-friendly potential. These findings demonstrate that polyoxometalates with antibacterial and catalytic capacity act as both synergists and photocatalysts, while porous MOFs function as delivery nanocarriers and protective scaffolds. This combination dramatically enhances the activity, photostability, and catalytic residue-degradability of biogenic insecticides, enabling high-efficiency, residue-free pest control.

title: Study on the spray and combustion characteristic of diesel/hexanol fuel doped with MIL-53 (Al) based on optical diagnosis and Optuna-CNN-LSTM prediction model
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Wei Guan, Jinbo Li, Changcheng Fu, Sheng Cao, Guoming Xie, Zhenhua Ji, Hao Chen, Yubao Xie, Kaifeng Zhong, Mingzhang Pan
abstract: Higher alcohols such as n-hexanol offer potential for reducing soot emissions from diesel combustion; however, their low-temperature oxidation characteristics may restrict combustion development and soot oxidation. In this study, MIL-53(Al) was introduced into a diesel/n-hexanol blend, and its effects on the coupled evolution of fuel spray, combustion, and soot formation were systematically investigated using constant-volume combustion optical diagnostics. Experimental results demonstrated that the addition of MIL-53(Al) at 20 ppm and 40 ppm significantly improved combustion characteristics. The catalyst's nanoporous structure might adsorb fuel molecules, potentially leading to micro-explosions at high temperatures that could optimize fuel atomization. Concurrently, MIL-53(Al) provided catalytic active sites, promoting combustion chain reactions and accelerated the oxidation of soot precursors. This dual mechanism enhanced combustion efficiency and elevated temperatures, leading to more complete and cleaner combustion. As a result, the KL factor, a line-of-sight optical indicator of soot loading, was reduced by 31.64% and 38.86% relative to pure diesel with 20 ppm and 40 ppm MIL-53(Al), respectively. Furthermore, an Optuna-CNN-LSTM prediction model has been developed to accurately invert and estimate KL factors. This model exhibited high predictive accuracy, achieving an R² value of 0.9927, thereby demonstrating the predictive consistency of the model with the experimental trends. This research thus provides a novel strategy for enhancing the low-temperature combustion performance of alcohol-containing fuels. Moreover, it delineates a promising technical pathway for reducing combustion soot output based on optical diagnostic measurements and supporting the development of high-efficiency and low-emission combustion technologies.

title: Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 facilitates pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 to degrade petroleum hydrocarbon through coordinated carbon metabolism and respiratory electron transfer
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Zhihao Wang, Jiaqi Kang, Linxuan Han, Ruixiang Li, Siyu Dong, Lean Zhou, Tian Li, Changwei Lü, Xin Wang
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon biodegradation often slows after an initially rapid phase as degrader activity declines and electron-acceptor availability becomes limiting. Overcoming these kinetic and thermodynamic constraints is therefore critical for effective remediation of petroleum-contaminated soils. Here, we identified a metabiotic interaction between Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 and Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 that enhanced n-hexadecane degradation. Although the relative abundance of MR-1 declined rapidly during co-cultivation, the co-culture achieved an apparent degradation efficiency of 100% within 9 d, compared with approximately 82% for PAO1 alone, without greater overall biomass accumulation. Experiments with non-viable MR-1 and riboflavin showed that MR-1-derived cellular and redox-active components contributed to this facilitation. Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed lower levels of hexadecanoic acid and acetyl-CoA, accompanied by coordinated responses in β-oxidation, TCA-cycle metabolism, cofactor supply, and respiratory electron transfer in PAO1. In nonsterile red soil, PAO1–MR-1 inoculation increased n-hexadecane degradation by approximately 47%. Together, these findings indicate that MR-1 acts as a redox-active facilitator rather than an independent hydrocarbon degrader, enhancing PAO1-mediated degradation through coordinated carbon metabolism and respiratory reprogramming. This study highlights metabiosis as a strategy for overcoming degradation bottlenecks and improving petroleum-contaminated soil remediation.

title: Observation-constrained assimilation of O 3 , NO 2 , and speciated VOCs reveals the chemical and transport drivers of summertime ozone pollution in the Fenwei Plain
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Xin Liao, Hongxi Yao, Dianhewen Liu, Danni Xu, Zibing Yuan, Bo Wang, Huipeng Zhang, Kaihui Zhao
abstract: Uncertainties in chemical initial conditions remain a major challenge for regional ozone (O3) prediction and hinder reliable assessments of O3 formation mechanisms and mitigation strategies. Here, we develop a multi-species observation-constrained assimilation framework that simultaneously integrates O3, NO2, and speciated volatile organic compound (VOC) observations to reconstruct a chemically consistent atmospheric state and investigate summertime O3 pollution over the Fenwei Plain (FWP). Aromatic and alkene assimilation reduced the absolute O3 mean bias and RMSE in Xi’an by 68.69% and 67.20%, respectively, relative to the baseline simulation. Beyond statistical improvements, process diagnostics suggest that assimilation modifies O3 production by enhancing radical propagation and reshaping NOx-VOC interactions. Aromatics and alkenes are identified as the dominant VOC groups controlling O3 sensitivity, with their assimilation strengthening RO2 + NO and HO2 + NO pathways, accelerating NO2 photolysis, and reducing O3 loss through NO titration. Integrated Process Rate analysis further demonstrates that assimilation improves O3 simulations by enhancing regional redistribution through horizontal advection and vertical diffusion while reducing excessive chemical production. Expanding the assimilation domain decreases the bias associated with short range intercity transport and increases local and adjacent source contributions by more than 9%, highlighting the importance of regional coordination in O3 mitigation. Overall, this study demonstrates that multi-species chemical data assimilation provides a powerful approach for resolving O3 formation sensitivity and regional transport pathways, offering scientific insights for targeted precursor control and coordinated air quality management.

title: Electron-transfer-mediated synergistic transformation of pollutants by carbon-based materials
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Wenjing Sun, Honghong Lyu, Jingjing Li, Yutong Li, Jingchun Tang, Yao Huang
abstract: Carbon-based materials (CBMs) have emerged as promising redox-active mediators for the remediation of complex co-contaminated environments due to their tunable electrochemical properties and structural versatility. Unlike conventional strategies targeting single pollutants, CBMs can facilitate the synergistic transformation of heavy metals and organic contaminants through coupled biotic and abiotic electron-transfer pathways, offering opportunities to enhance pollutant removal and reduce environmental risks. This review systematically summarizes the relationships between key electrochemical parameters (e.g., electrical conductivity, specific capacitance, electron-donating/accepting capacity, and charge-transfer resistance) and critical structural features of CBMs, including redox-active functional groups, graphitization, defects and heteroatom doping. The roles of CBMs in regulating radical/non-radical pathways and mediating electron transfer in systems containing dyes, chlorinated hydrocarbons, antibiotics, nitroaromatic compounds, and mixed heavy metals are critically discussed. Particular attention is given to the synergistic interactions among CBMs, dissolved organic matter, and iron minerals in constructing environmental electron-transfer networks. Furthermore, environmental factors and sustainability aspects, including life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic considerations, are evaluated to bridge laboratory performance with practical applications. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for scalable, low-carbon, and high-efficiency remediation technologies are proposed. This review provides a comprehensive framework linking CBM structure, electrochemical behavior, and synergistic transformation mechanisms for complex environmental pollution.

title: Longevity and impact of PFAS contamination from legacy landfills on groundwater
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Nika Bilić, Poul L. Bjerg, Biao Jin, Bolette B. Jensen, Klaus Mosthaf
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) leaching from landfills pose a risk to groundwater. This study developed a conceptual understanding of long-term PFAS leaching from legacy landfills by reviewing PFAS occurrence data and simulating leaching from two landfill types: dry landfills underlain by an unsaturated zone, and wet landfills without one. PFAS leaching was investigated using coupled 1D landfill leaching and 2D subsurface models. Scenario modelling evaluated the impact of sorption and infiltration on PFAS release over time. PFAS release and leaching longevity were controlled by retention processes within the landfill and underlying unsaturated zone, landfill type, landfill history, and hydrological conditions. Simulated dry landfills exhibited substantial retention of long-chain PFAS due to air-water interfacial sorption, leading to prolonged leaching over decades or centuries. Simulated contaminant mass discharge showed delayed peaks for long-chain PFAS, indicating the importance of long-term monitoring and management of legacy landfills. PFAS observations from Danish landfills suggest that long-chain PFAS reach groundwater earlier than predicted by the models, potentially due to heterogeneities and preferential flow paths not represented in the model. This study provides novel insights into PFAS leaching behaviour and offers a conceptual framework for risk assessment, while highlighting the critical role of the unsaturated zone.

title: Dual-mode chemosensor based on oxidative cyclization of 2-hydrazinobenzothiazole functionalized perylene diimide for rapid recognition of HClO in environmental samples and living organisms
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Ruida Shi, Jiamin Chen, Lu Wang, Yiwei Chen, Yujing Zuo, Linfeng Cui, Zhenguang Wang, Haitao Yu, Yanyu Qi
abstract: Based on the oxidative cyclization conjugation extension of 2-hydrazinobenzothiazole, we designed and synthesized a highly efficient fluorescent-colorimetric dual-mode chemosensor (PDI-BTZ) for the detection and bioimaging of hypochlorous acid/hypochlorite (HClO/ClO⁻). Experimental results demonstrate that it possesses excellent analytical performance with the following characteristics: 1) dual-response detection mode via UV-vis absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy; 2) a low detection limit of 26.2 nM; 3) excellent selectivity against 16 common interfering substances; 4) a rapid response time of 7 s; 5) applicability to visual detection via smartphone-based RGB (Red, Green, Blue) colorimetric analysis and testing of actual environmental water samples. Meanwhile, the probe was successfully utilized for fluorescence imaging in cells and zebrafish, allowing real-time monitoring of HClO/ClO⁻ fluctuations in living systems. This novel ratiometric fluorescent probe provides a new avenue for elucidating the pathophysiological mechanisms associated with hypochlorite.

title: Efficient remediation of As(V) and Pb(II) co-contaminated soil by ball-milled sulfide-modified zero-valent iron and schwertmannite composites: Immobilization effects and synergistic mechanisms
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Dejin Zhang, Jiahao Ni, Song Li, Lei Du, Mingjiang Zhang, Xuan Liu, Murong Wang, Jianru Liang, Lixiang Zhou
abstract: Simultaneous remediation of As and Pb in co-contaminated soils remains challenging due to their distinct geochemical behaviors. Here, a ball-milled schwertmannite/sulfur-modified zero-valent iron composite (Sch@S-ZVI) was developed for the simultaneous stabilization of As(V) and Pb(II). At the optimal Sch/S-ZVI mass ratio of 0.1:1, removal efficiencies exceeded the corresponding mass-weighted additive expectations by 25% for As(V) and 33% for Pb(II), respectively. Under optimized conditions (7 d, 0.5 wt% amendment dosage, 50% field capacity, and 2.00 mm soil particle size), Sch@S-ZVI outperformed pristine Sch and S-ZVI. Sequential extraction revealed that Sch@S-ZVI transformed labile As into Fe/Al oxide-associated fractions, whereas Pb fractionation showed no significant differences among treatments. Adsorption experiments indicated that chemisorption predominated, with Freundlich and Langmuir models providing best descriptions of As(V) and Pb(II) adsorption, respectively. As(V) immobilization mainly involved ligand exchange, Fe–O–As inner-sphere complexation, and coprecipitation with iron oxyhydroxides, whereas Pb(II) immobilization was primarily through Fe–O–Pb complexation and coprecipitation with iron corrosion products. Sequential ordinary Portland cement (OPC) solidification suppressed cement-induced As remobilization and reduced metal bioavailability. Ryegrass cultivation further demonstrated reduced phytotoxicity, with plant growth comparable to that in clean paddy soil. Combining Sch@S-ZVI stabilization with OPC solidification shows promise for remediating As/Pb co-contaminated soils.

title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in infant personal care products and preliminary dermal exposure assessment
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Mengxin Sun, Ziwei Wang, Qi Wang, Xiarui Fan, Zhiguo Cao, Zhaomin Dong
abstract: Personal care products are potential sources of human exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), but their occurrence in infant personal care products (IPCPs) remain poorly understood. This study systematically analyzed 37 target PFAS in 88 IPCPs and compared them with 35 adult products. All sampled IPCPs contained at least one target PFAS above the LOD, with Σ37 PFAS concentrations of 1.2–266 ng/g. Sunscreens had the highest median concentration (99 ng/g), and sanitary products the lowest (3.8 ng/g). Perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) were the dominant PFAS group across the five IPCPs categories, contributing 51.6–87.0% of total PFAS concentrations, whereas PFSAs contributed the least (0.59–18.5%). Σ7 PFSAs and Σ19 emerging PFAS differed significantly between sampled infant and adult products. Dermal exposure estimates indicated a maximum daily exposure dose of 378 pg/kg bw/day for a single product category. Category-specific cumulative HQs for seven PFAS ranged from 0.0002 to 0.18, and HQtotal for all five IPCP categories ranged from 0.34 to 0.52. Although IPCPs accounted for 6.7% of combined exposure from breast milk and IPCPs, their contribution to combined PFHpA exposure reached 23.3%, suggesting that IPCPs use may be a non-negligible dermal exposure pathway for some PFAS in infants.

title: Insight into dopant-dependent SO 2 poisoning behavior of Cu-, Co- and Ce-modified Fe 2 O 3 /SiO 2 catalysts in CO–SCR of NO x
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Yuqing Pan, Chenyang Wu, Ni Tang, Qulan Zhou, Cheng Gong, Ke Li, Na Li, Liang Xu
abstract: The selective catalytic reduction of NO x by CO (CO-SCR) over Fe2O3-based catalysts is a promising low-cost strategy for the simultaneous removal of CO and NO x , but SO2-induced deactivation remains a critical challenge hindering practical application. Although various metal promoters have been introduced to improve catalytic performance, their roles in regulating SO2 poisoning behavior during CO-SCR remain unclear. Herein, Cu-, Co-, and Ce-modified Fe2O3/SiO2 catalysts were investigated to elucidate dopant-dependent SO2 poisoning mechanisms. Activity evaluations reveal that Co-Fe2O3/SiO2 undergoes severe, irreversible low-temperature deactivation, while Cu-Fe2O3/SiO2 shows moderate, partially reversible inhibition. In contrast, Ce-Fe2O3/SiO2 exhibits superior SO2 tolerance (<10% NO x conversion loss across 25–500°C) with strong long-term stability and reversibility. Characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that dopants govern SO2 tolerance by regulating sulfate adsorption, redox properties, and surface acidity. Whereas Co drives severe sulfate accumulation via strong orbital hybridization and Cu suffers sulfation but slightly enhances its Lewis acidity, Ce mitigates deactivation through the Ce3 +/Ce4+ electron-buffering effect to preserve redox properties, coupled with weak sulfate stabilization and the generation of SO2-induced Lewis and Brønsted acid sites to sustain essential intermediates. Our findings offer guidance for improving SO2 tolerance of Fe2O3-based CO-SCR catalysts and reducing the hazardous impacts of NO x .

title: Combined heteroatom substitution and π-conjugation expansion for high-efficiency bifunctional fluorescent detection of phosgene and sarin simulant
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Wenjing Liu, Wenjia Tan, Chenxi Zhao, Yan Li, Feng Li, Ming Zhang
abstract: The practical application of bifunctional fluorescent probes for phosgene and Sarin is of great importance for public security, but is significantly hindered by their single response mode and slow response. To address these issues, this study proposes the combined heteroatom substitution and π-conjugation expansion strategy, which diversifies response modes and achieves efficient multi-target detection. By this approach, we designed and synthesized PIM3PCz, a probe that successfully modulates the optical output and switches the response mode from “turn-on” to “ratiometric”, which presents significant emission shifts of Δλem = 58 nm for phosgene and Δλem = 100 nm for diethyl chlorophosphate (DCP, the mimic of Sarin). Notably, PIM3PCz demonstrates high sensitivity (LODs: 8.26 nM-liquid/0.41 ppm-vapor for phosgene; 0.52 μM-liquid/57.49 ppb-vapor for DCP), rapid detection (5 s) for phosgene, a shortened response time (from 22 min to 5 min) and good selectivity (11 interferents for DCP). Theoretical calculations reveal that, keeping the donor fixed, the proposed strategy significantly reduces the electrostatic potential (ESP) and average localized ionization energy (ALIE) of recognition sites, thereby enhancing sensing performance. Furthermore, the developed portable detection platform enables quantitative vapor detection of both analytes and exhibits outstanding performance in realistic scenario simulations and long-term monitoring.

title: Exposure pathways modulate antidepressant effects on leaf litter decomposition through microbial-detritivore interactions
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Su Yan, Yang Xuan, Zhou Xun, Zhao Jianguo, Wu Naicheng, Jin Baodan, Du Jingjing
abstract: Antidepressants can disrupt freshwater ecosystem processes, yet how different exposure pathways influence these effects remains unclear. This study used the freshwater snail Cipangopaludina cathayensis as a representative detritivore to examine the effects of fluoxetine and amitriptyline on leaf litter decomposition under waterborne, detritus, and combined exposure pathways in freshwater microcosms. Antidepressant exposure significantly affected microbial biomass, extracellular enzyme activities, litter quality, detritivore physiology, feeding behavior, and decomposition processes. Microbial biomass increased by 35.18%-99.41% during early exposure but declined by 4.23%-65.34% at later stages under waterborne exposure. Enzymes involved in carbon and nutrient acquisition showed distinct responses among exposure pathways, indicating shifts in microbial resource-acquisition strategies. For detritivore, antidepressant exposure induced pathway-dependent oxidative stress responses and suppressed feeding activity of C. cathayensis. Detritus fluoxetine and amitriptyline exposure reduced detritivore-mediated decomposition by 20.34% and 25.83%, respectively, whereas microbially mediated decomposition increased by 145.74% and 68.19%. Despite this increase in microbially mediated decomposition, total decomposition rate declined significantly under detritus exposure. These findings show that exposure pathways strongly modulate antidepressants effects on detritus processing and emphasize the need to incorporate detritus and combined exposure scenarios in ecological risk assessments of freshwater ecosystems.

title: Chronic polystyrene nanoplastics exposure reprograms gene expression, alternative splicing, and disrupts host-microbiome-metabolic networks to promote atherosclerosis in LDLr⁻/⁻ mice
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Ajmal Khan, Delicia Esther Cardenas Vasquez, Yaru Si, Warren S. Vidar, Kerui Wu, Norman Chiu, Zhenquan Jia
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics have been detected in human blood and carotid atheromas, yet their mechanistic contribution to atherogenesis is poorly defined, and chronic exposure studies of nanoplastics are limited. This multi-omics study investigates chronic (12-week) oral exposure to 80 nm polystyrene nanoplastics in LDLr⁻/⁻ mice, integrating aortic plaque quantification, hepatic transcriptomics with alternative splicing profiling, gut microbiome 16S sequencing, and liver untargeted metabolomics into a unified host-microbiome-metabolite network. Nanoplastics increased aortic lipid deposition, suppressed hepatic detoxification and anti-atherogenic lipid pathways at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels including alternative splicing events. Exposure induced gut dysbiosis, reduced SCFA-producing commensals and enriched pro-atherogenic pathobionts, shifts co-occurring directionally with hepatic transcriptional modules. Hepatic genes (down-regulated Fbp1, Ccn1 and Cyp2c29; upregulated Chka) and gut genera (depleted Bacteroides; enriched Faecalibaculum and Streptococcus) were confirmed by RT-qPCR and genus-specific qPCR. Untargeted metabolomics showed elevated aromatic and branched-chain amino acids such as tryptophan and methionine, and depletion of glutathione precursor γ-glutamylcysteine and the antioxidant taurine, implicating oxidative stress and amino-acid dysregulation. Concordance with human MASLD (GSE135251) and atherosclerotic plaque (GSE100927) transcriptomes and gut signatures matching human atherosclerotic microbiome profiles suggest plausibility for human relevance. This research implicates nanoplastics as a cardiovascular risk factor involving splicing reprogramming and gut-liver crosstalk.

title: Visible-light inactivation of Microcystis sp. and mitigation of chlorination by-product formation potential by an S-scheme AgBr/Tp-Tta heterojunction
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Jing Luo, Chenyu Yang, Kai-qin Xu, Jialin Lin, Antong Shi, Gongduan Fan
abstract: The treatment of algal blooms requires consideration of both cell inactivation and downstream disinfection byproduct (DBP) formation. Here, an AgBr/Tp-Tta composite was prepared by in situ precipitation for visible-light inactivation of Microcystis aeruginosa. The optimized composite, with an AgBr mass ratio of 20:1, achieved 91.79% chlorophyll a removal within 180 min at a catalyst dosage of 100 mg L-1. Chlorophyll a removal remained at 96.82% in the third treatment cycle, demonstrating activity retention upon reuse. Humic and fulvic acids inhibited photocatalytic performance. Interfacial coupling enhanced light absorption and charge separation, while spectroscopic and electrochemical evidence supported an S-scheme charge transfer pathway. Superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes were the principal reactive species. Physiological analyses revealed an initial antioxidant response followed by membrane permeabilization, protein depletion, and photosystem II dysfunction, accompanied by changes in intracellular and extracellular organic matter. Photocatalytic pretreatment reduced the combined formation potential of nine quantified DBPs by 44.07% following chlorination with 50 mg L-1 NaClO for 3 d. These findings highlight the potential of AgBr/Tp-Tta for algal inactivation and reduction of subsequent chlorination DBP formation potential.

title: Mercury contamination in skin-lightening cosmetic products across market pathways: Implications for consumer exposure and risk-based surveillance
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Koichi Haraguchi, Mitsugu Saito, Yumi Ushikai, Kanako Nagatomi, Hirofumi Ikeshouji, Chacriya Malasuk, Kyaw Nyunt Maung, Satoshi Awata
abstract: Despite regulatory restrictions, mercury-containing skin-lightening cosmetic products remain a potential source of human exposure. We investigated mercury concentrations in 44 products, focusing on domestic physical retail, domestic online platforms, and cross-border e-commerce accessible to consumers in Japan. Mercury was screened by X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and quantified by thermal decomposition amalgamation atomic absorption spectrometry (TDA-AAS). None of the 21 products obtained through the selected Japanese domestic pathways exceeded the 1 mg/kg regulatory benchmark, whereas 8 of 13 cross-border e-commerce products did. Concentrations showed marked separation between predominantly low-level products and a few highly contaminated products. Six products contained 6220–24,200 mg/kg mercury and exceeded a hazard quotient (HQ) of 1 across all nine combinations of three principal daily-use scenarios and three dermal absorption fractions. HQ = 1 concentrations ranged from 22.7 to 3500 mg/kg depending on product use and dermal absorption assumptions. The XRF limit of quantification (16.25 mg/kg) was below the lowest principal HQ = 1 concentration, supporting screening under these assumptions. Confirmatory analysis remains necessary near the 1 mg/kg benchmark. These findings support a tiered strategy combining rapid XRF screening, confirmatory TDA-AAS analysis, and targeted, risk-oriented surveillance of cross-border market pathways.

title: Heavy metals in liquid anaerobic digestate: Occurrence, speciation, environmental risks and sustainable removal strategies
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Tina Kegl, Matjaž Valant
abstract: The rapid expansion of anaerobic digestion in renewable energy and waste management has increased liquid anaerobic digestate production, raising concerns for environmental protection, agricultural sustainability, and circular economy implementation. Although widely used as a fertilizer due to its high nutrient content, digestate may contain heavy metals that threaten soil quality, crop safety, ecosystems, and food security. These risks are intensified by its complex composition, where organic matter, ammonia, sulfides, colloids, and redox-active species control metal speciation, mobility, and bioavailability, often limiting conventional regulations and treatment technologies. This review addresses recent advances and remaining challenges in heavy metal removal from liquid anaerobic digestate through: 1) analysis of heavy metal occurrence and transformation from feedstocks through anaerobic digestion to liquid anaerobic digestate; 2) assessment of environmental risks and regulatory constraints for agricultural use; 3) conceptualization of liquid anaerobic digestate as a distinct chemical system, where heavy metal speciation controls their distribution among operationally defined sequential extraction fractions; 4) evaluation of heavy metal removal methods, reassessed through liquid anaerobic digestate-specific lens, linking metal speciation to the selection of removal strategies; and 5) outlook on research needs aligned with sustainable development goals. This integrated approach provides a conceptual framework for sustainable heavy metal management.

title: Electrocatalytic ozonation for removal of pharmaceuticals, pathogenic microorganisms, and antibiotic resistance genes from hospital wastewater
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Lingyun Gu, Chunxiu Yu, Yi Wu, Xingxing An, Kexin Chen, Jialiang Huang, Xuejie Wang, Zhaokun Xiong, Bo Lai
abstract: The widespread use of antibiotics, particularly in hospital wastewater, accelerates the proliferation of antibiotic-resistant genes (ARGs), posing a global threat. To address this challenge, an efficient electrocatalytic ozonation (ECO) process was constructed by injecting diffused ozone bubbles, using stainless steel and graphite as the anode and cathode. The ECO system exhibited superior catalytic performance in degrading dexamethasone (DXMS) with pseudo-first-order reaction rate constants (k obs, 0.401 min–1), which is 4 and 93 times higher than those of ozonation and electrolysis alone, respectively. Hydroxyl radicals(•OH) were identified as the primary reactive species. The ECO process effectively reduced bacterial culturability of Escherichia coli (E. coli) in 5 min by disrupting cell integrity and DNA structure. In real hospital wastewater treatment, the ECO system maintained a COD removal efficiency of 72.25% – 86.82% and eliminated 81 of the 119 detected pharmaceutical contaminants, achieving an average removal rate of 85.42%. The removal efficiencies for various ARGs ranged from −7.73–99.13%. The ECO process effectively caused substantial DNA degradation and altered the relative abundance of ARGs and microbial taxa in hospital wastewater. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the ECO system holds significant potential for the simultaneous removal of pharmaceuticals, pathogens, and ARGs from hospital wastewater.

title: Upcycling of iron-rich waste by MoS 2 interfacial engineering for enhanced Fenton-like reaction: Proton-coupled electron transfer mediated co-catalysis and surface oxidative complex formation
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Yiting Ma, Nan Chen, Min Zhang, Leixin Wu, Ying Li, Jing Guo, Cheng Chen
abstract: To achieve the utilization of iron-rich heating pad waste (HPW) in Fenton-like reaction and the regeneration of Fe(II) sites, HPW was upcycled by loading MoS2 to form HPW-MoS2 heterojunction via interfacial engineering for enhancing peroxymonosulfate (PMS) based Fenton-like reaction. The HPW-MoS2 exhibited performance in activating PMS for tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) removal, demonstrating degradation efficiency covering a broad initial pH range 3–11. The presence of interfering substances had negligible effects on TCH degradation, and the HPW-MoS2/PMS system also showed environmental adaptability in natural water bodies. The emergence of HPW-MoS2/PMS* with a oxidation potential contributed to the TCH elimination through electron transfer pathway (ETP). Experimental validation and density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated that the HPW-MoS2 heterojunction functioned as a mediator of the proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanism by constructing an acidic interface microenvironment via capturing proton, and mediated the generation of hydrogen radicals (H•) for Fe(II) regeneration, thereby exhibiting co-catalysis and driving the HPW-MoS2/PMS* generation. By integrating T.E.S.T. predictions, phytotoxicity tests, and life cycle assessment (LCA), this study demonstrated reduced toxicity of TCH degradation products and lower environmental burdens, highlighting HPW-MoS2 as an efficient and environmentally friendly catalyst.

title: Linking molecular transformations of dissolved organic matter to micropollutant attenuation across coupled full-scale wastewater and surface water treatment plants
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Chang Liu, Hang He, Bairun Song, Yunpeng Zhao, Hao Zhou, Lanfeng Li, Jing Ai, Peng Yang, Dongsheng Wang
abstract: Wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluents introduce micropollutants (MPs) and dissolved organic matter (DOM) into receiving waters supplying downstream surface water treatment plants (SWTPs), yet the molecular relationship between DOM transformation and MP attenuation across linked full-scale WWTP–SWTP systems remains unclear. DOM transformations and MP attenuation across a hydrologically connected WWTP–SWTP system were characterized using FT-ICR-MS and targeted UPLC–MS/MS. Biological treatment reduced dissolved organic carbon (DOC) by 65.4%, while anaerobic–anoxic–oxic (A²/O) treatment lowered total MP concentrations by 94.2% relative to aerated grit chamber (AGC) effluent. A²/O preferentially depleted reduced, relatively saturated DOM, enriching oxygenated CHO and CHNO formulas. Subsequent advanced treatment induced comparatively minor changes. In the SWTP, coagulation–flocculation–sedimentation (CFS) removed high-molecular-weight, oxygen-rich DOM but only 11.8% of MPs; ultrafiltration–reverse osmosis (UF–RO) increased overall MP removal to 96.5%. Spearman analysis linked MPs positively with reduced sulfur-containing DOM and negatively with oxygenated CHO and CHNO fractions. MP-positive formulas clustered at O/C < 0.5, with their largest depletion occurring during A2/O. These findings identify reduced, low-O/C DOM as an MP-associated molecular signature and highlight biological treatment as a key barrier to persistent MP discharge.

title: Thermally driven aerosol dynamics and ultrafine particle emissions during electric stove heating
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Museong Lee, Su-Gwang Jeong, Lance Wallace, Donghyun Rim
abstract: Understanding how thermal conditions and surface configurations govern ultrafine particle (UFP) dynamics during cooking is important for predicting indoor exposure to cooking-related aerosols. Although gas-stove emissions have been widely studied, the coupled effects of heating conditions, cookware materials, and particle loss processes in electric heating systems remain poorly characterized. This study investigated time- and size-resolved UFP dynamics across six electric-stove surface configurations at hot-plate controller settings of 250 °C and 540 °C, followed by heat-off decay. Particle evolution was characterized using Mode 1, representing concentration growth during heating, and Mode 2, representing subsequent decay. Under the no-pan condition, total UFP concentrations reached 2.53 × 10⁶ cm⁻³ at 250 °C and 5.08 × 10⁶ cm⁻³ at 540 °C, approximately doubling at the higher setting. Repeated heating generally reduced peak emissions, with reductions of up to 91% depending on configuration and cycle. At 540 °C, the hot plate and ceramic-coated pan exhibited source strengths of 5.47 × 1012 and 4.89 × 1012 particles min⁻¹ , respectively, for their initial emission episodes. Heating-associated particle contributions were concentrated primarily in the smaller size range, while cookware moderated the overall burden and shifted the size distribution in a material-dependent manner. Coagulation contributed more than 60% of early particle losses under selected conditions, whereas deposition and ventilation became increasingly important during subsequent decay. Experimental–numerical comparisons further showed that measured concentrations and size distributions were broader and higher than model predictions, revealing the influence of heterogeneous thermal and airflow conditions not captured by simplified well-mixed modeling. Together, these results demonstrate that UFP dynamics during electric heating cannot be described by temperature alone; they emerge from the coupled effects of surface-specific particle generation, evolving particle concentrations, and competing loss processes. This mechanistic framework provides a basis for improving predictive aerosol models and developing exposure-control strategies for thermally active indoor environments.

title: Legacy and emerging PFAS in full-scale leachate treatment systems at municipal solid waste disposal facilities
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Yuzhi Luo, Junda Ren, Bernard Crimmins, Jinxia Liu, Rui Li, Hui Lu
abstract: PFAS in leachate from municipal solid waste facilities have become an increasing environmental concern, yet knowledge gaps persist regarding the profiles and fate of PFAS throughout leachate treatment systems. In this study, leachates from full-scale treatment systems at incineration and landfill facilities were analyzed for 58 targeted PFAS, augmented by total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay and non-targeted analysis. Distinct PFAS profiles were observed in the two types of raw leachates and throughout the treatment processes. Additionally, some emerging PFAS, such as 8-chloroperfluorooctylphosphonic acid, remained persistent across treatment systems. The pretreatment and biological treatment exhibited lower PFAS removal efficiency compared to membrane treatment (e.g., RO unit). Seven newly identified PFAS were detected in the RO upstream and/or effluent. The TOP assay indicated the formation of ultrashort-chain perfluoroalkyl sulfonic acids and perfluoroalkyl phosphinic acids, revealing the presence of precursors capable of transforming into previously overlooked stable PFAS upon oxidation. Targeted PFAS mass loads in the effluent from the landfill were 4.17-fold higher than those in the incineration facilities, and were comparable to those in the sludge. This study provided new insights on the fate and transformations of numerous emerging and unknown PFAS during treatment at two types of MSW facilities.

title: Biocrusts promote soil multifunctionality recovery in gold mine tailings through heavy metal bioavailability regulation and microbial community reorganization
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 519 Author(s): Jin Fan, Chongfeng Bu, Wenxin Zhang, Chun Wang, Xinhao Li, Jiajia Luo, Shuo Liang, Jingwen Pang, Yuhan Yan, Fatong Song, Chen Yang
